body.authentication: reads need none; 150 operations require X-API-Key (a relayer key), 73 take it optionally, 9 need the operator token (in full or for one variant) — see tools[].auth
body.note: Import the OpenAPI document into an HTTP Request node, or copy a single tool below. Nothing here signs a transaction; the writes are listed with who may make them.

n8n_library.reading: thousands of agent workflows, almost no on-chain evidence in any of them

tools.name: root
tools.summary: The latest sealed superroot.
tools.returns: Root hash, seal time, leaf and peak counts.

tools.name: clock
tools.summary: The coordination clock: how far behind the tip every chain is and how many seconds a cross-venue transition takes from its block to visible in the pipe and coord (_COORD_CLOCK_v1_).
tools.returns: { schema taifoon.coord.clock.snapshot.v1, at, headline { transition hops p50/p95/max seconds, worst chains }, chains[] { chain, blocks_behind, seconds_behind, header_age, tree_gap, tip sources and disagreement, block_time, fast source, slo, state }, transitions[] (recent samples, each hop in seconds), writes[] (anchor age per chain, writers' last run, pending) }; refreshed every 30 s.

tools.name: clock__chain
tools.summary: One chain's clock: blocks and seconds behind the tip, header age, tree gap, both tip sources, its fast source and whether we use it.
tools.returns: { chain, blocks_behind, seconds_behind, header_age, tree_gap, tips[], block_time, fast, slo, state, transitions[] on this chain, anchor }; 404 for a chain the probe does not read.

tools.name: root_latest
tools.summary: The anchor feed: epoch, root, when it was anchored.
tools.returns: The latest root with its anchor age, and the recompute cadence named separately so the two are never confused.

tools.name: root_chains
tools.summary: What each chain contributed to the root.
tools.returns: Per-chain block and twig counts.

tools.name: root_submissions
tools.summary: How often each chain and protocol lands in the root.
tools.returns: Per chain: leaves in the last 1 m / 1 h / 24 h, last-leaf age, twigs; per protocol: transitions and sequence tip; the superroot’s own recompute count and age.

tools.name: root_proof__chain__block
tools.summary: Proof that one block is inside the root.
tools.returns: The sibling path from that block to the root. A block the root does not hold answers 200 with proof: null, proven: false and rpc_fallback { block } (its header read over warmbed) when the chain’s RPC has it, else 404 (chain_not_in_root, block_not_in_root, block_beyond_head).

tools.name: proof_tx_solana__sig
tools.summary: The layer’s attested record of a Solana signature: the pipe’s ack leaf, its batch root and the superroot once pushed — not a block proof.
tools.returns: { ok, chain: solana, signature, kind: attested-record, is_block_proof: false, words, envelope, leaf, slot, batch_root, superroot | null, path }. 404 not_recorded when the layer never saw the signature settle a sale of its own; 503 pipe_not_installed while the coord pipe is not installed.

tools.name: proof_tx__chain__tx
tools.summary: Proof that one transaction is inside the root.
tools.returns: The block it landed in, the superroot that commits to that block, is_finalized, and `checks` naming what was verified — including that the proof’s block hash equals the one in the transaction’s own receipt. proven: true only then. When no proof can be given (PROVABLE_GAP, not yet built, producer unavailable, chain not read) the answer carries proof: null, proven: false and rpc_fallback { source warmbed | static, endpoint_host, read_at, receipt { status, block, block_hash, from, to, logs_count, confirmations, final } }: the chain’s own receipt, never a proof (_RPC_FALLBACK_v1_).

tools.name: protocol__protocol_order__key
tools.summary: One order of any protocol leaf the producer holds — a LayerZero message by guid, an Across deposit, a Mayan order, an ERC-8183 job — its stages across chains, each with its transaction and its leaf under the superroot.
tools.returns: { protocol, key, latest, final, stages, counts, src_chain, dst_chain, expect[] (what the register expects next and the reason if late), transitions[], anchor, verify }; 404 for an order the leaf has not seen.

tools.name: protocol__protocol_stuck
tools.summary: The orders of one protocol past their expected next stage, each with one named reason from the protocol stage register: a LayerZero message verified but not committed or committed but not executed, an Across deposit not filled, an ERC-8183 job submitted but not evaluated.
tools.returns: { protocol, generated_at, tracked, lag, reasons[], counts, stuck[]: { key, reason, stage, age_s, expected, src_chain, dst_chain, stages } }, oldest first; 404 for a protocol not watched (with why).

tools.name: protocol__protocol_paths
tools.summary: Measured stage-to-stage times of one protocol per source and destination chain: seconds from the start stage to each later stage, p50, p90 and n.
tools.returns: { protocol, window, start, stages, paths[]: { src_chain, dst_chain, to: { <stage>: { p50_s, p90_s, n } } } }.

tools.name: protocol__protocol_quote
tools.summary: How long an order of this protocol takes from one chain to another, measured from delivered orders (fees where the protocol exposes them; a transfer’s price across bridges is /v1/compare).
tools.returns: { protocol, src_chain, dst_chain, time: { delivered_stage, p50_s, p90_s, n }, fees, fees_note }; 404 for a path with no delivered order in the window.

tools.name: projects
tools.summary: Every project workspace: a project (a bridge, a solver, a messaging protocol) whose orders the layer rebuilds as the generic order steps — its protocol’s stages on the one job lifecycle — with a board per project.
tools.returns: { generated_at, projects[]: { project, name, state: live | lane_pending | no_lane, protocols, filters, key: { scopes, outlets }, webhook: { set }, counts, board } }. ?deliver=1 (the layer’s own keys only) returns the registered rows with their webhook endpoints.

auth.rule: Keyless for the boards. ?deliver=1 (the webhook endpoints) answers our admin keys in full and the protocol watcher’s own key for projects whose owner key holds the webhooks permission (_WEBHOOK_PERMISSION_v1_).

tools.name: projects
tools.summary: Register a project once: its protocol leaves, the filters that pick its orders (chains, addresses, order key prefixes), an optional webhook that receives each new step, and the write outlets its key may reach (default none: read and stream only). A protocol the producer does not read yet is registered with its lane spec and state lane_pending.
tools.returns: 201 { ok, project, next: { key (the read/stream key call), board, orders, stream, webhook } }; 400 bad_param naming the field; 409 taken.

auth.rule: Any valid key, a free key included.

tools.name: projects_lanes
tools.summary: Every member’s own stream service as a user lane: a project that named its contract, its events and which event moves an order to which stage (stream: taifoon.stream.spec.v1) is served here compiled — a manifest the producer’s lane compiler runs without a rebuild, and the stage register the boards, stuck reasons and path times use.
tools.returns: { schema: taifoon.stream.lanes.v1, generated_at, paused, lanes[]: { project, owner (hashed key ref), protocol (u_<project>), chain_id, manifest, register, measure, paused } }

tools.name: projects__id
tools.summary: One project’s board: its orders as steppers (each step its protocol stage, lifecycle state, chain, transaction, block, time, leaf and proof link), its stuck orders with named reasons, its path times, its key’s scopes and write outlets — or the lane it waits for.
tools.returns: { project, name, state, protocols, key: { scopes, outlets }, orders[]: { protocol, key, latest, lifecycle, final, failed, src_chain, dst_chain, steps[] }, stuck[], paths[], counts, lane }; 404 for an unknown id.

tools.name: projects__id
tools.summary: Change your project: its name, what it is, its filters (chains, addresses, order-key prefixes), its webhook (deliver.endpoint, null clears) or pause it. The protocols and the lane stay as registered.
tools.returns: Send { name?, what?, filters?, deliver?, paused? }. { ok, role, project } (the public view); 403 role_denies { role, action, resource, reason }; 404 for an unknown id; 400 bad_param names the field.

auth.rule: The key that registered the project (or any key of its tenant; a delegate key needs manage). Any other key is 403 role_denies (not_owner); the operator may, audited.

tools.name: ops_search
tools.summary: Which operation answers a question: one search over every public /v1 operation’s name, summary and search keywords, and the protocol register (a protocol it names fills :protocol in the hits).
tools.returns: { q, protocols[], hits[]: { op, path, summary, score, protocol?, try, matched[] }, operations }.

tools.name: proof_verifiable__chain
tools.summary: The newest block of a chain that can be proven now.
tools.returns: Block number and hash. A chain not in the proof snapshot answers 200 with proof: null, proven: false and rpc_fallback { block } (the newest header read over warmbed) when its RPC answers, else 404 chain_not_in_snapshot.

tools.name: proof_onchain__chain__id
tools.summary: The on-demand proof batch for one source-chain transaction, ready for a gate on the target chain.
tools.returns: `attestation` (root, batchId, attestedAt, signature), `blob` (V5, superroot-only tail), `calldata`; 409 with `error` when the source, the target or the attestation is not ready.

tools.name: proof_blocks__chain
tools.summary: Proof that one or more blocks (?blocks=a,b,c, up to 256) are inside the root.
tools.returns: `blockTree` (multiproof: indices = block numbers, leaves = block hashes, shared nodes, empty-subtree flags), `full` (32 siblings) for a single block, and `anchor` (chain root, tip, chain leaf index and L3 siblings, superroot hash).

tools.name: protocols_proven
tools.summary: Every protocol whose transitions are inside the root, and how current each source is.
tools.returns: `protocols` (name, leaf id, transitions, orders, history root, state root) and `lanes` (chain, contract, events → state, next block, tip, blocks behind).

tools.name: proof_log__chain__tx
tools.summary: Proof that one event log (?log_index=, as eth_getLogs reports it) is inside the root, ready for an on-chain verifier.
tools.returns: `log`, `eventHash`, `anchor` (superroot, tip leaf path), `blockTree` (the block in the tip’s tree), `receipt` (header RLP, receipt RLP, trie nodes), `finality`, and `calldata` for verifyLogAt.

tools.name: proof_order__protocol__key
tools.summary: Proof of one order’s whole lifecycle (key like erc8183:8453:81401): every transition and its current state, inside the root.
tools.returns: `transitions` (each with its chain, block, transaction, log position and log hash), `history` (multiproof), `state` (path, present, currentState — absent orders prove absent), `anchor` (protocol leaf, its path to the superroot).

tools.name: proof_transition__protocol
tools.summary: Proof that given transitions (?seqs=0,1,2, up to 256) of a protocol are inside the root, in order.
tools.returns: `transitions`, `history` (multiproof, index = sequence number) and `anchor` (history and state roots, protocol leaf path to the superroot).

tools.name: chain__chain_block__id
tools.summary: One block, like eth_getBlockByNumber / ByHash, with its proof: {id} = latest (the newest block in the chain’s tree) | finalized (the tip the superroot leaf names) | a number | a block hash.
tools.returns: block { number, hash, parent_hash, timestamp, state_root, receipts_root, transactions_root, gas_used, gas_limit, base_fee_per_gas, logs_bloom, transaction_count, transactions[] with ?txs=1 }, source (indexed: from the header store, no RPC | fetched), header_source, final, proof (ExplorerProof), cost.

tools.name: chain__chain_tx__hash
tools.summary: One transaction, like eth_getTransactionByHash with its outcome, every event decoded, and the proof that its block is in the superroot.
tools.returns: tx { hash, status, block_number, block_hash, block_time, tx_index, from, to, to_label, value_wei, nonce, type, method, input, gas_limit, gas_used, effective_gas_price, fee_wei, contract_created, events[] }, source (indexed: kept, no RPC | fetched: read once and kept once final), final, head, proof (ExplorerProof; checks.block_hash_matches binds the receipt’s block hash; urls.logs prove each log), cost. 404 not_found | pending.

tools.name: chain__chain_tx__hash_receipt
tools.summary: One receipt, like eth_getTransactionReceipt: every log raw and decoded, each with its own inclusion proof link, and the block proof.
tools.returns: receipt { transaction_hash, status, block_number, block_hash, transaction_index, from, to, gas_used, cumulative_gas_used, effective_gas_price, contract_address, type, logs[] { log_index, address, topics, data, decoded, proof_url } }, source, final, proof (ExplorerProof), cost.

tools.name: chain__chain_logs
tools.summary: Event logs, like eth_getLogs, paged: the held headers’ blooms pick the blocks that may match and only those are read; a window over 10,000 blocks is a scan job (202).
tools.returns: logs[] { block_number, block_hash, transaction_hash, transaction_index, log_index, address, topics, data, decoded { event, family, args }, in_tree }, window { from, to }, scanned_to, next_cursor (the next from; null when the window is done), source, final, coverage { held_headers, unknown_blocks, bloom_via }, cost { rpc_requests, rpc_calls, headers_checked, candidates, blocks_read, saturation_pct }, proof (ExplorerProof over the page’s blocks). 202: job { id, progress, poll, stream }.

tools.name: chain__chain_address__addr_events
tools.summary: Account scan: every event the address emitted or is named in (as an indexed topic) over a block window, decoded, with proofs; the held headers’ blooms pick the blocks.
tools.returns: events[] (the logs shape), address, window, scanned_to, next_cursor, source, final, coverage { held_headers, unknown_blocks, bloom_via, sees }, cost, proof. Over 10,000 blocks: 202 with a scan job.

tools.name: chain__chain_address__addr_txs
tools.summary: Account scan: the transactions that produced an event naming the address, over a block window, with direction and proofs.
tools.returns: txs[] { hash, block_number, block_hash, transaction_index, from, to, to_label, value_wei, method, direction (out | in | other), events, in_tree }, address, window, scanned_to, next_cursor, source, final, coverage (sees: a native transfer with no log is not in a logs bloom), cost, proof. Over 10,000 blocks: 202 with a scan job.

tools.name: chain__chain_scans__id
tools.summary: A scan job (a logs or account window over 10,000 blocks): each read advances it one step and returns its progress and the rows so far.
tools.returns: job { id, kind, window, scanned_to, done, truncated, progress (%), rows, steps, error, cost, poll, stream }, the rows so far as logs[] | events[] | txs[], next_cursor, proof. 202 while running, 200 when done.

tools.name: chain__chain_scans__id_stream
tools.summary: A scan job as server-sent events: progress after each step, then done (or paused when the connection’s minute is up).
tools.returns: event: progress | done | paused | error, data: the job’s progress (scanned_to, progress %, rows, cost).

tools.name: transitions__protocol
tools.summary: A protocol’s state transitions from the protocol trees (no chain is read): one order’s lifecycle (?key=) or a page of the history by sequence, with both proof steps recomputed.
tools.returns: transitions[] { seq, order_key, from_state, to_state, chain_id, block_number, block_hash, transaction_hash, log_index, log_hash, kind, recorded_at, tx_url, log_proof_url }, current_state (with ?key=), history_count, next_seq, source indexed, proof { kind protocol_tree, verified, checks { history_in_root, protocol_in_superroot }, anchor, urls }. GET /v1/protocols/proven lists the protocols.

tools.name: protocols_decoders
tools.summary: The protocols the producer decodes, the chain tiers, and the manifest a new one sends.
tools.returns: `decoded` (id, source and fill topic, contract count, chains) read from the producer’s own table; `chains` (how many are proven per transaction, how many the superroot commits, and where the live list is); `does` (what registering changes today, per layer: proofs, attribution, decoding); `register` (the manifest shape); `pending` (manifests waiting for an operator).

tools.name: protocols_register
tools.summary: Register a protocol’s contracts and events for decoding; a v2 manifest adds the Lambda definition (key, states, transitions, actions, finality, author).
tools.returns: Send the manifest: id, name, type, contracts per chain, source_topic, fill_topic, events (name, canonical signature, topic0, role), identity; a v2 manifest adds version, key (chain-namespaced order id), states, transitions (trigger event among the events, bind paths resolved against the ABI, guards parsed in a small grammar, join, proof), actions (unsigned-call templates), abi, finality (a V5 type), author. Every check the manifest allows is made; 422 lists the problems. A manifest that passes is queued as submitted for an admin (201; `dry_run: true` keeps nothing; 409 version_conflict when the id exists with another hash and the version is not bumped) and the answer carries `hash` (keccak256 of the canonical JSON), `registry` (the unsigned submit() call, contract null until deployed), the three fragments the producer’s registries take, and `does`: what is proven, attributed and decoded for it today, and what is not.

auth.rule: Public by design (a manifest names only public contracts and public events): without a key 5 a minute and 30 a day per IP; a key spends its own budget.

tools.name: protocols_pending
tools.summary: The manifest approval queue: submitted, approved, rejected, deprecated.
tools.returns: view (admin | public), total, counts per status, manifests[] — { id, version, status } for anyone; the full row (manifest, hash, by, at, decided_by, decided_at, reason, fragments, chains) for an admin. ?status= narrows to one status.

auth.rule: Open: anyone reads ids, versions and statuses. The operator token or a relayer key the operator minted as ours reads every row in full (manifest, hash, who sent it, who decided and why). A key that is sent but not valid is 401.

tools.name: protocols__id_approve
tools.summary: Approve a submitted manifest.
tools.returns: The row with status approved, decided_by and decided_at, plus `registry`: the unsigned submit(id, version, manifestHash, uri) call for the author (contract null until deployed). 404 when no such manifest is queued, 409 already_decided when it was decided before.

auth.rule: Admin only: x-operator-token, or an X-API-Key the operator minted as ours (role ops). 401 without a credential, 403 ours_only for any other key.

tools.name: protocols__id_reject
tools.summary: Reject a submitted manifest with a reason.
tools.returns: Send { reason } (required; the author reads it). The row with status rejected, decided_by, decided_at and reason. 404 when no such manifest is queued, 409 already_decided when it was decided before.

auth.rule: Admin only: x-operator-token, or an X-API-Key the operator minted as ours (role ops). 401 without a credential, 403 ours_only for any other key.

tools.name: chains
tools.summary: Every chain the layer can move value between.
tools.returns: Chain ids, names and the assets each supports; rpc_url is the warmbed rotation’s current best endpoint for every chain the layer rotates (rpc_source warmbed | static), with rpc_rotation (GET /v1/rpc/{chain}) and rpc_gateway (/gw/rpc/{chain}) beside it; rpc_source catalogue for a chain the layer does not rotate.

tools.name: rpc
tools.summary: Every chain the RPC gateway serves (chain-agnostic JSON-RPC at /gw/rpc/{chainId}: the same methods on every chain), with the warmbed rotation’s current best endpoint and its health. Prices and limits: GET /v1/access.
tools.returns: chains[] { chain, name, source (warmbed | static), healthy, endpoints, logs_endpoints, best, best_logs, gateway, rotation }, healthy "n/m", gateway { path /gw/rpc/{chainId}, serves [eth_blockNumber, eth_call, eth_getLogs, eth_chainId, …], sends [eth_sendRawTransaction: your signed transaction relayed, limits in /v1/access rpc.sends], signing refused, budget }.

tools.name: rpc__chain
tools.summary: One chain’s RPC rotation as warmbed measured it: every endpoint, best first, with its health.
tools.returns: chain, name, source (warmbed | static), healthy, best, best_logs, call[] and logs[] (proven for 2,000-block eth_getLogs windows) { url, status, health_score, success_rate, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, logs_span_ok, archive, in_backoff, last_probe_at }, fallback[] (the measured static list), gateway (POST JSON-RPC here: /gw/rpc/{chain}; eth_blockNumber, eth_call, eth_getLogs, eth_chainId, …; eth_sendRawTransaction relays your signed transaction (limits in /v1/access rpc.sends); signing refused; each request a λ step; visitors 60 a minute, 2,000 a day; the routing fee: the first 100 requests a day without a key, 1,000 a day per key (both gateways together), are free, each further one 0.001 USDC from a key’s gateway credit or paid with x402, HTTP 402 otherwise), rotation, warmbed.

tools.name: gas
tools.summary: What gas costs now on every chain the layer prices: Base, Arbitrum, Arc, Robinhood Chain, Monad and Solana, from razor.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.razor.gas-all.v1 { chains { base, arbitrum, arc, robinhood, monad, solana } }, each the reading GET /v1/gas/{chain} returns; via razor. 503 razor_unavailable.

tools.name: gas__chain
tools.summary: One chain’s gas reading from razor: base fee, priority-fee percentiles, the L1 data fee, the native USD price and the p95 rise of the fee over a horizon.
tools.returns: {chain} = base | arbitrum | arc | robinhood | monad | solana or the EVM chain id; ?horizon_s=60..86400 (default 3,900). EVM: schema taifoon.razor.gas.v1 { chain, chain_id, block, at, age_s, stale, base_fee_wei, priority_fee_wei { p10, p25, p50, p75, p90 } (median of each over 1,024 blocks; Arbitrum-model chains ignore it), window_blocks, l1 { model op-stack (fee_upper_bound_wei_by_bytes, GasPriceOracle) | arbitrum (ArbGasInfo prices) | none }, gas_token (ETH | USDC on Arc), native { symbol, decimals, usd, usd8, usd_source (Chainlink ETH/USD or SOL/USD on Base; par for USDC), usd_updated_at }, rise { horizon_s, p95_bps, basis (razor samples | feeHistory window), covered_s }, model (the chain’s gas model in words) }. Solana: lamports_per_signature (getFeeForMessage), priority_fee_micro_lamports_per_cu { p10..p90 } over 150 slots, contended { accounts, priority_fee_micro_lamports_per_cu }. 404 chain_not_priced, 503 razor_unavailable.

tools.name: gas__chain_quote
tools.summary: What N transactions of one shape cost on a chain now, in wei (or lamports), the native token and USD.
tools.returns: EVM: ?shape=native_transfer | erc20_transfer | erc20_approve | swap | post_verdict | open_job, or ?gas=<units>&bytes=<signed size>; Solana: ?shape=sol_transfer | spl_transfer | sol_swap, or ?signatures=&cu=, &lane=global | contended. &txs=1 &pct=10|25|50|75|90 (default 75) &buffer_bps= (default: the chain’s p95 rise). schema taifoon.razor.quote.v1 { quote { gas_price_wei, l2_wei_per_tx, l1_wei_per_tx, total_wei, total_native, usd, buffer_bps, rule } (Solana: lamports_per_tx, total_lamports, cu_price_micro_lamports), reading { native, rise } }. 400 invalid_input, 404 chain_not_priced.

tools.name: protocols
tools.summary: Every bridge and protocol we can price.
tools.returns: Protocol names, the chains each covers, and its status.

tools.name: pipe_stream
tools.summary: The pipe’s subscription stream as Server-Sent Events: every envelope, ack, leaf and batch that matches your filters, replayed from a sequence number and then live.
tools.returns: text/event-stream of StreamEvent { seq, at, kind: envelope | leaf | ack | batch | lost | dropped, envelope?, address }. Filters: chains (CAIP or a bare EVM id), venues, agents, topics (the destination topic: bridge.icp-gate, market.signal, vault.<id>; bridge.* by prefix; protocol.<id> = every observation of one producer lane, e.g. protocol.erc8183, protocol.layerzero_v2, protocol.*), assets (terms.value.asset), kinds, states, order_keys, edges, addresses, carriers; from_seq replays; commitment = sent | delivered | acked | folded | pushed. Reconnect with from_seq = the last seq you saw.

auth.rule: Keyless: the public kinds only (observe, batch, advert, lost, dropped; the role table's public viewer), a short session — reconnect with from_seq. With any valid key (a free key included): your own envelopes too.

tools.name: pipe_send
tools.summary: Send one envelope (taifoon.pipe.envelope.v1) into the coord pipe: it is queued for its carrier and every state it passes becomes a leaf.
tools.returns: The pipe’s answer: { id, state: queued, carrier, batch }. Refused: a payload above 64 KiB (413), an envelope without schema/kind/from/to (400), a `to` no carrier takes (422 from the pipe). The id is keccak256 of the envelope’s content: the same content is the same envelope.

tools.name: pipe_inbox__who
tools.summary: A receiver’s inbox: the envelopes delivered to an agent (erc8004:<chain>:<id>) or a venue that it has not acked yet.
tools.returns: { who, envelopes[] } newest first; ?since= and ?limit= (max 200); ?wait= long-polls up to 25 s for the first envelope.

auth.rule: Any valid key (_SIGN_INBOX_DOOR_v1_: an envelope carries records and its digest, and an unsigned ack names a digest). The off-box signer’s inboxes (lang/gen/sign-inboxes.json) answer only the operator-minted relayer key whose label is their reader; any other key, a free key included, gets 403 inbox_private.

tools.name: pipe_ack
tools.summary: Ack a delivered envelope: an envelope of kind ack with reply_to and the receiver’s receipt over Ack(envelopeId, payloadDigest, at).
tools.returns: { id, state: acked }. 404 for an unknown envelope, 409 when it is not delivered (already acked, lost, dropped).

tools.name: pipe_keys
tools.summary: Publish the X25519 key senders seal envelopes to (sealed envelopes, a Team and Protocol plan feature): a statement signed by the receiver’s identity key.
tools.returns: { ok, who, at }. Refused (400, named): a signature that does not recover to `by`, a statement not newer than the stored one, a key not 32 bytes.

tools.name: pipe_keys__who
tools.summary: A receiver’s signed X25519 key statement, to seal an envelope to it.
tools.returns: { who, key: { scheme, by, x25519, at, sig, suite, info } }; 404 when that identity published none.

tools.name: pipe_status__id
tools.summary: One envelope’s state and every leaf it left, each with its batch root and, once pushed, the superroot and the path to it.
tools.returns: { id, state, carrier, attempts, history[], evidence[], handler, batch, leaves[] }; a receiver verifies its envelope under the superroot from the path.

tools.name: pipe_lost
tools.summary: Every envelope not delivered or not acked within its ttl: nothing is lost silently.
tools.returns: { envelopes[]: { id, kind, carrier, attempts, reason } }.

tools.name: pipe_dead
tools.summary: The dead-letter: every dropped envelope and the handler that ran (refund · redirect · dead-letter).
tools.returns: { envelopes[]: { id, handler, reason } }.

auth.rule: admin only (x-operator-token, or a key of ours): a dead letter names its endpoint and payload digest; anyone else gets 401/403 role_denies

tools.name: pipe_batches
tools.summary: The passes’ batch roots: one root over every leaf of the pass, attested once by the vault, pushed under the superroot by the sync loop.
tools.returns: { batches[]: { batch, root, leaves, attested, pushed, superroot } }; ?since= a batch number.

tools.name: pipe_twigster
tools.summary: Twigster: every outgoing envelope is signed by its actor’s session key, certified once per hour by the Taifoon vault key that attests (it lives in a secure sandbox and never leaves it); mode, live sessions, certificates, the issuer.
tools.returns: { mode, sessions, certs, pending, issuer, ttl_s, direct_max_per_s }.

tools.name: pipe_twigster_certs__ref
tools.summary: One Twigster session certificate by the cert_ref a signed envelope names, to verify its signature offline (issuer signature, validity, scope).
tools.returns: { schema, actor, session, scope, nbf, naf, issuer: { kind, id }, sig }.

tools.name: pipe_turbine
tools.summary: Deprecated alias of pipe/twigster (kept for one release). The signing turbine: every outgoing envelope is signed by its actor’s session key, certified once per hour by the Taifoon vault key that attests (it lives in a secure sandbox and never leaves it); mode, live sessions, certificates, the issuer.
tools.returns: { mode, sessions, certs, pending, issuer, ttl_s, direct_max_per_s }.

tools.name: pipe_turbine_certs__ref
tools.summary: Deprecated alias of pipe/twigster/certs/:ref (kept for one release). One session certificate by the cert_ref a signed envelope names, to verify its signature offline (issuer signature, validity, scope).
tools.returns: { schema, actor, session, scope, nbf, naf, issuer: { kind, id }, sig }.

tools.name: lambda_catalog
tools.summary: The lambda catalogue: for every canonical record type (job, agent, offer, verdict, settlement, order, …) the transformation into a sendable envelope and back — the envelope kind, the transition it names, who signs, the Rust (coord-core), TypeScript (t.coord.envelope) and proto faces, the vector that pins them — plus the aggregations the twig system folds and every venue adapter’s four transforms. Filters: ?entity= ?connector= ?kind= ?summary=1.
tools.returns: { schema, counts, entities{}, rows[] { id, kind, connector_type, entity, envelope_kind, direction, transitions[], order_key[], signer, access, price, proof, lambda, rust, ts, proto, vectors[], owner, product }, aggregations[], adapters[], ops }.

tools.name: lambda_components
tools.summary: The Lambda Studio component catalogue: every ready piece a Taifoon Lambda or a studio flow may be built from, native (coord RPC, the stream, the carriers, the vault signer guard, the Pons v2 venue, the market makers, the solver) and borrowed (Relay, LI.FI, Across, deBridge, Mayan, GOAT plugins, AgentKit, x402, Pons and pump.fun references), each with its source, licence, reuse mode (code · api · reference: code only under a permissive licence), the chains it serves and where it plugs into Taifoon. Filters: ?kind= ?chain= ?native=1.
tools.returns: { schema, rule, order[], items{ <id>: { id, name, kinds[], native, chains[], source{ repo, license, ref?, paths?[], stars?, pushed? }, reuse, taifoon[], state, note? } } }.

tools.name: lambda_golden
tools.summary: The five golden networks that work always (Solana, Robinhood Chain 4663, Base, Arbitrum, Arc): per network the six measured capabilities (read, quote, route, settle, fuel, stream) with the components behind each (two independent ones for quote and route), and the gas floor of every service signer acting there, computed from the measured gas price. Anything short of live names its reason and next step. ?chain= one network.
tools.returns: { schema, rule, order[], items{ <key>: { key, chain, name, caps{ <cap>: { status, via[], evidence, reason?, next_step? } }, fuel[] { id, who, gas_per_send, sends, topup, floor, state } } } }.

tools.name: lambda_flows
tools.summary: Lambda Studio flows: Taifoon Lambdas drawn as n8n-like DAGs of catalogue components (trigger · read · quote · route · guard · act · settle), every act behind the vault's signer guard and signing only what its lambda's acts allow, plus the registered Taifoon Lambdas they compile to (triggers, reads, acts, signed limits, guards, what the vault owns). The builder's workspace layout and commands (taifoon-sdk lambda flow check|compile|n8n).
tools.returns: { schema, rule, workspace{}, flows[] { id, name, what, lambda, chains[], nodes[], edges[], n8n }, lambdas{ schema, guards[], lambdas[] } }.

tools.name: pipe_dropped
tools.summary: The dropped envelopes classified by their language type: kind, entity (from the transition they name), venue and reason class, each with its count, a sample, the wiring cause and its fix. Admin only.
tools.returns: { schema, total, classes[] { kind, entity, venue, reason, count, sample, cause, fix } }.

auth.rule: admin only (x-operator-token, or a key of ours): a dead letter names its endpoint and payload digest; anyone else gets 401/403 role_denies

tools.name: commerce
tools.summary: The Taifoon Commerce Protocol (DRAFT 1.0-draft.1, internal review): the one agentic commerce standard — the parties (buyer, layer, seller, reseller, protocol, venue, evaluator, assurer, settler), the legs a payment leaves as (the one payment scheme, never a second fee rule), the twelve hops of a sale bound to the v2 transitions and the stage register, the vault transitions with receipts, the four queue views, every venue profile with the state each hop has today, and worked agreements whose legs sum to the payment. ?spec=1 returns the draft specification as markdown. Filters: ?venue= ?hop= ?summary=1.
tools.returns: { schema, version, state, rule, sources, counts{ hop_states }, hop_order[], parties[], legs[], hops[], vault_transitions[], queues[], venues[], examples[], conformance, versioning }.

auth.rule: DRAFT under internal review: a key of ours, the operator token, or a key/tenant named in COMMERCE_DRAFT_REVIEWERS (the allowlist); anyone else gets 401/403 draft_internal. Public once the owner marks 1.0.

tools.name: pipe_twigs
tools.summary: Every Twigster actor’s twig by class (_TWIG_CLASSES_v1_, docs/TWIGSTER.md §7.1): the two classes the language defines (permanent: every twig kept for good, any index provable, the head anchored under the superroot; transient: a bounded ring whose rows expire after a TTL), the actor rules (upgrades:<chain> for a chain’s upgrade records, signals:<topic> for broadcast signals) and each actor’s count, signed head, oldest twig retained in memory and rows TTL.
tools.returns: { schema: taifoon.pipe.twigs.v1, classes[] { twig_class, keep_twigs | null, rows_ttl_s | null }, rules[] { actor, twig_class, batch, kind, order_key_prefix, why }, default_class, twigs[] { actor, twig_class, count, head_hash, peaks[], oldest_retained, kept_in_memory, keep_twigs, rows_ttl_s, proofs, head (the last signed taifoon.twigster.head.v1 or null) } }.

tools.name: pipe_twigs__actor
tools.summary: One actor’s twig described: its class, count, head, oldest twig retained in memory and rows TTL — for example upgrades:36927, the devnet’s upgrade twig.
tools.returns: { schema: taifoon.pipe.twigs.v1, actor, twig_class, count, head_hash, peaks[], oldest_retained, kept_in_memory, keep_twigs | null, rows_ttl_s | null, proofs, head }; 404 { error, twig_class } before the actor’s first flush.

tools.name: pipe_twigs__actor_proof__twig
tools.summary: _TWIG_PROOF_PUBLIC_v1_: the inclusion proof of one twig in an actor's Merkle Mountain Range (the per-actor MMR of flush roots the Twigster signs, docs/TWIGSTER.md §7), with the actor's last signed head. A twig is addressed as <actor>#<twig> (taifoon#242700, directory:x402-base#3, upgrades:36927#0). Hashes only; keyless. The twig hash itself comes from the record that names it (a signed envelope's turbine record): siblings fold it to its peak, the peaks bag to the signed head.
tools.returns: { schema: taifoon.twigster.proof.v1, kind: twig, actor, head (the last signed taifoon.twigster.head.v1: actor, count, head, peaks[], at, cert_ref, sig) | null, proof { count, index, peak_index, peaks[], siblings[] } }. 400 bad_param (actor: [A-Za-z0-9:._-]{1,96}; twig: a whole number); 404 for an unknown actor, a twig beyond the head, or (a transient actor) one older than its retained ring; 503 while the pipe is unavailable.

tools.name: pipe_bench
tools.summary: _PIPE_LIVE_BENCH_v1_: the latest benchmark of the coord pipe, run read-only by coord coordpipe/bench/live (keyless public /v1 reads, loopback reads on the pipe's own host, its journal and Prometheus, the in-process micro benches): ingest throughput, ack latency p50/p95/p99, fold time per batch, search latency by query type, proof and twig lookups, stream delivery, memory per 100k leaves, start to ready. Every row names its source; a source that did not answer is status dead with its reason (shown as —), never a stale number. A generated constant (register/bench/pipe-bench.json): its age is now − finished_at. Keyless.
tools.returns: { schema: taifoon.pipe.bench.v1, run_id, run_at, finished_at, how, bounds, pipe { state, commit, installed_at, memory_max_bytes, last_batch, restarts_24h[] }, rows[] { id, group: ingest | ack | fold | search | proof | stream | memory | start, what, source: public /v1 | loopback | prometheus | journal | mac in-process, unit, status: ok | dead, value?, p50?, p95?, p99?, max?, n?, note? } }; ?group= the rows of one group; ?summary=1 the run and row ids. 400 bad_param for an unknown group.

tools.name: pipe_queues
tools.summary: The settlement queues of every chain (_SETTLEMENT_QUEUES_v1_): READ (what the lanes observed), SIGN (waiting for the Twigster signature), SETTLE (signed, waiting for a settler) and ACK (sent, waiting for the chain's inclusion), per chain and venue, with depth, the oldest age, declared value waiting and the last errors. Views of the one pipe, not separate queues. ?chain= filters (eip155:8453 or 8453).
tools.returns: { schema: taifoon.pipe.queues.v1, at, queues[] { name, why }, chains{ <chain>: { read|sign|settle|ack: { depth, oldest_s, venues{ <venue>: { depth, oldest_s, needs_signature?, value?, last_errors? } } } } }, read{ sources, chains } }.

tools.name: pipe_queues_detail
tools.summary: The settlement queues with the oldest envelope ids of every chain × queue × venue cell (?detail=N, at most 50). Owner only.
tools.returns: pipe/queues with venues{}.oldest[] { id, age_s }.

auth.rule: owner only (x-operator-token, or a key of ours): the ids name live envelopes; anyone else gets 401/403 role_denies

tools.name: pipe_claimable
tools.summary: The public SETTLE queue: the signed settle and release envelopes any settler may submit now, oldest first, each with its leaves, deadline and the plan the pipe's carrier priced: every call with who may send it, to, data, gas and fees. Calls whose who is anyone (and a wallet's own signed transaction) are open: submit one, then report it with pipe/settled. A sealed envelope's plan is withheld.
tools.returns: { schema: taifoon.pipe.claimable.v1, at, count, how, envelopes[] { id, kind, chain, venue, order_key, deadline, attempts, age_s, terms, signature, leaves, needs_signature, plan, open_steps[], sealed } }.

tools.name: pipe_settled
tools.summary: An outside settler reports the transaction it submitted for a claimable envelope. Nothing moves on the report: the carrier reads the receipt, and a successful transaction that is the plan's call (or the wallet's own bytes) delivers the envelope; the chain's inclusion acks it. The first valid inclusion wins; a later one is recorded and changes nothing. At most 5 reports per envelope.
tools.returns: { outcome: recorded (202) | duplicate (200) | full (429) | not_claimable (409) | unknown (404), id, tx, chain, state, reports }.

tools.name: pipe_stats
tools.summary: The pipe’s counts: envelopes by state, kind and carrier; the delivered ones with their evidence; the adverts generated, delivered, acked, converted.
tools.returns: { envelopes, by_state, by_kind, by_carrier, delivered[], adverts }.

tools.name: pipe_volume
tools.summary: What went through the layer, summed from the envelopes themselves (_PIPE_VOLUME_v1_): envelopes, base units, USD, the layer's cut, venue fees, reseller markup and seller share per venue, asset, kind and state. Filters: venues, from_venues, to_venues, topics (= to_agents; bridge.* by prefix), chains (CAIP or a bare EVM id), assets, kinds, states, window (1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, all) or since/until; group_by (from_venue, to_venue, to_agent, asset, kind, state, chain) and an optional step for a series.
tools.returns: { schema, since, until, resolution, group_by, rows[{…group, envelopes, units, usd, unpriced, cut_usd, venue_fee_usd, markup_usd, seller_usd}], total, series?, ready }.

tools.name: compare
tools.summary: Price one transfer across every protocol at once.
tools.returns: A row per protocol: what arrives, what it costs, how long it takes.

tools.name: transfer_plan
tools.summary: The exact calls a wallet must sign to make a transfer.
tools.returns: An ordered list of contract calls. Nothing is signed or sent here. `tenant: "moonbeam"` points every call at Moonbeam’s own hook and factory on Base.

tools.name: bridge_plan
tools.summary: The same call as POST /v1/transfer/plan, under the planner’s own name.
tools.returns: The ordered, unsigned contract calls of a USDC transfer (approve + bridge through the CCTP fee router), the fees and what arrives. Body: { src_chain_id, dst_chain_id, amount (USDC units, 6 decimals), sender, recipient }.

tools.name: transfer__chain__tx
tools.summary: Where one transfer has got to.
tools.returns: Its state, timings, and the destination transaction once it lands.

tools.name: transfers
tools.summary: The transfers the service has seen.
tools.returns: Records plus totals: volume, fees, and how long each tier really took.

tools.name: transfer_watch__chain__tx
tools.summary: Follow one transfer as it moves.
tools.returns: A server-sent event per state change.

tools.name: openapi.json
tools.summary: This API as OpenAPI.
tools.returns: A schema an agent or client generator can read: every operation (info.x-taifoon-parts points to the parts). _OPENAPI_PARTS_v1_: ?group=<group> and/or ?prefix=<first path segment> answer one part, a valid OpenAPI 3.1 document with those operations (the group's tag, the paths under /v1/<prefix>) and the component schemas they reference; 404 not_found with groups[] and prefixes[] for a selection no operation is in. GET /v1/openapi/index.json lists the parts.

tools.name: openapi_index.json
tools.summary: The OpenAPI document in parts: one smaller document per group, for a reader that cannot take the whole.
tools.returns: _OPENAPI_PARTS_v1_: schema taifoon.openapi.parts.v1, whole { url, paths, operations, bytes }, parts[] { group, description, paths, operations, bytes (as served), url (GET /v1/openapi.json?group=<group>), segments[] { prefix, operations, bytes, url (?group=<group>&prefix=<prefix>) } }, contents[] { op ("<METHOD> <path>"), group }: every operation, rule. Every operation is in exactly one group and one segment of it.

tools.name: agents_jobs
tools.summary: Every agent job the layer has settled.
tools.returns: Totals funded and paid, by month, since the first day.

tools.name: agents_providers
tools.summary: The agents doing that work.
tools.returns: Per provider: jobs done and USDC earned.

tools.name: agents_profiles
tools.summary: Every seller’s profile in one list: state, classes, price, checks, jobs with unrelated buyers; ?class=&state=clean&admitted=1 is the verified sellers of a class (_SELLER_PROFILE_v1_).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.seller.profiles.v1, read_at, age_s, stale, counts { sellers, by_state { clean, findings, parked, unchecked }, by_kind, outside }, states (the words of each state), rules { admit_after, park_after, disprove_after, findings_window_days, state, words }, matched, by_state, rows[] { id (the seller’s host), name, state, classes, price, scheme free | x402 | listing | escrow_other_chain | not_payable | unknown, network, checks (passed/all), jobs_unrelated, response_ms, findings, opt_out, last_seen, link }, next_offset. ?class= &state=clean|findings|parked|unchecked &side=outside|layer &admitted=1 &q= &limit (≤ 500) &offset. Folded every 30 min from the hireable rows, the listings and their class probes, the seller probe, GET /v1/explorer/jobs, the paid canary lane’s ledger and the opt-outs.

tools.name: agents__seller_profile
tools.summary: One seller’s on-hire properties: what it serves, how it is paid, how its replies checked, who it worked for (_SELLER_PROFILE_v1_).
tools.returns: :seller = its host (agent402.tools), <chain>:<agentId>, listing id (ls_…) or address. id, name, aliases, side outside | layer, classes { declared, derived, admitted }, venues, endpoints, payment { scheme, price_usd, asset, network, why }, admission[] { class, passes_in_row, probes, paid_passes, admitted, need, by }, checks { pass, fail, by_check[] { check, pass, fail, last_failure { at, why, link } } }, grades { code, jev } { n, pass, fail }, jobs { unrelated, practice, settled_unrelated, delivered }, response_ms, opt_out, last_seen, state clean | findings | parked | unchecked, state_words, state_why, parked_until, findings { n, by_kind, latest }, links, read_at, age_s. 404 for a seller the profiles do not hold.

tools.name: agents__seller_findings
tools.summary: One seller’s findings as facts, each with its record: a reply that failed its check, a paid call that returned nothing or something unrelated, a payment that did not settle, a payee or endpoint that changed, a reply copied from another seller, a claimed class the probes disprove (_SELLER_PROFILE_v1_).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.seller.findings.v1, id, state, state_why, parked_until, n, by_kind, words, findings[] newest first { kind check_failed | paid_empty | paid_unrelated | payment_unsettled | identity_mismatch | reply_copied | class_claim_disproved, at, words, asked, came_back, rule, ref { demand, handshake, listing, tx, chain, nonce }, link, paid_usd }, profile, read_at. A finding is not a verdict on the seller.

tools.name: agents__seller_assurance
tools.summary: One seller’s assurance record on the time axis (_ASSURANCE_RECORD_AXIS_v1_): one point per graded job, oldest first, with k passed of n graded and the premium for the next job from that record (jev-wilson premium: the Wilson upper bound on the failure rate, covered while at most 30 %). The history is the layer’s own records, so every point links the job it comes from; hire terms come only from POST /v1/pools/quote.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.seller.assurance.v1, id, name, asked? { alias, agent } (an agent of a host asked by <chain>:<agentId>, a listing id or an endpoint: the axis is that agent’s own), k, n, score (the Wilson lower bound of the pass rate k/n at z = 1.959963984540054, jev-wilson wilsonLower: the pass rate the record supports at 95 %; null when n = 0), score_rule, premium_ratio (the next job’s premium ÷ price, null with no passing job), covered, first_at, last_at, points_n, points[] oldest first (the newest 30) { at, class, verdict pass | fail, by code | jev, whose practice | unrelated, k, n, premium_ratio, covered, ref { demand, handshake, job, tx, chain }, link }, rule, quote (POST /v1/pools/quote: the terms of one job now), profile, read_at, age_s, stale. 404 for an unknown seller; 503 before the first fold. :seller = the seller's host, <chain>:<agentId>, listing id or address.

tools.name: agents__id_listings_suggest
tools.summary: Taifoon Search: the venues an agent should list on (_LISTING_SUGGEST_v1_, release 2026-11-07 item C2). For a registered agent (its id, a listing id or an endpoint; or ?classes=a,b for a card not registered yet) every venue whose market carries one of its classes, ranked by expected USD a week = that venue's paid USD for the class over the window × the share a new seller takes (1 / (sellers + 1)); each row carries the venue's own incentive (its fee row, its stake, the words its buyers search), the paid and ask medians, the buyer price at the median (the one price rule, _UNDERCUT_v3_: 20 % under the cheapest matching seller, never under cost × 1.2), and the listing's state on that venue from the listing keep (pending · awaiting_owner · listed) with its next step. One table with the genie CLI (`genie suggest`) and the MCP action taifoon_find.listings: the same vectors (coord lang/gen/listing-suggest.vectors.json).
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.listing.suggest.v1, rule: LISTING_SUGGEST_v1, read_at, agent { id, classes[], venue, price_usd }, rows[] { venue, market, class, expected_usd_wk, paid_usd_7d, sellers, median_usd, buyer_usd_at_median, origin, incentive { fee, stake, words }, keep { state, next } }, why? (no venue carries a class of this agent), source }. A figure the sides file did not give reads null; the rank never divides by zero.

auth.rule: Open: no key needed; a key sent is passed on, never required.

tools.name: tree_search
tools.summary: Taifoon Search over the whole layer: a need said in plain words ("find a trading strategy", "sell gpu inference") against one index of the classes, the venues, the /v1 operations, the genie programs, the studio strategies and, for a key, the markets and the open-market routes. Words and meaning are fused (BM25 and vectors by reciprocal rank), a need is an OR of its words, and every row carries its highlights and `next`: the one call that acts on the hit. Every answer names the leaf of the index it was read from. vertical=agents finds working agents across every market they are listed on (each row with its venues and its cohort mark), vertical=n8n is the n8n landscape the harvester holds (each kind, creator, publisher and template with who runs it, its class, its public page, how Taifoon deals with it and the n8n-nodes-taifoon operation that does it), and facet= counts every match by venue, cohort, class, vertical or a commerce facet (side, stage, step, category, why, next_move, state) before the cut. The order is the organic one: no row is promoted here (the marked strip is GET /v1/tree/spotlight). One metered read per call.
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.tree.search.v1, q, mode, verticals[], visibility public | key, top, matched, total (every match before the cut), facet? and facets? { <value>: count } when facet is sent, rows[] { id, vertical, title, score, why { said[], text?, vector? }, highlights[], attrs, mark? { cohort, label, promoted (always false here) }, next { op | cli | mcp | step, why } }, leaf { address, epoch, digest }, took_ms, why? and next? when nothing is near }. 400 bad_param (q missing, an unknown vertical, mode or facet) with next_step; 401 key_required when a key-only vertical is named without a key; 503 while the index is not readable.

auth.rule: Open: without a key the public verticals (classes, venues, agents, ops, programs, strategies, n8n); a valid key reads every vertical (markets and routes too).

tools.name: tree_outlets
tools.summary: From a need in plain words to a series of listings: the classes the words name (the tree's classes vertical; a need no class is near answers no_class, never a guess), the venues whose market carries them ranked by expected USD a week (LISTING_SUGGEST_v1, the rows of GET /v1/agents/:id/listings/suggest), and one ordered series of calls: one listing definition, one claim per venue, the publish. A read: every step is a request the caller sends with its own key; nothing is sent, signed or paid here. One metered read per call.
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.genie.tree.outlets.v1, need, state outlets | no_class | no_venue, why?, classes[] { class, category, score, said[], highlights[] }, rows[] (the suggestion's rows; without a key the figures are left out), series { state ready | preview, needs, steps[] { n, op, why, sends, venue?, classes?, rank?, keep?, entry?, body?, gate? }, venues, dropped } | null, leaf { address, epoch, digest }, read_at, visibility public | key }. 400 bad_param (neither need nor classes, a class id or price that is not one) with next_step; 401 for a key that is not valid; 503 while the market sides or the index are not readable.

auth.rule: Without a key: the public preview (the venues in order, no figure). With a valid key: the plan with its figures; its series is ready only when the key has an active monthly plan (GET /v1/access/key), else a preview that starts at GET /v1/access/plan.

tools.name: tree_leaf
tools.summary: The head leaf of the search tree: the address of the index epoch every search answer names (the language's canister scheme, coord://offchain/genie/index/<namespace>@v<epoch>/<digest>), its epoch and its digest, with what each vertical holds. Free.
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.tree.leaf.v1, namespace, leaf { address, epoch, digest, docs, wal_seq }, as_emitted (the leaf this deployment built equals the one coord emitted), verticals { <name>: { visibility public | key, what } }, search, outlets }. 503 while the index is not readable.

tools.name: tree_spotlight
tools.summary: The strip of one house cohort (taifoon or moonbeam) a site shows above its search answer: the cohort's agents nearest the need first (q), then its widest-listed ones. A placement that says so: every row carries mark.promoted = true and the cohort's label, and the answer of GET /v1/tree/search under it is ranked without the cohort. Free.
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.genie.tree.spotlight.v1, cohort, label, placement, q, top, agents (the cohort's agents), markets[] (the venues they are listed on), rows[] { id, vertical agents, title, score, why, highlights[], attrs { cohort, venue, venues[], venue_count, classes[], hireable, listed, site, since }, mark { cohort, label, promoted: true }, next, near (the row is near q) }, leaf { address, epoch, digest } }. 400 bad_param for a cohort that is not taifoon or moonbeam (the Grid first cohort has no strip), with next_step; 503 while the index is not readable.

tools.name: venues
tools.summary: Where outside buyers pay for agent work, money first: x402 on Base, Solana, Arbitrum, Robinhood Chain and Monad, Virtuals memo-ACP, ERC-8183, BitAgent; what they buy by class, who buys on a schedule, the sellers admitted there and the next action (_VENUES_v1_). ?view=pipeline: the reseller pipeline per venue and class, counts only (_RESELLER_PIPELINE_v1_). ?view=sides: every marketplace on both sides per class in the commerce hops — what sellers ask and what buyers actually paid, the most expensive single payment with its tx, the biggest spender and the resale room (_MARKET_SIDES_v1_).

tools.name: prices_cheapest

The cheapest is the lowest output price among quoted rows read in the last 24 h; a model with none prints —. The buyer price is the one sell price (sellPriceOf: the higher of 20 % under the cheapest and the Taifoon cost x 1.2); the full-fee line is the supplier price at or under which a seller is routed at the full 20 % fee.

tools.name: chat_completions
tools.summary: The OpenAI-compatible door of the inference reseller: point any OpenAI client (n8n's OpenAI Chat Model node, the openai SDK, LangChain, a coding agent) at base URL https://coord.taifoon.dev/v1 with a tfr_ key. The model picks the listing (GET /v1/models data[]); each call is priced per request and charged to the key; one usage row and one meter line per call; the hire recorded with its agreement. stream: true answers as chat.completion.chunk events ending in [DONE]. Parameters the gate does not apply (temperature, tools, images …) are named back in taifoon.not_applied.

auth.rule: _OPENAI_GATE_v1_ (M4 + M10): your tfr_ key as the OpenAI API key (Authorization: Bearer tfr_…, or X-API-Key). Paid from the key's balance at the list price (a key with nothing holds the free agreement: a cold free key is served from it, _FREE_TRYOUT_v1_); a child key pays from its reseller. Every key holds the inference right by default (_INFERENCE_RIGHT_v1_); its owner revokes it with POST /v1/tenant/keys { action: update, prefix, inference: false }. _AGREEMENTS_ENFORCED_v1_: the key holds TSUL-1.1 and TAT for inference (its own, or inherited from any key of its reseller tenant), or it paid (a bought plan or a credited balance: never refused), else 403 agreement_required with taifoon.next_step (POST /v1/access/agreements); AGREEMENTS_REQUIRED=0 switches the check off. _FREE_AGREEMENT_CAPS_v1_: the free agreement is held per key, per tenant, per IP (every key minted from it and every call from it, by its salted hash) and per IP × outside model; an outside model above 0.50 USD per 1M output tokens is not on the free tier. _WALLET_CREDIT_v1_: no key needed for a wallet that topped up (POST /v1/access/subscribe without a key credits the paying wallet): send SIGN-IN-WITH-X (x402 sign-in-with-x: base64 JSON of the EIP-4361 fields for domain coord.taifoon.dev, a fresh nonce, issuedAt within 5 minutes, and the wallet's EIP-191 or EIP-1271 signature; or Authorization: Bearer siwx_<the same value>) on each call; it is debited from the wallet's credit, never into debt.

tools.name: models_verify
tools.summary: The inference verification board (_MODEL_VERIFY_v1_, coord lang/cue/model-verify.cue): one row per model × supplier, each verified in layers as others do it. L0 live: a call to the supplier itself every few minutes under a fresh nonce (status, latency, the answer's model field, right or not). L1 identity: seeded fingerprint probes once a day, compared with the other suppliers of the same weights and with our attested or own row of them. L2 use case: two tool calls checked by code, two reasoning items with exact answers and one open task graded by Jev under RUBRIC_v2, weekly, against the peer median. L3 attestation: the NEAR attested path. Verdicts: attested · verified · echoed · suspect · failing · — (stale). Only attested or verified rows claim the model name; a failing row is not sold; a suspect row is routed after its verified siblings.

tools.summary: Claim one hit of match/search: the pipe answers the leaf's inclusion proof against the venue's signed head now, and the bundle the delivery lane of its class prescribes (compute: offer → hire → settle; grade: offer → hire → grade; content: offer → hire → delivery; alert: offer → delivery; rpc: offer → hire), ordered and atomic, with the agreement of the Taifoon Commerce Protocol (the legs, Σ = the payment). The bundle is sent into the pipe under the key's actor when `send` is true (devnet and the taifoon outlet; a mainnet outlet needs the key's outlet grant), else returned to send yourself. Charged: one match unit plus the settlement leg the carrier priced.

tools.name: vault_arm
tools.summary: The latest arm of a tenant vault: the owner-signed EIP-712 VaultArm a program's runner verifies before it may act live, with the policy hash it must equal and the vault's current owner.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.vault.arm.v1 { vault, tenant, arm { vault, armed, policy, expires, nonce, signature, signer, recorded_at } | null, policy_hash, owner_key (the CURRENT owner walked from the owner chain; "pending" when none is linked), state armed | dry | expired | stale_policy | stale_owner | no_arm | unpaid (a customer vault whose tenant holds no running paid plan: vault.cue vault_arm.paid_plan), armed_until, next_nonce, eip712 { domain, primaryType, types }, addresses[] { purpose, address }, chains[], caps { spend, debit, keys[], program, program_limits }, balances? (with ?balances=1: [{ purpose, address, chain, wei, eth }], a chain that did not answer is null) }. 400 bad_param, 404 unknown_vault, 429.

auth.rule: Open: no key. _VAULT_ARM_v1_ (lang/cue/vault.cue vault_arm): a signature is not a secret, so the latest arm is public; held to 120 a minute per IP (vault_admission reads.per_key_min, per IP because it is keyless), cached 5 s.

tools.name: vault_arm
tools.summary: Arm or disarm a tenant vault with the owner's wallet signature: the cockpit's Arm button, t.vault.arm() and taifoon_vault_arm all build the one typed message; stored as the vault's arm and recorded on vault:intents:<tenant>. Nothing is signed or sent here.
tools.returns: Send { vault, armed, policy (the vault's policy_hash), expires (unix s; armed: after now and at most 30 days ahead; disarm: any), nonce (above the stored one), signature }. 201 schema taifoon.vault.arm.v1 { stored: true, arm, state, armed_until, stream recorded | deferred, envelope_id? } (deferred: the arm is stored, the pipe record is retried by the next arm or read). 400 bad_param | expired | too_long, 402 plan_required (arming a customer vault needs its tenant's running paid plan; a disarm never does), 403 not_owner (owner pending, or the signer is not the current owner) | bad_signature, 404 unknown_vault, 409 policy_mismatch | stale_nonce, 429, 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: Keyless: the authority is the signature. An EIP-712 VaultArm (domain Taifoon Vault v1, no chainId) recovered to the vault's CURRENT owner (the owner chain of vault/owner, from owner_auth.genesis); a pending owner answers 403 not_owner. 10 a minute, 100 a day per IP.

tools.name: vault_custody-standing
tools.summary: One CLOB vault account's standing as coord-sign's custody.release reads it (_CUSTODY_STANDING_v1_): its own operator wallet from the orderbook's identity door and whether that wallet's taifoon.io account holds a running paid plan, from the billing source.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.vault.custody-standing.v1 { account, operator_wallet (0x lowercase | null: a house principal or no linked wallet), paid, state plan_running | no_plan | no_wallet }. 400 bad_account, 404 no_principal, 503 unread (a source did not answer: the signer refuses).

auth.rule: Only the off-box signer's own key: the key that reads its inbox (sign.cue deploy.inbox, lang/gen/sign-inboxes.json); any other key is 403 signer_only. A person's billing standing is never public. Never cached.

tools.name: vault_owner
tools.summary: The owner authentication of a tenant vault: the genesis owner and the ordered chain of signed link, rotate, recover and cancel acts, walked to the current owner and the pending change.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.vault.owner.v1 { vault, tenant, genesis, current, pending { action, owner, effective, nonce } | null, recovery, rotation_delay_h, recovery_delay_h, next_nonce, chain[] { vault, action, owner, effective, nonce, signatures { owner?, current?, recovery? }, recorded_at, state effective | pending | cancelled }, eip712 { domain, primaryType, types }, signatures (who signs each action) }. 400 bad_param, 404 unknown_vault, 429.

auth.rule: Open: no key. _VAULT_OWNER_v1_ (lang/cue/vault.cue vault_owner): the chain of signed owner acts is public; 120 a minute per IP.

tools.name: vault_owner
tools.summary: Link, rotate, recover or cancel a tenant vault's owner with signed EIP-712 VaultOwner acts; stored in the vault's owner chain and recorded on vault:intents:<tenant>. A bearer key alone never changes an owner.
tools.returns: Send { vault, action, owner, effective, nonce, signatures { owner?, current?, recovery? } }. 201 schema taifoon.vault.owner.v1 { stored: true, act, current, pending, stream recorded | deferred }. 400 bad_param | too_early | no_recovery, 401 unauthorized (link without a key or session), 403 not_vault_tenant | not_owner | bad_signature, 404 unknown_vault, 409 owned | stale_nonce | pending_change | nothing_pending | same_owner, 429, 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: Keyless but for link: the authority is the signatures over one EIP-712 VaultOwner — link [owner] (only while the vault has no owner, and only for the vault's own tenant: its tenant key or signed-in session holding one of the vault's key refs), rotate [current, owner] (effective ≥ now + rotation_delay_h), recover [recovery, owner] (effective ≥ now + recovery_delay_h), cancel [current]. One pending change at a time; nonce strictly increasing. 10 a minute, 50 a day per IP.

tools.name: vault_setup
tools.summary: What a tenant requested for its vault (_VAULT_SETUP_v1_, lang/cue/vault.cue vault_lifecycle: a vault is born requested): every face (main and each vault added in Studio) with its settings, digest and revision, the policy hash its VaultArm will name, and the record on vault:intents:<tenant>.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.vault.setup.v1 { vault, tenant, state (the lifecycle state), requested { revision, updated_at, policy_hash, record { revision, envelope, recorded written | refused | unavailable }, faces { <face>: { config, digest, revision, requested_at } } } | null, proof (/v1/pipe/status/<envelope>) | null }. 401 unauthorized, 403 not_owner, 429, 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: The vault's own tenant: its key, or its signed-in session on www.taifoon.io. A key reads only its own tenant's vault (vault:tenant:<slug>); 20 a minute, 300 a day per IP.

tools.name: vault_setup
tools.summary: Request a tenant vault's settings (_VAULT_SETUP_v1_): one face's roles, skins, integrations, networks, what it holds, pay-in rails, caps, wires, region and pay-out, checked against the sets read on the server (the Studio drawer's own check). Without commit: the unsigned plan. commit: true stores it as the vault's requested config and records one envelope on vault:intents:<tenant>.
tools.returns: Send { face? (main, or the id of a vault added in Studio), config (the Studio drawer's VaultCfg), commit? }. 200 { plan { schema taifoon.vault.setup.v1, vault, tenant, face, unsigned: true, config, digest, record, policy, policy_hash, changes[] { field, part record | policy, from, to }, acts[] { act record | link | provision | arm, op, signer, state done | next | later, why, typed_data? (the VaultArm the owner signs) }, unchanged }, stored: false, next_step }; with commit: 201 { stored: true, requested { revision, policy_hash, record { envelope, recorded }, faces }, proof } (200 unchanged: true when it is the stored request). 400 invalid_input { field, problems }, 401 unauthorized, 403 not_owner | read_only_key, 409 too_many_faces, 429, 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: The vault's own tenant: its key, or its signed-in session on www.taifoon.io; a read-only key plans and never records (403 read_only_key). Nothing is signed here: the record is the tenant's own act; the arm stays the owner wallet's VaultArm (vault/arm), the provision the box's. 20 a minute, 300 a day per IP.

tools.name: vault_receipt
tools.summary: Report one act a vault program mined (sweep, claim, buy, sell, approve, airdrop, topup, deploy): the door reads the tx from the chain, checks it succeeded and was sent from the vault, and records it on vault:intents:<tenant>. Idempotent per tx; nothing is signed or sent here.
tools.returns: Send { vault, kind sweep | claim | buy | sell | approve | airdrop | topup | deploy, chain (CAIP-2, one of the vault's chains), tx (0x + 64 hex) }. 201 schema taifoon.vault.receipt.v1 { stored: true, receipt { vault, kind, chain, tx, from, from_purpose, to, block, gasUsed, effectiveGasPrice, fee_wei, recorded_at }, stream recorded | deferred, envelope_id? } (deferred: the receipt is stored, the pipe did not answer). 200 the same body with duplicate: true when the tx was already recorded. 400 bad_param, 404 not_a_vault | tx_not_found (no receipt yet: retry once it is mined), 409 tx_failed (the receipt is reverted) | not_from_vault (tx.from is not one of the vault's addresses), 422 chain_not_served (the chain is not one of the vault's), 429, 503 chain_unreadable | store_unavailable.

auth.rule: Keyless: the chain is the proof. The door trusts nothing the caller says but the tx hash: it reads the receipt and the transaction itself over the coord RPC rotation (lib/chain-tx readTxs, the one /v1/chain/tx read) and records the act only when the receipt is success and tx.from is one of the vault's own addresses (vault · topup · spend). 10 a minute, 300 a day per IP.

tools.name: vault_receipts
tools.summary: The acts a tenant vault's program reported and the door verified on chain, newest first: kind, chain, tx, from, to, block and the gas each one cost.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.vault.receipt.v1 { vault, tenant, count, receipts[] { vault, kind, chain, tx, from, from_purpose, to, block, gasUsed, effectiveGasPrice, fee_wei, recorded_at }, gas { txs, fee_wei } (over the receipts returned) }. 400 bad_param, 404 not_a_vault, 429.

auth.rule: Open: no key. Tx hashes are public; 120 a minute per IP, cached 5 s.

tools.name: attest_hire
tools.summary: Check an agent’s hire claim against the chain.
tools.returns: A verdict per claim: confirmed, contradicted, or unverifiable — with what the chain actually says.

tools.name: n8n_catalog
tools.summary: Every operation as an n8n-importable tool.
tools.returns: One entry per operation in the shape an HTTP Request node wants, plus what we measured about n8n’s own library.

tools.name: n8n_demand
tools.summary: The n8n harvest's verdicts on both sides, row by row (_N8N_DEMAND_PAID_v1_): every n8n template, community node, creator and node publisher the harvester reads (the daily taifoon-n8n-demand pass), with its sell-side verdict (we can resell it: class fit, a callable endpoint, terms that allow resale) and its buy-side verdict (it calls a class we sell). Paged: one manifest and at most 12 pages of 200 rows per call; the answer states read_at, and a source that is dead or older than 72 h is 503 with read_at '—', never stale rows.
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.n8n.demand.v1, read_at, age_s, run, kind, side, filters{ q, class }, limit, total (rows of the view; null when q or class filter), view_rows, count, rows[] (template { id, name, url, creator, verified, views, price, classes[], buy_classes[], sell, buy, why } · node { name, publisher, description, downloads_monthly, updated, npm_url, repository, licence, classes[], buy_classes[], sell, buy, why } · creator { username, verified, takes_fees, templates, paid_templates, views, paid_views, price, classes[], sell, buy, both, resale } · publisher { publisher, nodes, downloads_monthly, sell, buy, both, classes[] }), next_cursor (null at the end), scanned_pages, summary{ templates, nodes, creators, publishers, sold[], buy_classes, licences }, sources, paid{ by, with plan | balance | none, micro_usdc, usdc }, meter{ step, product, served_by, kept } }. 400 bad_request names the parameter; 402 paid_key_required | budget with next_step; 410 cursor_expired (a cursor of an earlier pass); 503 unavailable { read_at: '—' } (nothing charged).

auth.rule: _N8N_DEMAND_PAID_v1_: paid Taifoon keys only. No key 401; a key that never paid (a tfr_free_ key, or any key with no balance and no plan) 402 paid_key_required with next_step (a top-up from 1 USDC, or a plan, with prices); a spent balance 402 budget. Each answered call is paid at the list price of one expensive read (0.001 USDC) from the key's plan or balance and writes one meter line on the key (served_by harvest:116:n8n-demand).

tools.name: n8n_templates
tools.summary: Taifoon's own n8n templates (_N8N_TEMPLATES_LIST_v1_): one per class of work n8n users buy most, each sold by Taifoon under the agentic-commerce agreement on one key, with its class, the n8n kinds it serves, the channel it sends, whether it was verified live in an n8n instance against production, and the wall's live price. ?class= narrows to one class.
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.n8n.templates.v1, rule, count, templates[] { id, title, class, kinds[], channel (n8n-template:<id>), verified, verified_at, price { usdc, units, per, rule, read_at, source } (the wall's live list price; '—' with why when it could not be read), listed { usdc }, door, file, who, why }, waiting[] { kind, class, why }, setup { seller_of_record, vault, pool, agreement }, channel_share }; 404 not_found for a class no Taifoon template sells.

tools.name: channels
tools.summary: Your registered channels (_CHANNEL_SHARE_v1_): each channel id your key registered, the payTo its share is paid to, and the rule (the share of Taifoon's fee a channel earns on every sale it names).
tools.returns: { ok, rule { id: CHANNEL_SHARE_v1, header: X-Taifoon-Channel, leg: channel, share_bps, of: our_fee, never, paid }, limit, count, channels[] { channel, pay_to, network, registered_at, updated_at, earns }, next_step }.

auth.rule: _CHANNEL_SHARE_v1_: the caller's own channels only (a free key too). No key 401.

tools.name: channels
tools.summary: Register a channel to your key (_CHANNEL_SHARE_v1_): send { channel, pay_to?, network? }; every sale whose buyer sends X-Taifoon-Channel: <channel> and is not your own purchase pays you a share of Taifoon's fee as the leg `channel` (share_bps in lang/gen/channel-share.json, 20 % today, the owner's number), paid on Base USDC to pay_to (or the network registered with it) from the loop vault as an unsigned plan; with no pay_to the leg is Held no_payee.
tools.returns: 201 (registered) | 200 (payTo updated) { ok, created, channel { channel, pay_to, network, registered_at, updated_at, earns }, rule, held? (no pay_to), next_step }; 400 bad_request | bad_channel | reserved_channel (one of Taifoon's own doors or templates) | bad_pay_to | bad_network; 401 no key; 409 channel_taken | too_many_channels; 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: _CHANNEL_SHARE_v1_: a key registers a channel id to itself (a free key too: the channel earns for the key that registered it). First come: another key's channel is 409 channel_taken; the same key may change its payTo. At most 20 channels per key. Never a raw key stored: the channel row holds the key's hashed ref.

tools.name: n8n_usage
tools.summary: Report one closed UTC day of an n8n workflow's executions (_N8N_USAGE_FEED_v1_): send { workflow (the channel id you registered for it), period (YYYY-MM-DD, before today, at most 92 days back), executions, template? }. Recorded once per (workflow, day) as usage evidence attributed to you (self_reported); the same report again is a replay, another count for that day is 409. Evidence only: it pays nothing. A payout follows an outside buyer's payment (a sale your workflow makes pays you its markup as reseller of record, or the channel share); paying for executions of a workflow that sells nothing through Taifoon needs a funder and is not built.
tools.returns: 201 (recorded) | 200 (replayed) { ok, created, replayed, report { workflow, period, executions, template, evidence, reported_at, digest }, rule { id, schema, evidence, pays: false, paid_by, funder, once }, next_step }; 400 bad_request | bad_workflow | bad_period | open_period | too_old | bad_executions | bad_template; 401 no key; 403 not_your_workflow; 409 period_reported (report: the day's first report); 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: _N8N_USAGE_FEED_v1_: the key that registered the workflow's channel (POST /v1/channels), or a key of the same tenant (a free key too); any other workflow is 403 not_your_workflow and nothing is stored. Never a raw key stored: the report holds the key's hashed ref.

tools.name: n8n_usage
tools.summary: Your n8n workflows' reported executions read back (_N8N_USAGE_FEED_v1_): every day you reported, narrowed by ?workflow= and ?from= / ?to= (UTC days), with totals per workflow. Evidence only: it pays nothing.
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.n8n.usage.v1, author, filters { workflow, from, to }, count, totals[] { workflow, days, executions, first, last }, reports[] { workflow, period, executions, template, evidence, reported_at, digest }, rule }; 400 bad_workflow | bad_period; 401 no key; 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: _N8N_USAGE_FEED_v1_: the caller's own reports only (its tenant's, else its key's). No key 401.

tools.name: ecosystems
tools.summary: Which agent ecosystems are on chain, and how much they overlap.
tools.returns: The job market and the registries side by side, with how many agents appear in both.

tools.name: landscape
tools.summary: Every agent ecosystem the harvester has read, as one figure: chains, work surfaces, claims, and the chains not yet scanned. `?eco=<id>` narrows the body to one ecosystem (404 with the id list otherwise); the public page for one ecosystem is /landscape/:eco.
tools.returns: totals (agents, handshake-ready, jobs, chains scanned) + ecosystems[] with a position, two figures each naming its field, a tag that means what it says (REAL / CLAIMED / BUILDING / PROPOSED), and the REGISTER prefill; data_as_of says which source answered; `funnel` = the agent funnel on every read (agents → endpoint → answered → hireable → graded → paying: count, conversion from the step before, the last different value, read_at, late flag, source route), host concentration (top hosts by hireable, hireable excluding the top host), our own purchases apart, the top probe causes with their fixes.

tools.name: landscape_funnel_history
tools.summary: How the agent funnel moved: one point per readiness pass (every 30 min), append-only.
tools.returns: points[] oldest first, each { read_at, export_at, steps: { agents, endpoint, answered, hireable, graded, paying }, paying_ours, concentration (top host, its owners, hireable without it), causes (top probe causes) }; a rebuilt point says so in `backfill`. ?since=<unix s | ISO>, ?limit=. The latest point is also in GET /v1/landscape `funnel`.

tools.name: landscape_phases
tools.summary: The five phases of the agreement as live metrics, recounted every 30 min: the Phase 0 gate, the record, x402 capture, the n8n onramp, the pools, enterprise, and the reach row by venue.
tools.returns: gate { open[], closed[], deposits_blocked }, reads_failed[], latest { read_at, metrics[] { phase (0..5, money, reach, board: listed in `phases`), metric, value | null, outside (true = outside only, false = ours only, null = not told apart, na = not a count of actors), by, source, note } }, age_s, late, unread. A null value is unread and its note says why. ?phase=, ?venue=, ?metric= filter; ?history=1 (or ?since=<unix s | ISO>, ?limit= ≤ 500) adds points[] of earlier passes. The same lines print with `npx @taifoon/cli phases`.

tools.name: landscape_wire
tools.summary: The landscape with its agents on it, in one read: every ecosystem carries the agents that answered on the wire.
tools.returns: The landscape (totals, ecosystems, data_as_of) plus per ecosystem `agents[]` — the registry’s wire-ready set for a chain (best trust first, ?per_chain= ≤ 60), the onboarding flows’ candidates for a work surface — each with label, owner, endpoint, protocol, trust, skills; `answered` names which chains the registry answered for and whether the flow store did. Cached 60 s.

tools.name: agents_named
tools.summary: The agents that can stand on a hiring page: an ERC-8004 identity whose own card has a name and a description.
tools.returns: ?chain=8453&limit=&q=. Each agent: agentId, owner, name, description, skills, endpoint, protocol, trust, wire, tee, card_source. One row per owner, best trust first; `read` says how many registry agents were scanned and `presentable` how many passed.

tools.name: agents_identity
tools.summary: ERC-8004 records read on chain, in one batch: owner, token URI and the registration card.
tools.returns: ?chain=8453&ids=17666,59048 (≤ 20). agents[] { agentId, registry, owner (ownerOf; null = no such agent, undefined = the chain did not answer), exists, tokenURI, card { name, description, endpoints }, read_at }, unread[]. The judge reads the same record when a task asks for an identity report.

tools.name: agents_card__chain__id
tools.summary: One agent’s ERC-8004 registration card, parsed.
tools.returns: name, description, skills, endpoint as the agent wrote them (tokenURI), and `presentable` — whether it can stand on a hiring page.

tools.name: agents__chain__agentId_readiness
tools.summary: What one agent still needs to be hireable, and to be assured: the ordered checklist from identity to a guaranteed quote.
