(8453 only: { by: x402, units, tx, payer, network, confirmed } | { by: balance, units, ref, funded: usdc }) }, delivery { status, reply_digest (0x keccak of the reply | null), handshake_id }, sale? and edge? (8453 only: edge { state, promoted, why }: promoted true when this payment was the edge's first outside sale and moved it to live, its evidence on the edge as live_evidence) }. 8453 (_FIRST_SALE_LIVE_v1_): unpaid, with or without a key, 402 payment_required { x402 (the v2 challenge at the scheme's price to the buyer), terms, next_step }; a payment the facilitator refuses 402 payment_refused; a seller reply with no content 503 not_delivered (nothing settled, a key's debit handed back); a key balance that is not USDC-funded (GRID credit, a plan, debt) or short 402. A payer of ours (coord ours.gen.cue), a key payment or an unconfirmed envelope serves the call and never makes the edge live. Refusals, in this order, each { ok: false, code, error, edge_id }: 400 bad_request { field }; 404 edge_not_found; 409 edge_not_live (a planned record, or an unpriced dry edge on 8453; a dry devnet edge takes calls in test units, a quoted or priced dry 8453 edge paid calls); 403 closed_by_policy (a Moonbeam edge on 8453); 409 edge_not_metered (36927 in test units; 8453 only with a whole, positive USDC quote); on 8453 a call with no payment and no key: 402 payment_required BEFORE any agreement check (_HOUSE_UNSIGNED_v1_); 403 agreement_unsigned (no signature, or the address recovered from agreement.hash + agreement.signature is not both agreement.signer and seller_of_record; the HOUSE, tenant taifoon with Taifoon's own vault as seller of record, goes on its unsigned agreement, agreement_basis house_unsigned); 403 outside_agreement (class is not the edge's class); a paid call refused here is never settled or debited; 401 without a key (except a payable 8453 edge: 402); 503 store_unavailable. Every refusal from 409 edge_not_live on counts one on the edge (GET /v1/exchanges/:edge_id/agreement refusals).

auth.rule: A relayer key (X-API-Key) the operator minted, as POST /v1/exchanges/edge; a free key answers 403 free_scope, no key 401. _FIRST_SALE_LIVE_v1_: a mainnet (8453) edge that takes calls is bought per call with x402 (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE / X-PAYMENT) and needs no key; without a payment (and without a key with a USDC balance) it answers 402 with the challenge.

tools.name: exchanges__edge_id_meter
tools.summary: The meter lines of one exchange edge (_EXCHANGE_CALL_v1_): one line per call made through the edge, newest first.
tools.returns: ?limit (1..200, default 50) → { ok, edge_id, meter_row (meter:exchange-<tenant>-<edge16>), lines[] (the meter lines POST /v1/exchanges/:edge_id/call wrote: { id, edge_id, at, class, handshake_id, status, unit, legs { seller_share, our_fee, reseller_markup }, price, edge_state, paid? (8453: how the call was paid) }), count }; 400 bad_request { field }; 404 edge_not_found; 503 store_unavailable.

tools.name: exchanges__edge_id_agreement
tools.summary: The agreement of one exchange edge as it is enforced on calls (_EXCHANGE_CALL_v1_): who signed it, whether that is the signer it names and the seller of record, its scope and the calls it refused.
tools.returns: { ok, agreement { edge_id, id (agr_<hash[2:18]>), enforced: true, signed (a signature is stored), signature_valid (the address recovered from hash + signature equals both signer and seller_of_record), recovered (0x address | null), signer, seller_of_record, basis (signed | house_unsigned | unsigned), admits (a call goes through on it: a valid signature, or the house unsigned), hash (the EIP-712 digest, recorded signed or not), scope { tenant, class, chain_id }, state (the edge's state), refusals (calls refused on this edge, a number) } }; 400 bad_request { field }; 404 edge_not_found; 503 store_unavailable.

tools.name: pools_plan
tools.summary: The pool plan for a tenant: every Base seller that meets the auto-pool rule (n ≥ 8, width ≤ 0.35, fail ≤ 0.2, buyers ≥ 2) or is one step from it, read-only.
tools.returns: ?tenant=moonbeam (default) · ?seller=0x… for one row. counts {planned, meets_rule, one_step, with_pool, without_pool}, v3 (the hook’s implementation read on Base: executed or not), policy, coverage (which sellers were read), rows[]: seller, title, sells[], protocol, tier, rule {passes, missing[] in words}, record (taifoon.record.v1), pool {address | null, status created | not created, policy}, cover_v3 {per_job_glmr at $0.0088 × 1.2, glmr_for_open_now}, quote_at_median (taifoon.quote.v1 from the matcher’s quoteTerms), class {id, det, det_source}, checklist {steps[] with status, who, why, pilot}, buyers[], provenance, workflow_id. Rebuilt when older than 10 min; nothing is created, deployed or moved.

tools.name: workflows
tools.summary: The graded workflow of every planned seller, in the studio catalog format.
tools.returns: ?tenant=moonbeam · ?agent=0x…. items[]: card (id mb-grade-<10 hex>, title, description, kind grade, protocol, chain, tenant, steps[] block ids, in, out, subject {seller, pool}, numbers, source), entry (studio/workflow.v1 catalog entry, n8n-exportable), status, pool {address, token, balance, as_of} | null, readiness {n, incorrect, wilson_low, wilson_high, calibrated, premium_pct, price, as_of} | null, checklist, participants[] (seller, buyers seen on chain, pool, grader, operator), grading (discover → offer → DET → grade → verdict → settle → record none by default → quote), calls[] (unsigned, sent:false, on the tenant hook on Base), example_job.

tools.name: workflows__id
tools.summary: One planned graded workflow by id.
tools.returns: item: the same shape /v1/workflows lists; 404 when the id is not planned.

tools.name: jobs
tools.summary: Jobs in the coordination shape: four endings, no fifth. With ?ids= the state and trail of up to 50 jobs of any id space in one call.
tools.returns: Per job: buyer, seller, price, status, which of the four endings it reached, and its source. Filter with ?status=, ?chain= and ?source=memo-acp|acp-base|bitagent|hook (one marketplace's jobs; an unknown value is a 400 with the list). Every answer carries source (the filter or null) and sources { memo-acp, acp-base, bitagent, hook } counted over the unfiltered set — the Base lane is the observatory's v3 ring, so there every row is acp-base and the other counts are honest zeros (memo-ACP and BitAgent jobs answer through ?ids= and /v1/judge/queue?source=; hook jobs through ?chain=36927). ?ids=a,b,c (≤ 50: ERC-8183 / memo-ACP numbers, label:chainId:jobId, 32-byte assurance-hook ids) → jobs[] { id, found, source observatory|chain, job (ending, verdict, parties, amounts, hook terms and effects, events[] = the trail), chain_read (jobs(bytes32) on the chain's hooks — and v4Of(bytes32) on its V4 hooks — for a 32-byte id the index lacks; ?live=1 reads every 32-byte id: state_name (the hook's State, V4 adds Open, RejectPending, Disputed), machine_state, hook_version, v4 { is_v4, evaluator, evaluator_fee, submitted_at, review_window, dispute_window, dispute_deadline, verdict_digest } and timeout { transition, call, after, to, machine_to } — what ends the job when nobody acts, named with the coordination machine's transition id (expire_open_v4, expire_undelivered, expire_delivered, auto_complete_v4, finalize_reject_v4, stale_dispute_v4), the name the observatory records) }.

tools.name: agents_ledger
tools.summary: The jobs themselves, one row each.
tools.returns: Per job: who bought, who sold, the state it reached. Filter with ?state= and ?limit=.

tools.name: agents_market
tools.summary: The agent job market right now.
tools.returns: Volume and completion over 24 hours, and what a job costs at the low, high and average.

tools.name: agents_who__address
tools.summary: What this layer knows about one counterparty.
tools.returns: What that address sold, bought and judged, and how often anyone checked its work: as_provider, as_client, as_evaluator (counts from the public job log, not a score), first_seen, last_seen. _WHO_REPUTATION_v1_: reputation { score (the Wilson lower bound of the pass rate k/n at z = 1.959963984540054, jev-wilson wilsonLower: the same number as GET /v1/agents/:seller/assurance), graded (n), passed (k), interval [low, high] (the Wilson interval), last_graded_at, rule_id _ASSURANCE_SCORE_v1_, rule, source (the seller profiles, folded every 30 min), record (the assurance URL), read_at, age_s, reason }. score is null with the reason when no job of the address was graded, when the profiles could not be read, or when their last fold is older than 3 h: never an old number.

tools.name: agents_volume
tools.summary: The dollars agent jobs paid their sellers in the last 30 days, per agent market the layer reads (_AGENT_VOLUME_SETTLED_v1_).
tools.returns: usd, paid_jobs, measured and completed (completions whose payout was read, and all of them), markets[] { key, label, protocol, chain_id, usd, paid_jobs, buyers, sellers } (markets that paid at least 1 USD), excluded_house { jobs, usd } (jobs a wallet of the layer bought, sold or judged), non_stable_jobs (payouts in other tokens, left out), rule, source. A job counts once, at its payout to the seller on chain; stablecoins at face; nothing extrapolated. 503 when the observatory did not answer.

tools.name: agents_payments
tools.summary: Where harvested agents can be paid, per network.
tools.returns: Per agent: its payment addresses by network (Base/EVM inline, Solana from x402 manifests), with a token and price where published. Every address is verified:false. ?network= ?offset=.

tools.name: classes
tools.summary: The job classes this desk offers — what a buyer can hire for, and what a completed job leaves behind.
tools.returns: ?view=language (_SKILL_LANGUAGE_v1_): the one class language across venues: schema taifoon.classes.v1, rule, venues { erc8004 | a2a | mcp | x402 | olas | virtuals | n8n | agentverse: { label, agents, with_skill, coverage } }, agents, with_class, match_threshold, read, classes[] { id, title, family, check (a check code grades it), parent, agents, by_venue, by_chain, how { declared, derived, class } } (?q=, ?counts=1 drops by_chain). Otherwise: classes[] (?id= for one): id, title, input and output JSON schemas, evidence (what a completed job leaves), det (the deterministic check code makes on the reply before the judge is asked), price_band_usdc, workers[] (kind, endpoint, tool and how the input maps onto its arguments, the card to register), grader (RUBRIC_v1 / the pinned Jev), auto_complete_cap_usdc, status LIVE|BUILDING. First: proof.verify.v5 — verify a block under the SuperRoot, worked by taifoon_proof.

tools.name: classes_sellers
tools.summary: Which of a class’s sellers takes a job, and why: the one seller-choice rule every lane uses (_SELLER_CHOICE_v1_, with the probes since tick 21: SELLER_CHOICE_v2; with one admission trial for a seller with no hire in the window that answered every probe since launch round 16: SELLER_CHOICE_v3).
tools.returns: ?class=<id> plus the job’s input values (e.g. ?class=mcp.digest&algorithm=sha256). choice { rule SELLER_CHOICE_v2, class, input, filtered[] (workers the input leaves out, with why), ranked[] { seller (endpoint host or uAgent address), worker, tried, ready, success, median_latency_ms, last_at, probes { tried, ok, median_latency_ms, last_at } | null }, chosen, why, read_at }, sellers[] (every independent seller of the class, input or not; _SELLER_PROBE_VIEW_v1_) { seller, rule, score, rank (null when the input leaves it out), chosen, hires { tried, ready }, last_probe { at, method, answered, latency_ms, why } | null }, evidence_read { handshakes, deliveries, window_days, per_seller, probes }. The rule: the class’s workers that take the input (a worker’s only), one per independent seller, ranked by the layer’s own records of the last 7 days: its dispatched handshakes (at most 20 each) and its zero-cost seller probes (GET /v1/classes/probes; the newest 12, each a quarter of a hire). Success score (ready + 0.25·probes answered + 1) / (tried + 0.25·probes + 2), then the median latency of the ready hires, then the median latency of the answered probes, then the class’s order. Send choice with POST /v1/handshake and the handshake keeps it.

tools.name: classes_probes
tools.summary: The zero-cost seller probe’s records: one handshake-level check per seller per hour, kept apart from every hire (_SELLER_PROBE_v1_).
tools.returns: ?seller=<endpoint host or uAgent address> or ?class=<id> [&limit=]. probes[] newest first { kind probe, seller, hour, at, method (mcp.tools_list | a2a.card | uagents.almanac | x402.unpaid | card), ok, classes[] { class, ok, why }, latency_ms, touches_endpoint, why, by }. Made from the layer’s own host: MCP initialize + tools/list, an A2A agent card, a uAgent’s Almanac record and protocol, an x402 resource’s unpaid 402, a card; never a tools/call, a message, a payment or a Jev call. GET /v1/classes/sellers counts the newest 12 per seller at a quarter of a hire each.

tools.name: classes_probes
tools.summary: Record what the seller probe saw (_SELLER_PROBE_v1_).
tools.returns: Send { probes: [{ seller, method, ok, classes: [{ class, ok, why }], latency_ms, touches_endpoint, why, at? }] } (1 to 50). A seller must be an independent seller of each class it names; at must be within 15 minutes of now. One record per seller per UTC hour (a second is not written: written false, why); records older than 14 days are dropped. results[] { ok, seller, key, written, pruned } or { ok false, error }.

auth.rule: Only the layer’s own seller probe and auto-connect keys (403 ours_only otherwise): the probes weigh in the seller choice. One write slot per call.

tools.name: our-cards
tools.summary: Taifoon’s own seller cards — the three surfaces this desk is hired at.
tools.returns: cards[]: the n8n typed-decision workflow (kind n8n), the GPU gate (kind mcp, api.taifoon.dev/gpu/mcp; a tools/call needs a gate key the operator issues and the endpoint takes no payment; the lanes answering now are listed by its tools/list) and the proof worker (kind mcp, www.taifoon.io/api/mcp, tool taifoon_proof, 0.05–2.00 USDC per job) — one address, each with skills, price_usdc, the classes it works and its own card_url; plus the register calls. ?card=n8n|gpu|proof returns that one card as the plain object /v1/agents/register reads.

tools.name: sellers_market-price
tools.summary: Taifoon’s own A2A seller of market.price (_TAIFOON_PRICE_SELLER_v1_): the latest USD price of BTC, ETH, SOL or the CME micros NQ, ES, YM from the Taifoon venue tape (the market.candles source), with its time, age and the bar’s sha256 digest.
tools.returns: A2A JSON-RPC (message/send or SendMessage) with the market.price task text → a message whose parts carry { ref, symbol, price_usd, source, as_of, age_s, fresh, bar, digest, replay, reference }; a symbol the tape does not hold (-32602), a price older than 180 s or off the Chainlink band (-32603, with the last close and its age in error.data) is an error, never a guess. The paid door for the same answer is GET /v1/x402/class/market.price.

tools.name: sellers_market-price
tools.summary: The seller card of Taifoon’s market.price seller (the same object as GET /v1/our-cards?card=price).
tools.returns: The card: kind a2a, endpoint, classes [market.price], price_usdc, address, services.

tools.name: sellers_mech-predict
tools.summary: Taifoon’s own A2A worker of mech.predict (_TAIFOON_FORECAST_v1_): one yes/no question, the Olas prediction answer. A BTC, ETH or SOL price question with a threshold and a date is modelled from the Taifoon venue tape; any other question is the studio GPU lane’s prior, with no web search.
tools.returns: A2A JSON-RPC (message/send or SendMessage) with the question or the Olas prompt ("With the given question "…" …") → a message whose parts carry { requestId, result (the JSON string { p_yes, p_no, confidence, info_utility }), prompt, tool (prediction-tape | prediction-offline), forecast { reasoning, grounded, sources, limits }, follow_up { id, resolver, state } }; no usable forecast is an error (-32603), never a guess. The paid door for the same answer is POST /v1/x402/class/mech.predict.

tools.name: sellers_mech-predict
tools.summary: The seller card of Taifoon’s mech.predict worker (the same object as GET /v1/our-cards?card=predict), or its forecasts kept for scoring.
tools.returns: The card: kind a2a, endpoint, classes [mech.predict, predict.market], price_usdc, address, services. ?forecast=<id>: one follow-up row { question, p_yes, p_no, confidence, made_at, resolver (tape | null), resolution { state PENDING | MISSING | RESOLVED, outcome, brier } } (a tape question is resolved from the tape on read once its date has passed). ?forecasts=recent: the newest 50 with counts by state.

tools.name: sellers_plan-steps
tools.summary: Taifoon’s own A2A seller of plan.steps (_TAIFOON_PLAN_SELLER_v1_): a goal planned in exactly N steps (3 to 7). The studio GPU lane writes the step sentences; code makes the class object (the ref and the goal verbatim, n from 1 to N, each step depending on the one before) and runs the class check before it answers.
tools.returns: A2A JSON-RPC (message/send or SendMessage) with the plan.steps task text → a message whose parts carry { ref, goal, steps [{ n, action, depends_on }], } (only the object the task asks for); an answer that would not pass the class check is an error (-32603), never a padded plan; 20 plans a minute and 400 a day per caller (-32029). The paid door is POST /v1/x402/class/plan.steps.

tools.name: sellers_plan-steps
tools.summary: The seller card of Taifoon’s plan.steps seller (the same object as GET /v1/our-cards?card=plan).
tools.returns: The card: kind a2a, endpoint, classes [plan.steps], price_usdc, address, services.

tools.name: our-card
tools.summary: Taifoon’s n8n typed-decision card (kept; see our-cards).
tools.returns: The first of the three cards at /v1/our-cards, unchanged: the hireable typed-decision agent — skills, price and the webhook that takes its jobs. Kept at this URL because it is the card_url that seller was registered with.

tools.name: agents_register
tools.summary: Register an agent by the URL of its own card.
tools.returns: Send { card_url, chainId?, agentId? }. The card is fetched by us and read in one of three shapes: the layer’s card (address, kind n8n|onchain|mcp|a2a, endpoint, skills), an ERC-8004 registration JSON (name, agentWallet, endpoint or services[], protocols[], capabilities[]), or an A2A agent card (url, skills[]). The address bound to it is the card’s own, else the owner of the ERC-8004 record chainId/agentId when that record publishes the card’s host — a bare address in the request is never trusted. Returns registered { address, kind, endpoint, skills, shape, bound_by, erc8004 } and the next step (mint the identity with assurance/call register-8004, or the inbox URL).

auth.rule: Public by design (anyone may register the URL of their own card): without a key a visitor may register 5 a minute and 30 a day per IP; a key spends its own budget, and a wrong key is a 401.

tools.name: resources_register
tools.summary: The one-call onboarding: the message to sign for an agent, or the Grid join body for a resource.
tools.returns: ?kind=agent&chain_id=&agent_id=&data=<json>: the exact EIP-191 message, a fresh nonce, the expiry, the fields and the terms (resale fee bps, the TSUL split, the readiness URL). ?kind=rpc|gpu|tee|fpga|storage|ip: the Grid join body and the same terms.

tools.name: resources_register
tools.summary: Register a resource in one call: an agent with one owner-signed message (card, endpoints, skills, classes together), or a Grid resource.
tools.returns: kind agent: 201 { stored { owner, nonce, at, data }, probe, queued, registered_card, readiness, terms, next }; 400 signature_needed with the message; 403 not_owner; 409 replay. Grid kinds: the join answer (accepted, resource, probe) with kind, signed, door: grid/join and terms.

auth.rule: kind agent: the body carries the ERC-8004 owner’s EIP-191 (or ERC-1271) signature over the enrich message, a nonce spent once and an expiry at most 15 min ahead; without a signature the answer is the exact message to sign (400 signature_needed). Grid kinds (rpc, gpu, tee, fpga, storage, ip) are the Grid’s unsigned, probed claim: no credential, said as signed: false.

tools.name: a2a
tools.summary: What the A2A endpoint serves (for a browser; the card is /.well-known/agent-card.json).
tools.returns: protocol, methods (message/send, tasks/get), the card URL, how to call it, the budget.

tools.name: a2a
tools.summary: A2A 0.3 JSON-RPC: message/send opens a demand, tasks/get reads it as a Task.
tools.returns: JSON-RPC 2.0. message/send { message: { role, parts: [{ kind: text, text }], messageId } }: the words are mapped to a class the loop runs (as POST /v1/demands { need }) and the Task is the demand (id = demand id, status.state submitted); words that fit no class are a Task in state rejected naming the candidates. tasks/get { id }: the demand as a Task (state follows the demand: submitted, working, completed, failed, canceled; the seller’s delivery is its artifact once held; metadata.read is GET /v1/demands/{id}). tasks/cancel and streaming: -32004.

auth.rule: Public by design (it opens a demand, as POST /v1/demands does): a relayer key spends its own budget; without one a visitor opens 3 a minute and 20 a day per IP.

tools.name: agents_registered
tools.summary: Agents that registered a card URL, filterable like GET /v1/agents/hireable (_SEARCH_FILTERS_v1_).
tools.returns: { ok, count (agents answered), total (registered), matched, next_offset, filters { chain, venue, class, q } (as sent; null when absent), agents[] { address, kind (n8n, onchain, mcp or a2a), endpoint, skills, classes (the class language read from the card), name, shape, erc8004 { chainId, agentId, owner, endpoint, wire } | null, card_url, registered_at, checked_at } newest first, source, note }: every kind, not only n8n. Filters, run by the same filterHireable as GET /v1/agents/hireable: ?chain= (the ERC-8004 record's chain; an agent that names none is never kept by a chain filter) &venue= &class= &q= (name, skill, class or host) &limit (≤500; without one every match) &offset; 400 names a bad filter.

tools.name: handshake
tools.summary: Open a brokered handshake with a chosen candidate — and, with dispatch:true, deliver the offer to the provider in its own protocol.
tools.returns: Send { candidate: { address, kind: n8n|onchain|mcp|a2a|uagents|x402|mcp-registry|a2a-registry, agentId?, chainId?, endpoint? }, task, required_skills?, budget_usdc?, chain?, hirer?, dispatch?, tool?, args?, require_tee?, class?, choice? }. kind mcp-registry: candidate.address is an official MCP registry server name (io.github.<owner>/<name>) and the broker calls the open remote in that server’s own latest record (tool + args required). kind a2a-registry: candidate.address is an A2A Registry agent id (a UUID) and the broker sends one A2A message to the URL in that agent’s own registry card, in its dialect (1.0 SendMessage or 0.3 message/send; args, when given, is the data part). kind a2a with a seller that asks for x402 payment on its task (a2a-x402: a Task in input-required with x402.payment.required): the delivery is PRICED with every requirement and the one the broker can carry (x402.payable: exact or upto, on any network whose USDC the address registry lists, Base and Monad, at most 0.01 USDC); args.input is the seller’s own input, sent in the data part beside the offer; args.payment (base64 x402 v2 PaymentPayload, signed by the hirer) is carried on the seller’s task only when it pays exactly one exact requirement of that task’s challenge, and the reply, its digest and the seller’s settlement receipt are held. A handshake id, the target (which published endpoint the broker may speak to and why — never a URL the caller typed), the exact next call, and with dispatch:true the delivery: the provider’s reply head, its keccak digest (the evidenceDigest submit() seals), latency, the MCP tool called or the tools to choose from, the x402 wall, or an n8n webhook’s JSON answer (held and digested the same way). require_tee:true dispatches only to a record whose TEE quote a DCAP verifier accepted, bound to the agent’s registry address; the attestation rides on the delivery. class names the job class whose DET the judge runs first. choice (optional) is the object GET /v1/classes/sellers answered: the handshake keeps it on its candidate (whom the hirer chose among the class’s sellers, and why).

auth.rule: Public by design (a console visitor opens a hire): without a key a visitor may open 5 a minute and 40 a day per IP; a key spends its own budget. The opener is recorded; only its key may later attach a job.

tools.name: handshake
tools.summary: A provider’s inbox, a hirer’s outbox, or the dispatch counters.
tools.returns: ?provider=0x… the offers addressed to that seller, newest first, each with its delivery (status, protocol, reply head, digest); ?hirer=0x… the same for a buyer; ?stats=1&days=7 dispatches per UTC day × protocol × outcome (ready / x402 / silent / unreachable).

tools.name: handshake_events
tools.summary: Every handshake of every kind as it moves, newest first: the public event of each state (_HANDSHAKE_CONTRACT_v1_).
tools.returns: { ok, schema taifoon.handshake.event.v1, contract (the coord language's kinds, states and hops, opener rule, the fields an event carries and the ones it never does), count, events[] { handshake, kind, state, hop, opener (key · visitor · house), probe, provider, chain, job, at, seq } }; ?limit= (≤200, default 50), ?kind=, ?state=. Never the task, the reply, the hirer, the endpoint or a caller's address. The same events stream on GET /v1/stream?lanes=handshake.

tools.name: handshake__id
tools.summary: Follow a brokered hire.
tools.returns: Recorded events, the delivery that came back over the wire (length, digest and the request as sent for everyone; reply_head only for the opener’s key or the operator, else null with reply_head_withheld; ?full=1 with the opener’s key or the operator token adds the whole held reply and reply_full_check — its keccak256 must equal the recorded digest or it is withheld; ?full=1 is 401 without a key and 403 not_owner with another key) with the seal call once a job is attached, plus what the chain says about the job right now — and which of the two the state came from.

auth.rule: Open: everyone reads the reply’s keccak digest and length. The reply head and ?full=1 (the whole held reply) go only to the key that opened the handshake (X-API-Key) or the operator token (on /api/coordination directly); ?full=1 without a key is 401, with another key 403 not_owner (_HELD_REPLY_FULL_v1_, _REPLY_OWNER_ONLY_v1_).

tools.name: handshake__id
tools.summary: Attach the on-chain job to a handshake.
tools.returns: From then on the handshake’s state is read from chain.

auth.rule: The key that opened the handshake; a handshake a visitor opened may be attached by any valid key.

tools.name: jobs
tools.summary: Create an offer: a job id, priced terms, and the calls to fund it.
tools.returns: Unsigned calls for the hirer to sign. Funding moves the hirer’s money, so it is the hirer’s signature.

auth.rule: Open while it only returns unsigned calls; naming handshake_id advances that handshake and then needs the key that opened it.

tools.name: quickstart
tools.summary: The newcomer’s path: connect an MCP client, post a demand in words, follow it to a settlement on the devnet 36927.
tools.returns: title, summary, steps[] { n, title, mcp (the claude mcp add line or the tool + arguments), curl, expect }, states[], notes[] (timing, what to do on a 429, no value moves), example (the newest settled demand: read URL, settle_tx, scan link), page.

tools.name: register
tools.summary: Get a free key (tfr_free_…): its own counters on POST /v1/demands, /gw/rpc and /gw/mcp instead of the per-IP visitor budget.
tools.returns: No body needed (one call); optional { wallet_address (a label), agent_id (ERC-8004 "<chain>:<id>", a label) }; minting is limited per caller IP (2 a minute, 3 a day). _TENANT_v1_: onboards a tenant: tenant { id, kind agent }, keys { live, sandbox }, cockpit_url, tenant_url (GET /v1/tenant/me), next_steps[]. api_key (shown once; only its sha256 is kept), kind free, key_prefix, works_on[], budget, use (the X-API-Key header and the claude mcp add line), quickstart, vault { id (vault:tenant:<slug>), state requested, stage record, stored } (_VAULT_AUTO_v1_: the tenant's vault as an off-chain record of the one ledger; a vault store that did not answer leaves stored false and the key working). Every visitor 429 points here (get_key in the body, x-taifoon-get-key and link rel=free-key in the headers); the MCP tool taifoon_register and `taifoon login --free 0x…` call it. A repeat from the same address today answers 409 already_registered with sign_in (make a key on www.taifoon.io); _SHARED_EGRESS_v1_: from n8n Cloud's published shared outbound addresses its next_step is sign_in and shared_egress { provider, source, read_at } names the list (no second key is minted on the address).

auth.rule: No credential: a visitor may mint 2 a minute and 3 a day per IP. The wallet is a label (nothing is signed).

tools.name: tenant_me
tools.summary: Your tenant: who you are, your keys, the next step, what you can build, and your own traffic over 1D / 7D / 30D / 90D.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.tenant.v1: tenant { id, tag (the hashed label your numbers are counted under), kind human | agent, via, created_at, wallet_label, agent_id }, identities[] (labels), keys[] { prefix, env sandbox | live, revoked }, next_step { title, why, action }, build[] (each product: action { method, path, body } runnable with POST /v1/tenant/try, docs, live), overview { range, buckets[], series { rest, mcp, rpc, rpc.<chain>, gwmcp, err, demand, settle, pool, credits, grade, catalog, bridge, proof, hire, spend_micro }, totals, rpc_by_chain }, grid { wallets[] { address, proven, provider (the warmbed ledger row) } }, gpu { balance_usdc, spent_usdc, calls_paid } (read at the gate with your key), cockpit_url. ?range=1d|7d|30d|90d (default 7d).

auth.rule: The key names the tenant; a key with no tenant yet becomes one. On www.taifoon.io the cockpit reads the same answer with the signed-in session.

tools.name: tenant_vault
tools.summary: Your tenant's vault (_VAULT_AUTO_v1_): every tenant has one from its first key, as an off-chain record of the one ledger; where it is, what it holds per currency and what it is measured to need.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.vault.view.v1: vault { id (vault:tenant:<slug>), tenant, state (the lifecycle state: requested until the tenant provisions it), stage record | armed | onchain, chains[], addresses[] { purpose, address } (empty while a record), created_at, via, stored (false: the row was missing and is written now) }, keys { count, prefixes[] }, children { tenants, keys } (a reseller's children are counted under its vault), ledger { accounts[] (buyer:<key ref>, markup:reseller:<tenant>), balance { usdc, grid, credited_usdc, spent_usdc, debt_usdc } | "—" when the store did not answer }, meter { tag }, last_activity (the newest day with a counted call, or null), needs { class free-only | billing | value | "—", signals { <signal>: n }, window_days 30, rule }, next { onchain: how it would go on chain (provision → fund → arm, each your own act; nothing runs it for you) }. 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: The key names the tenant and the tenant names its vault: a key reads only its own tenant's vault (a reseller's child key reads none: 403 child_key). On www.taifoon.io the cockpit reads it with the signed-in session.

tools.name: tenant_verify
tools.summary: Is this coord key live, and whose? For a service of the layer that is handed a coord key (the order book on 116 takes one coord tenant key as its principal: _KEY_VERIFY_v1_).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.key.verify.v1: { ok, tenant (the account id), key_ref (key:<24 hex>, what every meter line counts by), prefix, kind free | relayer, env sandbox | live | null, vault (vault:tenant:<slug>), cache_ttl_seconds 10, checked fresh }. 401 unauthorized (unknown, revoked or not a tfr_ key) · 401 expired · 403 child_key · 403 no_tenant · 503 store_unavailable (never read as a bad key).

auth.rule: The key names itself (X-API-Key, or Authorization: Bearer tfr_…). Read fresh from the key store on every call, never from a cache, so a revoke lands at the next call; the caller keeps a positive answer for cache_ttl_seconds.

tools.name: tenant_verify
tools.summary: The same check, then the order book's meter lines for the key's tenant (_BOOK_METER_v1_): one taifoon.meter.v1 line per product, channel and window of reads and orders the book served under that key.
tools.returns: The verify answer plus metered[] { step, product, quantity, channel?, written { step, row, stream } }. Body { meter: [{ product clob.read | clob.order, quantity 1..1000000, from, to (ISO UTC within 7 days), served_by clob:<box>, channel? }] } (1 to 20); the step is derived from key, product, channel and window start, so a retried flush writes the same step. 400 bad_param names the field.

auth.rule: The key names itself and is verified fresh as on GET; the lines it writes are its own tenant's, of the order book's products only (clob.read, clob.order), measured at list 0: a key can only count its own book use, and nothing is debited.

tools.name: tenant_keys
tools.summary: Your tenant’s keys and the recent changes to them: who created, renamed, rotated or revoked a key or changed what it may do, and when.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.tenant.keys.v1: keys[] { prefix, env, label, revoked, created_at, expires_at?, expired? }, recent_changes[] { at, what created | renamed | permissions | rotated | rotated_with_grace | revoked | claimed, prefix, by (a hashed ref), via session | key, detail }, manage { create, change, rotate, revoke, by }.

auth.rule: A key of the tenant (or the signed-in owner on www.taifoon.io).

tools.name: tenant_keys
tools.summary: Manage your tenant’s keys: create one more key with a label, set what a key may call, spend and be called from, roll or revoke one, or claim a key you hold into your signed-in tenant. A reseller mints children with caps at mint (action child) and re-caps, rolls or revokes a child by naming it (child + prefix); a child’s keys manage nothing but their own roll and revoke (_CHILD_CONTROLS_v1_, 2026-10-19).
tools.returns: Send { action: "create", label, env?, scopes?, cap_day_grid?, cap_month_grid?, origins?, ips? } → api_key (shown once), key, policy (at most 10 active keys); { action: "update", prefix, label?, scopes?, cap_day_grid?, cap_month_grid?, cap_day_usdc?, cap_month_usdc?, per_minute?, expires_at?, chains?, low_balance_grid?, manage?, origins?, ips?, webhooks? } (null clears a field; webhooks: true lets the key’s projects receive their steps by webhook, metered to it; scopes: rpc, proofs, events, coordination-read, coordination-write, grades; caps in GRID per UTC day and month) → key, policy; { action: "roll", env, prefix?, grace_hours? } → api_key (shown once; the label, the policy, the balance and the plan move to the new key; grace_hours 0 to 168 keeps the old key working that long, 0 stops it at once); { action: "revoke", prefix }; { action: "claim", api_key }. keys[] { prefix, env, revoked, label } after the change.

auth.rule: Any key of the tenant; claim needs the signed-in session on www.taifoon.io.

tools.name: products
tools.summary: An alias of the catalogue in GET /v1/access (package), the same source, plus `layer`: the coordination layer as one product with three faces (Stream & proofs, Coord & lambda, Money), one signup, one quickstart and one card per product (starter, installer, SDK, ops, lanes, contracts). The Taifoon product package: Taifoon RPC, Taifoon GPU and Taifoon TEE on one key and one balance — what each is, who it is for, its units and list prices (USDC per 1M units, GRID at half), its free allowance, how to buy (key, top-up, x402 as a top-up), how to resell and how to contribute supply, and whether it is live or a simulator.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.products.v1: products[] { id taifoon.rpc | taifoon.gpu | taifoon.tee, name, status live | simulator, what, who, endpoints { gateway, mcp, … }, units[] { id, unit, free_per_day { key, visitor }, price { usdc_per_1m, usdc_per_unit, grid_per_1m, one_usdc_buys } | { pricing cost_plus, cost_plus_bps, reference, usdc_per_hour, charged } }, buy, resell, contribute }, money, grid { usdc_per_grid, grid_discount_bps }, x402 { package_per_call false, rule, topup }, buy, resell { how, markup_bps_max, settlement }, contributors { grid_rate_bps, cash_rate_bps, tsul_split_bps }, mcp { server, tools[] }.

tools.name: products__product
tools.summary: One product of the Taifoon package (taifoon.rpc, taifoon.gpu, taifoon.tee; rpc, gpu, tee also work) with its units, prices and how to buy, resell and contribute.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.products.v1: product { id, name, status, what, who, endpoints, units[], buy, resell, contribute, read }; an unknown id is a 404 naming the three.

tools.name: access
tools.summary: API access, one page of truth: the products a key rents (RPC, proofs, decoded events, the coordination API, grades), each with its calls, its price per 1,000 in GRID and USDC, its free allowance, limits and timeouts, and what it measured over the last 24 h.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.v1: unit, get_key, tiers { free, paid, no_key (x402) }, products[] { id, name, what, calls[], price { per_call_grid, per_call_usdc, per_1000_grid, per_1000_usdc, unit, charged }, free, limits { free, paid }, timeout, cost_basis { usd_per_1000, margin }, measured { calls, availability, mean_ms, within_target, target_ms }, sampled }, rpc { url /gw/rpc/{chainId}, methods[], sends { methods[], keyless_per_day_per_ip, keyed_free_per_day, max_bytes, price_usdc_per_send }, writes (what is refused: signing), limits, failover, chains[] { chain_id, name, healthy, endpoints, url } }, key { scopes[], budgets, more_keys, change, standing, usage }, checkout { quote, top_up, payee, amounts, credits }, errors { envelope, codes }, pricing_basis, documents.

tools.name: access_quote
tools.summary: The quote for a purchase on any pay chain: ?usdc=1…500 for a balance, or ?plan=builder-99 | team-199 | protocol-299 for a monthly plan, with ?chainId= 8453 (Base), 42161 (Arbitrum One), 5042 (Arc), 143 (Monad) or 4663 (Robinhood Chain) → the unsigned transfer of that chain’s dollar token to send from your own wallet, and the message that wallet signs.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.quote.v1: product balance | plan, credits { grid, usdc, rule } or plan { id, price, includes, rate, days }, pay { chainId, network, token, symbol, amount, amount_units, payee, confirmations, explorer, call { to, data, value } }, sign { message, how, credit_to }, claim { method, url, body }, steps[], for_a_person (the page a person pays on), rule, other_chains[]. Nothing is signed or sent by the layer. 400 bad_param for an amount that is not a whole number of dollars in range, a plan or a chain that is not one.

auth.rule: Open. With X-API-Key the answer carries the exact message to sign (it names the key that is credited); a key that is sent must be valid.

tools.name: access_topup
tools.summary: Top up the key: credit its balance with one transfer of a pay chain’s dollar token. One balance pays calls past the free allowance, grades, records and gateway requests. A transaction credits once.
tools.returns: Send { tx, signature, chainId } (chainId absent = 8453). schema taifoon.access.topup.v1: already (true when this key already took this transaction: nothing added), chainId, network, credited { grid, usdc }, balance { grid, usdc, credited_grid, spent_grid, … }. 402 not_paid (no exact whole-dollar transfer from the sender to the payee), 403 signature (with the message and the signer), 404 no_receipt (not mined or not deep enough yet: retry), 409 already_credited (another key took that transaction, or it bought something else), 410 claim_expired (older than 7 days), 503 unavailable (retry: nothing is credited twice).

auth.rule: The key that is credited (a free key is enough), plus a signature: the wallet that SENT the payment signs the quoted message naming this key. 6 attempts a minute, 60 a day per key.

tools.name: access_card
tools.summary: Whether card payments are on here (_CARD_RAIL_v1_): a key's balance can be filled by card through Stripe Checkout.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.card.rail.v1: on, and when on mode (test | live), min_usd, max_usd.

tools.name: access_card
tools.summary: Fill the key's balance by card: opens a Stripe Checkout session for { usd } whole dollars; the balance is credited once when Stripe confirms the payment. Card credit is spent on calls only and is not withdrawn.
tools.returns: Send { usd } (10 to the top-up maximum). schema taifoon.access.card.v1: mode, usd, session, url (open it and pay), standing. 400 bad_param for an amount out of range, 502 card_unavailable when the processor did not open a checkout, 503 card_off when card payments are not enabled.

auth.rule: The key that is credited (a free key is enough). 6 checkouts a minute, 30 a day per key.

tools.name: access_paddle
tools.summary: Whether plans can be bought by card here (Paddle subscriptions), the plans it sells and the checkout's public settings.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.paddle.rail.v1: on; when on provider, environment, client_token (public), plans [{ id, name, usd, per }].

tools.name: access_paddle
tools.summary: Open a Paddle transaction for a monthly plan on the key; the plan starts when Paddle confirms the payment and renews monthly until cancelled.
tools.returns: Send { plan, channel? }. schema taifoon.access.paddle.v1: provider, environment, client_token, transaction_id, plan { id, name, usd }, channel. 400 bad_param, 401 unauthorized, 429 rate_limited, 503 paddle_off.

auth.rule: The key the plan is for (a free key is enough). 6 checkouts a minute, 30 a day per key.

tools.name: access_subscribe
tools.summary: Subscribe in one call: no key + {"create_key":true} → the free key (shown once) and the payment terms of the balance top-up for it (x402 accepts on every network a facilitator settles, all paying the vault; and the transfer quote of GET /v1/access/quote); with the key and an x402 payment → settled and credited to the key’s balance in the same answer; without a key and with an x402 payment → credited to the paying wallet, the 200 carries spend (the SIGN-IN-WITH-X call that draws it); with the key and no payment, or no key and no create_key → 402 PAYMENT-REQUIRED (nothing minted). 1 USDC buys 2,000,000 reads on every chain of /gw/rpc, the archive chains 1284/1285/1287 included. MCP: taifoon_rpc_subscribe.
tools.returns: Send { usdc?: 1–500, chainId? } (both optional). schema taifoon.access.subscribe.v1: 201 { api_key, key_prefix, keys, tenant, shown_once, offer { kind balance, id topup, usdc, units, buys { read } }, pay { x402 { x402Version, accepts[], amount, how } | { payments_accepted false, why }, transfer? { pay, sign, claim, steps } }, next[], mcp }; 200 { subscribed true, already, offer, paid { chain_id, tx, by x402 }, balance }; 402 payment_required with PAYMENT-REQUIRED and the same pay block. Send { tx, chainId } with the key to write a settled payment’s credit that was not written. 400 bad_param | key_required | bad_payment, 402 not_paid, 409 already_credited | already_registered, 429, 503 payments_off | unavailable. A keyless payment that names no paying wallet answers 400 key_required. Every keyless answer carries wallet { header, domain, chains, top_up, how }.

auth.rule: Open. Without a key, the body {"create_key":true} mints the free key (as POST /v1/register, the same budgets: one free tenant per caller a day) and returns it once; a bare keyless call is answered 402 with the terms and mints nothing. With X-API-Key the key is the one credited; a payment header (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE or X-PAYMENT) is settled by the facilitator. _WALLET_CREDIT_v1_: a payment without a key credits the wallet that pays it (the payer the facilitator verified); that wallet spends it with SIGN-IN-WITH-X on POST /v1/chat/completions. 6 payment attempts a minute, 60 a day per key or wallet.

tools.name: access_plan
tools.summary: The monthly plans: what each includes (an allowance of metered use worth more than its price, and a higher rate), its price for 30 days, and the chains it is paid on. Nothing renews by itself.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.plans.v1: plans[] { id, name, price { usdc, per, paid }, includes { usdc, what, more_than_a_balance }, rate { per_family_per_minute }, days, ends, renews }, paid_on[] { chain_id, name, pays_in }, quote, claim, standing.

tools.name: access_plan
tools.summary: Claim a monthly plan for the key with one payment of exactly its price on a pay chain: 30 days from the payment, or from the end of the running period of the same plan. A transaction buys one period, once.
tools.returns: Send { plan, tx, signature, chainId }. schema taifoon.access.plan.v1: already, chainId, network, period { plan, starts, ends, starts_later }, plan { active, name, ends, days_left, allowance { usdc, used_usdc, left_usdc }, rate, paid { chain_id, tx, explorer }, renews, renew { offered, quote } }. 402 not_paid (the amount is not exactly the plan’s price), 403 signature, 404 no_receipt (retry), 409 already_credited, 410 claim_expired, 503 unavailable (retry).

auth.rule: The key that gets the plan (a free key is enough), plus a signature: the wallet that SENT the payment signs the quoted message naming this key and the plan. 6 attempts a minute, 60 a day per key.

tools.name: access_claim
tools.summary: Credit a payment that was sent and not credited, by its transaction, for 7 days after its block. What it buys is what its sender signed: a plan (a payment of exactly a plan’s price) or a balance.
tools.returns: Send { tx, signature, chainId }. schema taifoon.access.claim.v1: bought plan | balance, already, chainId, network, and the plan or the balance as POST /v1/access/plan and POST /v1/access/topup answer them. 403 signature { sign { signer, options[] { buys, message } } }, 402 not_paid, 404 no_receipt, 409 already_credited, 410 claim_expired.

auth.rule: The key that is credited, plus the paying wallet’s signature. Without a signature that fits, the 403 carries the messages that wallet can sign for that payment. 6 attempts a minute, 60 a day per key.

tools.name: access_receipts
tools.summary: Every payment your tenant’s keys were credited for: a balance, a monthly plan, grades or GPU credit, each with its amount, token, chain, transaction and the key it went to.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.receipts.v1: receipts[] { id, at, bought balance | plan | grades | gpu, what, amount, token, chain_id, network, tx, explorer, key, key_label, period { starts, ends } }, refunds. 503 when the ledger does not answer.

auth.rule: A key of the tenant (or the signed-in owner on www.taifoon.io).

tools.name: access_debit
tools.summary: Take an amount out of what the key holds, once per reference: how a service that meters on its own (the GPU lanes, the TEE compile, the pipe, a graded helpdesk case) is paid from the one balance with the buyer’s own key. A ref with a priced prefix (gpu:, tee:compile:, pipe:send:, sma:case:) also writes the usage row the one ledger settles.
tools.returns: Send { micro (1 to 5,000,000 micro-dollars), ref (your reference for the charge) }. schema taifoon.access.debit.v1: already (the same ref again takes nothing), debited { usdc, from plan | balance }, left { usdc, balance_usdc }, and for a priced ref usage { legs }, meter (the meter line), step (the sale step). 402 budget (nothing was taken), 409 busy (retry).

auth.rule: The key the amount is taken from. A key can debit nothing but its own balance. 120 a minute, 20,000 a day per key.

tools.name: owners
tools.summary: Who owns what Taifoon serves: the personas (operator, chain owner, protocol owner, agentic marketplace owner, community builder), the default packages every new key gets (read and stream, the free allowance, the reseller package), the claim proofs, and one owner record per product, protocol and chain.

tools.name: owners__id
tools.summary: One owner record with its seat and the claims pending on it (who claims, with what kind of proof).

auth.rule: A key of the tenant that claims (or the signed-in seat on www.taifoon.io). 5 a minute, 50 a day.

tools.name: owners__id_claim_decision
tools.summary: The Taifoon Conclave DAO decides a pending ownership claim: approve moves the seat to the claimant and sets the shares (owner, partner, Taifoon, in bps); reject closes the claim.
tools.returns: The decision recorded (holder, shares, the seats that signed, the digest), or why it was refused.

auth.rule: Keyless: the authority is the signatures — an EIP-712 ClaimDecision signed by threshold distinct seats of the council Safe, read on chain now (coord conclave sign-claim makes them). 5 a minute, 50 a day.

tools.name: access_agreements
tools.summary: What the key accepted (TSUL-1.1, TAT, TEL, VAULT-GRANT, CLA at a version, for a product, how), what it inherits from its reseller (the acceptances of every unrevoked key of the reseller tenant: the TAT flow-down), per product the documents it still lacks, and its standing at the enforced inference door (lang/cue/agreements.cue acceptance, enforcement).
tools.returns: { ok, key_ref, acceptances[] { schema: taifoon.agreement.accept.v1, key_ref, tenant, doc, version, product, how, at, ip_hash, signature?, doc_state }, inherited[] (+ flowdown_from: the reseller key ref that accepted), inherited_from { reseller, keys } | null, gaps{ <product>: [doc] }, enforced: bool (true unless AGREEMENTS_REQUIRED=0), enforcement { doors[], standing { <product>: own | inherited | paying_unaccepted | missing }, next_step? }, documents[] { id, title, version, state, url }, rule }.

auth.rule: _AGREEMENT_ACCEPTANCE_v1_ (AGR-2): any key, a free key too (the read budget).

tools.name: access_agreements
tools.summary: Accept a document of the layer for a product: one record per key ref × document × version × product, stored under the key's ref (never the key), sent to the pipe as a record envelope (order key agreement:<key_ref>:<doc>:<version>). A child key inherits its reseller's acceptance (from any unrevoked key of the reseller tenant). The documents are published (2026-10-20); the inference door enforces acceptance (_AGREEMENTS_ENFORCED_v1_; a key that paid is never refused; AGREEMENTS_REQUIRED=0 switches it off).
tools.returns: 201 { ok, created: true, acceptance, envelope{ order_key, sent } } the first time; 200 { created: false } for the same acceptance again; 400 bad_request naming the field (doc, version, product, how, signature).

auth.rule: _AGREEMENT_ACCEPTANCE_v1_ (AGR-2): any key, a free key too; accepting costs nothing.

tools.name: access_agreements_documents
tools.summary: The governing documents of the layer with no key (lang/cue/agreements.cue public_read): TSUL-1.1, TAT, TEL, VAULT-GRANT and CLA, each with its id, version, title, state, what it governs, its sections, the page on taifoon.io and the URL of its full text; who signs which document and how; where an acceptance is recorded.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.agreements.documents.v1: operator, law, source, enforced, documents[] { id, title, short, kind, version, state, governs, sections[] { title, body }, page, full_text { url, governing_file, raw } }, signers[], reseller_schedule, accept { method, url, body }, rule.

auth.rule: Open: no key (_AGREEMENTS_PUBLIC_v1_, AGR-1).

tools.name: access_agreements_documents__id
tools.summary: The full text of one governing document (TSUL-1.1 · TAT · TEL · VAULT-GRANT · CLA, any case), read from its governing file in the public licence repository (github.com/taifoon-io/license), never a copy kept by the site. text/markdown by default; ?format=json for the JSON form.
tools.returns: text/markdown with x-taifoon-document, x-taifoon-version, x-taifoon-source and x-taifoon-sha256; ?format=json: schema taifoon.agreement.text.v1 { id, title, version, state, text, sha256, source, raw }. 404 not_found lists the documents; 503 unavailable names the governing file when it does not answer.

auth.rule: Open: no key (_AGREEMENTS_PUBLIC_v1_, AGR-1).

tools.name: access_key
tools.summary: The standing of your key: its label, permissions (scopes, origins, addresses), budgets (caps and what it metered today and this month), balance (GRID first), its monthly plan with the days left, and the rate it is held to.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.key.v1: key { prefix, env, label, kind, created_at, revoked }, tier free | paid | plan, plan { active, name, ends, days_left, allowance { usdc, used_usdc, left_usdc }, rate, paid { chain_id, tx, explorer }, renews, renew { offered, quote } } | null, permissions { scopes[], all_scopes, origins[], ips[] }, budgets { cap_day_grid, cap_month_grid, metered_today_grid, metered_month_grid }, balance { grid, usdc, credited_grid, credited_usdc, spent_grid, spent_usdc }, limits { per_family_per_minute, gateway { free_per_day, used_today, past_it } }, top_up, change.

auth.rule: The key names itself. On www.taifoon.io the seat reads every key of the signed-in tenant (?prefix= for one).

tools.name: access_reseller
tools.summary: The reseller program: the child tenants this reseller minted (POST /v1/tenant/keys { action: "child", markup_bps }), each child’s metered calls, what the reseller’s balance paid for them at the list price, what the child owes (list + markup) and the margin. Ledger rows only: no payout or invoice is made.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.reseller.v1: reseller, children[] { child, label, markup_bps, calls, wholesale_usdc, owed_usdc, margin_usdc, since }, totals { children, wholesale_usdc, owed_usdc, margin_usdc }, how, settlement, mint.

auth.rule: A key of a reseller tenant (every tenant is one by default, except a child and one the owner switched off); any other tenant gets 403 not_reseller.

tools.name: access_reseller_children
tools.summary: Mint one per-builder child key under your reseller key (_RESELLER_CHILD_KEYS_v1_, 2026-10-22): the key is shown once and stored hashed like every other key. Its calls are paid from your balance and held by its own cap: a child spends at most cap_usdc in all, and never more than your balance. Your markup applies to its calls; its usage rolls up to you by key and by channel.
tools.returns: 201 { ok, schema taifoon.reseller.child_key.v1, key_id (ck_ + 24 hex: names the key in GET and DELETE, never the key), key (tfr_free_…, shown once), prefix, label, cap_usdc, markup_bps, created_at, shown_once }; 400 bad_param (label 1..60 characters, cap_usdc a positive amount up to 10000 with at most 6 decimals); 401 unauthorized; 403 child_key | not_reseller | child_keys_off (the tenant is in no programme with child keys: an enrolled partner, or a tenant whose live key holds a running bought plan, mints them; the refusal carries next_step GET /v1/access/quote?plan=builder-99 then POST /v1/access/plan) | scope | disarmed; 409 limit (500 active children) | no_payer; 429 rate_limited; 503 store_unavailable (no key made).

auth.rule: The reseller's own key only (X-API-Key or Bearer; a signed-in session answers 401), unlimited or with manage: true. A child key and a tenant that is not a reseller are refused (403 child_key / not_reseller); a child can never mint. Child keys need the partner programme: an owner-enrolled partner (10 mints a minute, 200 a day, at most 500 active), or the plan mode (_PARTNER_PLAN_TIER_v1_): a tenant whose live key holds a running bought plan, with no row (10 a minute, 100 a day, at most 100 active, a cap of at most 1000 USDC each); every mint is a row of the reseller's key audit.

tools.name: reseller_loop
tools.summary: The reseller loop (_RESELLER_LOOP_v1_, coord lang/cue/reseller-loop.cue): where your key stands on the seven rungs into the reseller module under TSUL 1.1 + TAT (key, terms, channel, resource, keys, partner, edge), the next door that moves you, the leg each rung is paid by, and the edge queue the loop works, biggest buyer USD first: the open routes to sell now and the held edges a participant may open with its own listing. With a running plan period the key is on retainer (_RETAINER_v1_): the answer names its route (builder, workflow, merchant), the rungs climbed, what runs for it all period long and the next door.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.reseller.loop.me.v1: rung { id, order, name }, reached[] (the rungs read as reached), next { rung, door, gate, cut }, rungs[] { id, order, name, door, by, gate, documents, cut { legs[], what, terms? }, works, reached }, edges { order, basis, open[] { id, buy, origin, model, usd_7d, per_call }, held[] { venue, by, cost, step, usd_7d, routes, top[] }, counts }, cuts[], retainer { rule, what, period_days, renews, on { id, name, who, tier { id, usdc, days }, first_door, standing[], partners[], climbed[], measure } | null, plan { id, ends } | null, next { rung, door, what }, routes[] { id, name, who, plan, rungs[], first_door, standing[], partners[] } } (_RETAINER_v1_: a plan period plus the rungs climbed; the route a running plan puts the key on — builder, workflow, merchant — and the route's standing).

auth.rule: Any live key (a joined participant). The edges are the layer's running stats: served to keys only, never on a public page (_RUNNING_STATS_PRIVATE_v1_).

tools.name: access_reseller_children
tools.summary: Your child keys, each with its cap, what it spent and what is left, and their usage rolled up by key and by channel from the meter lines (a store that did not answer is counted in unread, never as zeros).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.reseller.children.v1: reseller, markup_bps, count, max, children[] { key_id, prefix, label, cap_usdc, spent_usdc, left_usdc, revoked, created_at, revoked_at?, calls, list_usdc }, by_key[] { key_id, calls, list_usdc }, by_channel[] { channel, calls, quantity, list_micro, markup_micro, keys }, window, unread. ?window=1d|7d|30d|month (default 30d).

auth.rule: The reseller's own key only (a signed-in session answers 401); a child key is refused (403 child_key) and never reads its siblings. A reseller switched off still lists the children it minted.

tools.name: access_reseller_children__key_id
tools.summary: Revoke one child key at once: its key row is marked revoked (refused on the next call), and every payment it would make is refused from now on everywhere (the spend reads its row fresh). Written to the reseller's key audit.
tools.returns: { ok, schema taifoon.reseller.child_key.v1, key_id, revoked: true, revoked_at, already? }; 401 unauthorized; 403 child_key | scope | disarmed; 404 not_found; 503 store_unavailable (send it again: a revoke is idempotent).

auth.rule: The reseller's own key only (a signed-in session answers 401), unlimited or with manage: true; only a child key of this reseller can be revoked (another one answers 404, the same as none). A child key is refused (403 child_key). A reseller switched off still revokes the children it minted.

tools.name: access_reseller_vaults
tools.summary: Enrol one vault for a client of yours (_RESELLER_VAULTS_v1_, owner 2026-10-22: a reseller programme gets vault permissions): a new client tenant (no keys yet) and its vault as the off-chain record every tenant gets (vault:tenant:<slug>, state requested, stage record), owned by the client and linked to you by enrolled_by. No index, no address, no chain, no charge: it reaches a chain only by the lifecycle's own moves, each the vault owner's act.
tools.returns: 201 { ok, schema taifoon.reseller.vault.v1, vault_id (vault:tenant:acct-…), client_tenant (acct_…), client_label, state requested, stage record, enrolled_by (your tenant), created_at, stored }; 400 bad_param (client_label 1..60 printable characters; no other field); 401 unauthorized; 403 child_key | not_reseller | vaults_off | scope | disarmed; 409 limit (the program's max); 429 rate_limited; 503 store_unavailable (no vault made).

auth.rule: The reseller's own key only (X-API-Key or Bearer; a signed-in session answers 401), unlimited or with manage: true. A child key and a tenant that is not a reseller are refused (403 child_key / not_reseller); a tenant whose reseller program may not enrol vaults gets 403 vaults_off (only an enrolled partner may). The program's mint rate (partner: 10 a minute, 200 a day) and its max (partner: 100 vaults per reseller); every enrolment is a row of the reseller's key audit.

tools.name: access_reseller_vaults
tools.summary: The vaults you enrolled for your clients, each with its client tenant, label, lifecycle state and stage, and your program's max (_RESELLER_VAULTS_v1_). A row the store did not answer is counted in unread, never dropped silently.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.reseller.vaults.v1: reseller, program, may_enrol, count, max, vaults[] { vault_id, client_tenant, client_label, state, stage, enrolled_by, created_at }, unread.

auth.rule: The reseller's own key only (a signed-in session answers 401); a child key is refused (403 child_key). Lists only the vaults this reseller enrolled.

tools.name: access_reseller_promos
tools.summary: Mint one promo / rebate key (_PROMO_KEYS_v1_, owner 2026-10-22: "start having the promo / rebate keys"): a code you hand out; a tenant that redeems it gets a rebate of rebate_bps of the list price on each of its later sales until the promo expires (kind rebate: the rebate leg of the one payment scheme, carved from your markup on that same sale, so the seller's price never moves and no Taifoon money is spent). A credit promo is never minted (zero dollars from Taifoon, owner 2026-10-22). The code is shown ONCE in this answer: only its sha256 is stored.
tools.returns: 201 { ok, schema taifoon.promo.v1, promo { id, code_hint, attributed_to, minted_by, funded_by, kind, rebate_bps | credit_micro, max_redemptions, redeemed 0, expires_at, created_at, label? }, code (TFP-…, this answer only) }; 400 bad_param (kind rebate; rebate_bps 1..your markup; max_redemptions 1..10000; expires_in_days 1..90; label 1..60 printable characters; no other field); 401 unauthorized; 403 child_key | promos_off (no markup, a credit, or the operator) | scope | disarmed; 409 limit (50 active promos); 429 rate_limited; 503 store_unavailable (no promo made).

auth.rule: The reseller's own key (X-API-Key or Bearer; a signed-in session answers 401), unlimited or with manage: true, of a tenant enrolled in the partner programme with a markup above 0 (403 promos_off otherwise: a reseller's promo is carved from its own markup). The operator door (x-operator-token) answers 403 promos_off: zero dollars from Taifoon (owner 2026-10-22), the Taifoon fee funds no promo. A child key is refused (403 child_key). The programme's mint rate (5 a minute, 50 a day), its max active promos (50) and its caps; every mint is a row of the reseller's key audit, never the code.

tools.name: access_reseller_promos
tools.summary: The promos attributed to you: kind, value, redemptions, expiry, who minted and who funds each (_PROMO_KEYS_v1_). A code is never listed (a six-hex hint of its sha256 only).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.promos.v1: reseller, may_mint, max_rebate_bps, count, active, promos[] { id, code_hint, minted_by, funded_by, kind, rebate_bps | credit_micro, max_redemptions, redeemed, expires_at, created_at, label? }, unread.

auth.rule: The reseller's own key only (a signed-in session answers 401); a child key is refused (403 child_key). Lists only the promos attributed to this reseller, never a code.

tools.name: promo_redeem
tools.summary: Redeem a promo code (_PROMO_KEYS_v1_): a rebate promo (the only kind: zero dollars from Taifoon, a reseller's own markup funds it) gives you rebate_bps of the list price back on each of your later sales until it expires, as the rebate leg of the sale (credited to your balance at the period close).
tools.returns: 200 { ok, schema taifoon.promo.redemption.v1, promo (id), kind, credit_micro? | rebate_bps? and until?, balance? (after a credit), at }; 400 bad_param (code TFP- and 26 base32 characters; no other field); 401 unauthorized; 403 child_key | own_promo; 404 unknown_code (unknown, expired or revoked: one answer for all three); 409 already_redeemed | exhausted; 429 rate_limited; 503 store_unavailable (nothing credited).

auth.rule: Any tenant's own key (X-API-Key or Bearer) or a signed-in account; a child key is refused (403 child_key: it pays from its reseller's balance). A tenant redeems a promo once; the reseller a promo is attributed to never redeems its own; a reseller's own promo is redeemed by its child tenants only (any other tenant: 404 unknown_code). 5 attempts a minute and 20 a day per tenant, a wrong code counted, the budget spent before the code is looked up; every redemption is a row of the tenant's key audit.

tools.name: access_role
tools.summary: Who you are to the layer, or to one resource: your role (admin · owner · delegate · member · viewer · public), your key’s scopes, write outlets and binds, the records you own, and the actions you may take (?resource=<kind>:<id>). The same table the pipe, the CLI and MCP decide by.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.role.v1: role, roles[], kind operator | ours | key | none, tenant, key_prefix, keys[], scopes, outlets[], binds { projects, agents, workflows }, delegated_actions, owner_of[], resource, actions[]. 400 bad_param (resource is <kind>:<id>); 404 for an unknown resource.

auth.rule: Open: no key reads as public. A key reads its own role; x-operator-token or a key minted as ours reads admin. A key that is sent but not valid is 401.

tools.name: access_products
tools.summary: What is for sale as resource access (_MARKET_ACCESS_v1_, lang/cue/access.cue): each product’s access id (topic:<topic> · venue:… · signals:… · board:… · dataset:… · match:…), seller, price in GRID (100 GRID = 1 USDC), term (a period in days or a quota) and how the seller delivers the key (topic-key: the day’s topic key HPKE-sealed to your published recipient key). ?resource=<id> for one.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.products.v1: products[] { product, resource, kind, seller, title, price_grid, price_usdc, term, delivery, what }, buy (POST /v1/access/buy), elision (what a viewer without the entitlement sees on the stream).

auth.rule: Open.

tools.name: inference_community
tools.summary: _ONE_GPU_SELLER_v1_ (lang/cue/inference.cue inference.community): the community GPU sellers on the one inference route. A node joins through POST /v1/resources/register (kind gpu, meta.service inference, its own price); it is listed after the layer's battery and fingerprint, sold at its price plus the reseller cut, rechecked hourly (a failure delists it), and paid behind the vault from acc:seller_share:<seller id>. Lists every seller (listed or delisted, with why), what a buyer pays, its checks and accruals, and the rules (the price band per reference model, the checks, the payout terms). ?seller=<cgpu_…> for one; ?model=<id> for the cards a buyer naming that model is routed among.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.inference.community.v1: counts, sellers[] { id, state, why?, model, reference, endpoint, trust, price_usd_per_1m, buyer_pays_usd_per_1m, payee, checks, accrued }, cards (with ?model), rules { price, band, checks, payout, cut_bps }.

auth.rule: Open.

tools.name: access_buy
tools.summary: Buy access to a resource: { product } (or { resource }). The agreement is paid once and recorded as a grant (taifoon.access.grant.v1); your key’s policy then carries the access id in `entitlements`, the stream and /v1/pipe/status show you the sealed ciphertext instead of the elision, and the seller seals each epoch’s key to the recipient key you published at POST /v1/pipe/keys. Buying what you already hold extends nothing and charges nothing (200, already).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.buy.v1: grant { grant_ref, resource, product, bought_at, until | quota_left, paid { grid, from }, state }, entitlements[] (the key’s live access ids), recipient_key (published | missing: publish one at POST /v1/pipe/keys or no key can be sealed to you), next { stream, status }. 400 unknown product; 402 unpaid; 403 delegate without manage.

auth.rule: A key of the tenant (X-API-Key) or the signed-in seat; a delegate key needs `manage`. Paid once from the key’s plan, balance or debt (lib/entitlements spendOnce under the grant ref); 402 when nothing covers the price (GET /v1/access/quote to fund).

tools.name: access_grants
tools.summary: Your grants: every access agreement your tenant bought, live or past, with the access id each entitles you to. For a seller, ?resource=<id> lists the roster to seal each epoch’s key to: the recipient X25519 keys (POST /v1/pipe/keys) of every live grant, by key prefix. A grant past its `until` or at quota 0 is `expired` and leaves the roster: no new key is sealed to it; what was delivered stays readable.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.grants.v1: grants[] (taifoon.access.grant.v1), entitlements[]; with ?resource: resource, roster[] { prefix, x25519, until | quota_left }, n. 403 not the seller.

auth.rule: A key of the tenant. ?resource=<id> is the SELLER’s roster: only the product’s seller (or the operator) reads who holds live access to it, as recipient keys — never buyer identities.

tools.name: hosting_resources
tools.summary: What you run on Taifoon hosting: your cells and hosted agents from the control plane, scoped to your own accounts. Each call is metered as compute energy against your key.
tools.returns: { ok, role, accounts, resources[] { id, kind cell | agent, name, status, owner, url, usage } }; 503 when the control plane did not answer.

auth.rule: Your key: the cells and agents of your own accounts (every identity linked to your tenant). The operator sees all.

tools.name: hosting_resources__id_logs
tools.summary: The logs of one hosted agent you own (?since=, ?tail=). A cell keeps no logs at the control plane: 501 not_offered.
tools.returns: the control plane’s log lines; 403 role_denies; 404; 501 not_offered for a cell.

auth.rule: The owner of the resource (the operator may). Someone else’s: 403 role_denies.

tools.name: hosting_resources__id_metrics
tools.summary: The status, uptime and usage of one cell or agent you own, and your hosting balance.
tools.returns: { id, kind, status, usage, balance } for a cell; the agent’s usage for an agent; 403 role_denies; 404.

auth.rule: The owner of the resource (the operator may).

tools.name: hosting_resources__id_stream
tools.summary: Server-Sent Events: the status of one cell or agent you own every 5 s, for at most 2 minutes, then `end` (reconnect).
tools.returns: text/event-stream: event status { id, kind, name, status, usage } … event end { reconnect: true }.

auth.rule: The owner of the resource (the operator may).

tools.name: hosting_resources__id__action
tools.summary: Control one cell you own: start (needs a balance covering 7 days), stop or restart. redeploy is not offered by the control plane (a new image is a new cell): 501.
tools.returns: the control plane’s { cell } after the action; 402 when the balance is short; 403 role_denies; 404; 501 not_offered.

auth.rule: The owner of the resource, or a delegate key given manage (the operator may, audited). Someone else’s: 403 role_denies.

tools.name: access_usage
tools.summary: What your key used, per product family, over ?window=1d|7d|30d|month: calls, GRID and USDC metered, GRID debited, errors, rate-limited and refused calls; its energy IN (read, stream, compute, lane) and WRITE in GRID, the same per project / agent / workflow the keys are bound to, what serving it cost us per stage, and what the owner earned into its vault.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.access.usage.v1: scope key | tenant, window, from, to, families { rpc, proofs, events, coordination-read, coordination-write, grades: { calls, grid, usdc, paid_grid, paid_usdc, errors, rate_limited, refused } }, total, by_day[] { day, calls, grid }, keys[] { prefix, env, label, …, energy { in, write }, binds }, energy { in, write, sources { <source>: { direction, calls, grid, usdc, paid_grid } } }, by_bind[] { kind project | agent | workflow, id, keys, in, write }, cost { <stage>: { micro, grid } }, earnings { rows[] { leg reseller | provider, ref, usdc, grid }, total, vault { connector, release, payout { state held, held_by } } }, columns. 503 when the counters do not answer (never zeros).

auth.rule: The key names itself (?scope=tenant: every key of its tenant). On www.taifoon.io the seat reads the signed-in tenant.

tools.name: access_enclave
tools.summary: A dedicated enclave (taifoon.tee enclave_hour): the quote and the offer. One buyer’s own Phala Cloud TDX CVM running a compose on the allowlist (by its file’s sha256), priced at Phala’s live hourly rate plus disk, plus 20 %, paid from the one balance hour by hour. ?compose= (an allowlisted id or sha256) &hours= (1 to 720). mode says live, dry_run (the provisioner rehearses: nothing deployed, nothing taken) or offline.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.enclave.quote.v1: compose { id, name, compose, compose_sha256, instance_types, port }, instance, disk_gb, hours, mode live | dry_run | offline, provisioner { seen_at, live, fresh }, rate { usd_h, at, source, disk_usdc_per_gb_hour, cost_plus_bps }, price { per_hour_micro, per_hour_usdc, hold_usdc, total_usdc }, hold, debit, request, allowlist[], hours_range, enclaves[] (with a key). 503 rate_unread when Phala’s live rate cannot be read (never a stale number); 400 not_allowlisted.

auth.rule: Open (the quote). With X-API-Key the answer also lists that key’s enclaves; a key that is sent must be valid.

tools.name: access_enclave
tools.summary: Request a dedicated enclave: the first hour is held from the key’s balance and the provisioner deploys the allowlisted compose under Taifoon’s Phala workspace, accepts it (Phala’s verifier says quote.verified on a fresh challenge and the attested compose is the allowlisted file) and hands the endpoint over. Each further hour is taken before it starts; when the balance cannot cover the next hour the enclave is stopped, and it is deleted on release. DRY RUN until the owner’s live switch: nothing deployed, nothing taken, every answer says so.
tools.returns: Send { compose (id or sha256; absent = the first on the allowlist), hours (1 to 720) }. 201 schema taifoon.enclave.request.v1: enclave { id, state Requested, dry_run, compose, compose_sha256, instance, hours, hours_debited 1, price { per_hour_usdc, rate_usd_h, paid_usdc }, transitions[], release }, quote. 402 budget (the balance does not cover the first hour; a Refused record is kept), 409 busy, 429 too_many | rate_limited, 503 provisioner_offline | rate_unread (nothing taken).

auth.rule: The key whose balance pays (a free key with a balance is enough). 6 requests a minute, 60 a day; at most 2 active enclaves per key.

tools.name: access_enclave__id
tools.summary: One enclave of your key: its state, the endpoint once it is accepted, the acceptance (quote verified, compose attested, the proof link), the hours paid, its usage keys and every transition it fired.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.enclave.v1: enclave { id, state Requested | Deploying | Accepting | Running | Stopped | Released | Refused | Failed, dry_run, rehearsal, compose, compose_sha256, instance, hours, hours_debited, price, endpoint, resource_key, acceptance, created_at, running_since, stopped_at, stop_reason, why, refunded_usdc, usage_keys[], transitions[] { at, machine, transition, event }, release }.

auth.rule: The key that requested it; any other key gets 404.

tools.name: access_enclave__id_release
tools.summary: Release your enclave: no further hour is taken; the provisioner stops it and deletes it on Phala. One that was not deployed yet is closed at once and its held hour given back.
tools.returns: already (it was released or closed before), enclave (as GET /v1/access/enclave/:id). 404 not_found.

auth.rule: The key that requested it.

tools.name: tenant_try
tools.summary: Run one sandbox action of your tenant’s build tiles (dry-run demand, catalog counts, devnet pool plan, devnet RPC read, provable block, grade credits, GPU terms, USDC bridge plan), counted on your tenant.
tools.returns: Send { tile: demand | catalog | pool | rpc | proof | grade | gpu | bridge }. tile, call, status, ms, answer (the operation’s own answer). Nothing is signed, sent or kept.

tools.name: relayer_whoami
tools.summary: Check an API key without side effects.
tools.returns: The key’s label, prefix and rate limit. Does not count against the limit — a credential form should not burn quota.

tools.name: relayer_keys
tools.summary: Your projects and every collaborator key in them: prefix, member, scope, budgets and today’s use.
tools.returns: owner (key:<24 hex>), owner_prefix, projects[] { project, owner, created_at, members[] { key_prefix, ref, member, member_kind address | name, label, scope read | write, per_minute, per_day, created_at, revoked_at, today { day, writes, reads } } }. With a collaborator key: member_of { project, owner, scope, per_day }. Never a key, never a full key hash.

tools.name: relayer_keys
tools.summary: Invite a collaborator to a project: mint their own scoped relayer key, returned once.
tools.returns: Send { project, member (0x… address or a name), label?, scope? (read | write, default write), per_minute? (≤ your own, ≤ 60), per_day? (≤ 5,000, default 500) }. Returns key (ONCE; only its sha256 is kept), member { key_prefix, ref, member, scope, per_minute, per_day }, project. A read key is refused every write (403); a key over its day is refused (429). A denied wallet or a personal wallet is never a member. Operator: { label, per_minute? } → an owner key.

auth.rule: With the owner’s relayer key: invite a collaborator (a collaborator key is refused). With x-operator-token and no key: mint an owner key for a named integrator.

tools.name: relayer_keys_revoke
tools.summary: Revoke a collaborator key (or, as the operator, any key) by its prefix.
tools.returns: Send { key_prefix, project? }. revoked, already (true when it was revoked before), project, member. The key is refused from the next call on; nothing is deleted.

auth.rule: The owner’s key revokes its own collaborator keys; the operator token revokes any key by prefix (free keys included); a free key revokes itself with { "self": true }.

tools.name: relayer_activity
tools.summary: Who did what in one of your projects: each collaborator key’s calls per day and the gateway steps it made.
tools.returns: ?project=. members[] { key_prefix, ref, member, scope, days[] { day, writes, reads } (7 UTC days), totals, gateway_steps[] { id, at, resource, state, methods, tools } }, owner_gateway_steps[], sources. Owner key only.

tools.name: jobs__jobId_complete
tools.summary: Hand a completed job to the relayer.
tools.returns: The proof is re-verified and the completion recorded, idempotent on jobId + nonce. `write` says which of three things happened: a hosted vault will sign, the provider must sign, or there was nothing to write.

tools.name: jobs__jobId_complete
tools.summary: Poll a completion.
tools.returns: Its status and, once mined, the settlement transaction. Pass ?nonce=.

auth.rule: Polling spends the key's read budget (max(120, 4 × per-minute) a minute), never its write slots.

tools.name: jobs__jobId_record
