tools.summary: The task and the delivery of an assurance-hook job, committed off chain in its record.
tools.returns: GET ?chain=8453. The stored record, each part re-checked against the job’s on-chain row (the delivery must hash to the sealed evidence digest; the task must carry the on-chain buyer’s EIP-191 signature, or have been sent with the funding plan before JobFunded), and the exact message the buyer signs. A delivery bound from the broker’s held reply shows its 400-character head to a public reader and the whole text to a relayer or operator key. The judge’s evidence pack for the job reads the parts that check, whole. Nothing is written to a chain.

auth.rule: Open. A delivery bound from the broker’s held reply is shown whole to the key that opened its source handshake (X-API-Key) or the operator, as its 400-character head otherwise (_REPLY_OWNER_ONLY_v1_).

tools.name: jobs__jobId_record
tools.summary: Commit a hook job’s task or delivery to its record.
tools.returns: POST { chainId?, task?, task_signature?, delivery?, source_handshake?, delivery_from_source? }. delivery_from_source:true with source_handshake and a relayer key (or the operator token) reads the whole reply the broker holds for that handshake (up to 100,000 characters, nothing pasted, nothing cut) and keeps it when its keccak256 is the sealed digest. A delivery is kept only if its keccak256 (or sha256) equals the evidence digest sealed on chain; a task only with the buyer’s signature over the message GET returns. Answers what was admitted and why the rest was not (422 when nothing was).

auth.rule: Open (a pasted delivery must hash to the sealed digest; a task needs the buyer’s signature). delivery_from_source:true reads the broker’s held reply and needs a relayer key (X-API-Key).

tools.name: resale_sales__id
tools.summary: One resale sale of a class wall: what the buyer paid, the terms, the delivery’s Jev grade and the seller’s listing as it stands now (_RESALE_SALE_READ_v1_).
tools.returns: rule, sale { schema taifoon.resale.sale.v1, id, at, class, seller, handshake_id, payment { tx, network, payer, pay_to, asset, paid_units }, terms { price_units, fee_units, payout_units }, content_check { ok }, payout { state, payee, tx? (a tx hash, once paid) }, seller_payment? { units, tx, from, network? (a network id) }, channel (the X-Taifoon-Channel the sale was recorded with, null when none: _SALE_READ_CHANNEL_v1_) }, delivery { id, at, content_check { ok }, grade { decision_id, verdict, task_met } | null } | null, listing { id, key, endpoint, whose, state, payout, owner, probes[] } | null. The buyer’s task and the reply are not returned. 404 sale_not_found.

tools.name: resale_sales
tools.summary: The resale sales whose seller share is still owed, oldest first (?since=<ISO, at most 7 days back>&limit=).
tools.returns: rule, state owed, since, count, sales[] { id, at, class, network, payout_units }.

tools.name: deliveries_stats
tools.summary: Delivery evidence, public view: per paid product, how many paid answers were recorded and how many passed the product’s content rule, per day over 14 days.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.delivery.stats.v1: records, content_ok, content_ok_rate, products[] { product, source, records, content_ok, content_ok_rate, last { at, ok, rule, status }, days[] }. No bodies, no payers.

tools.name: capabilities
tools.summary: What the n8n population can do: workflow templates and community nodes. ?view=jev: what a Jev grade covers per network (Base, Arbitrum, Arc, Robinhood, Monad, Solana) and job type, each covered cell with the mainnet transaction its live test resolves.
tools.returns: Capabilities, NOT agents — none of these can be hired until someone deploys one and registers a card. Per source: how much was read and why not all of it.

tools.name: capabilities_skills
tools.summary: The n8n-side skill vocabulary.
tools.returns: Per tag, in the same kebab-case /v1/match compares: how many templates and how many community nodes carry it.

tools.name: capabilities_search
tools.summary: Browse and search every n8n template and community node.
tools.returns: Matching capabilities, most used first, each with the request that plans enrolling it. None of them can be hired as they are. ?q= ?kind=template|node ?skill= ?offset= ?limit=

tools.name: enroll_plan
tools.summary: Plan turning a capability into a hireable agent.
tools.returns: The card to publish, the steps, and the economics: the deposit the operator must hold, what each of the four endings costs it, and why it is not insurable on day one. Registers nothing.

tools.name: assurance
tools.summary: Where the assurance layer is deployed, and on which chains it is not.
tools.returns: Per chain: the hook and pool factory addresses, who may upgrade them, and a plain statement when a chain has nothing deployed yet.

tools.name: assurance_quote
tools.summary: Price the guarantee on a job before anyone commits to it.
tools.returns: The premium interval from that seller's settled record, the deposit the protocol requires, and a refusal with a reason when the terms could not settle.

tools.name: assurance_call
tools.summary: The exact calls to fund, settle or cover an insured job.
tools.returns: Unsigned calldata with the effect in plain words and who must sign it. _LINE_CLOSED_v1_: back-seller is planned only into a vault that answers encumbered() and freeAssets() at the time of the call, and create-pool never on the first line of Base or Arc: otherwise 409 { code: line_closed, why (the chain fact), refused, still_open (withdrawals and redemptions), open_instead { line, factory, how } }; a new pool is planned by POST /v1/pools/open. Kinds: fund-job, submit, complete, expire, reject, create-pool, back-seller, post-verdict, set-evaluator, stamp, give-feedback, accept, cancel-open, dispute, finalize-reject, claim-auto-complete, settle-stale-dispute (_V4_ENDINGS_PLAN_v1_: with expire, each is planned on the hook that holds the job, from that hook’s own read of its state and deadlines, with moves[] and the signer; a transition that is not available answers 409 { code: wrong_state | too_early | window_closed | not_your_call | not_v4 | use_auto_complete, available_at }), register-8004 (register(agentURI) on the canonical ERC-8004 identity registry — the signer’s wallet becomes the owner; Base, Arc, Ethereum, BNB, Abstract, Robinhood and the devnet). Nothing is signed or sent here.

tools.name: assurance_markets
tools.summary: Every public two-sided assurance line: FOR backs a seller to deliver a job, AGAINST and COVER pay out if it fails. One round per job, priced from the seller’s record in the market, settled by the job’s own ending.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.assurance.markets.v1: markets[] { network, chain_id, runtime, name, status, market (where new rounds open), open_list (anyone lists a job on it), prior[] { market, from_block } (the line's earlier markets: their rounds and positions are served to their end), source, hook, asset, evaluator, arbiter, answer_log, params, state Active|Paused|Shutdown, owner, positions, rounds, markets_of_line[] { market, role current|earlier, opens_rounds, anyone_lists, from_block, state, owner, positions, rounds }, links }, hidden (lines not served until approved). positions, rounds and sides count every market of the line; state and owner are the current market's.

tools.name: assurance_book
tools.summary: One seller’s assurance books: its record in the market, the price a position gets now, both sides estimated, open rounds with depth, past resolutions with the Jev ruling.
tools.returns: ?network= (36927, 8453, 42161, 5042, 4663, 143) &seller=0x… &class=? → schema taifoon.assurance.book.v1: market (where the next round opens), anyone_lists, fee { bps, min_units, when }, books[] { book, market, opens_rounds (the current market's book: the price now), class_id, record { delivered_counted, failed, distinct_buyers }, price_now { p, p_pct, insurable, parts_pct }, sides { AGAINST, COVER, FOR: expectedReturn, variance, sd, winProbability, ifWin, ifLose; fair_p_pct, offered_p_pct, basis }, senior { open, cap, rule }, manipulation, rounds[] { job_id, state, label, price, for_junior, for_senior, x_total, against_gross, cover_gross, liability, collateral_free, held, jev { ruling, answers_digest, answers }, links } }.

tools.name: assurance_round
tools.summary: One job’s assurance round: its positions, the live price, whether positions are open.
tools.returns: ?network=&job=0x(32 bytes) → schema taifoon.assurance.round.v1 { market (the line's market that holds the round), state, label, open, job_state, quote { p, p_pct, insurable }, depth fields, positions[] { id, owner, side FOR|AGAINST|COVER, junior, active, stake, fee, p, pays_if_fails, pays_now, opened_tx } }; 404 no_round.

tools.name: assurance_positions
tools.summary: One wallet’s assurance positions and what each pays now.
tools.returns: ?network=&owner=0x… → schema taifoon.assurance.positions.v1 { positions[] { id, market (position ids count from 0 on each market of a line), job_id, side, active, stake, fee, pays_if_fails, round_state, claimable, opened_tx } }.

tools.name: assurance_networks
tools.summary: Every network the assurance suite is live on, one row each: the V4 line, the market, the Safe owner, health, settlements, Jev grades, cases and genome coverage, with a pass/fail check per part.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.assurance.networks.v1 { networks[] { chain_id, chain, line { hook, factory, adapter, market, outcome, settle_live, why_not_live, token, symbol }, safe { expected (registry), name, hook_owner (owner() read now), ok }, market { address, state, owner_ok, rounds, positions, last_round, ok } | null, settlements { v4_discovered, x402_discovered, last_found, lag_s, error } | null, jev { seen, graded, agree, disagree, review } | null, cases { total, dispute, grade, wrong } | null, genome { contracts, events, unrecognised, scanned_to, head, complete, error } | null, checks[] { name, ok, why } }, solana, unread[] (a source that did not answer), sources }. Rows come from the address registry: a chain gains a row when its V4 hook lands there.

tools.name: assurance_health
tools.summary: Every served assurance line, checked live: the market answers, owner() is the network’s Safe, its state (paused?), rounds and the last round.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.assurance.health.v1 { ok (every line ok), at, lines[] { network, chain_id, name, market, answers, owner, owner_expected, owner_ok, state Active|Paused|Shutdown|unread, paused, positions, rounds, anyone_lists, earlier[] { market, answers, owner, owner_ok, state, positions } (the line's earlier markets, each checked the same way), last_round { job_id, block, tx, market } | null, read_ms, ok (the current market and every earlier one) } }.

tools.name: assurance_plan
tools.summary: The unsigned transactions to back a seller (FOR), challenge it (AGAINST), buy cover, withdraw, claim, open, resolve, void or sweep a round, simulated, for your own wallet. The layer never signs and never holds a key.
tools.returns: Send { network (36927, 8453, 42161, 5042, 4663, 143), action open_round|back|challenge|cover|withdraw|claim|resolve|void|sweep, from (your wallet), job (bytes32), class? (open_round), amount (back, withdraw), x (challenge, cover), max_price_pct? (default 2), position? (withdraw, claim), market? (one of the line's markets; found from the job's round or your position when not named) } → schema taifoon.assurance.plan.v1 { market (the market the transactions go to: open_round the current one, anyone lists where open_list; every other action the market that holds the round or your position), txs[] { step, to, data, value "0", chainId, from } (an exact approve first when needed, never a standing one), quote { p, p_pct, max_price, pays_if_fails, fee, you_pay, estimate } (challenge, cover), simulation { ok, error, with, balance_short? } (the position call simulated with your approve applied by a state override; a market refusal is named, e.g. RoundNotOpen) }. 404 network_not_served (a network with no public line), 409 round_on_earlier_market (open_round on a job whose round is on the line's earlier market) { market, round_state }, 409 market_closed_to_new_rounds (open_round with market = an earlier one), 400 bad_request (withdraw/claim: your position id is on two markets of the line: name one), 409 no_round, 409 round_not_open { refusal ref_position_locked, error RoundNotOpen, round_state }, 409 not_insurable (challenge, cover while the seller’s record is short) { refusal ref_not_insurable, error NotInsurable, p_pct, max_ratio_pct, record, opens_at_delivered_counted }.

auth.rule: Each plan runs a simulation: a relayer key spends its own write budget; without one (a free key counts as a visitor here) a visitor is held to 10 a minute and 200 a day (429 rate_limited past it). The same plan (network, action, from, job, class, amount, x, max_price_pct, position) asked again within 5 s is answered from that simulation (x-plan-cache: hit).

tools.name: cover_quote
tools.summary: Cover a job you bought elsewhere: a quote signed by the layer’s attestors on a job you funded on Virtuals ACP (v3 or memo), BitAgent or another ERC-8183 market, or before an x402 call or an Olas Mech request. The pool pays what the market kept when nothing was delivered, or when an arbitrator’s finding goes against the delivery; nothing otherwise.
tools.returns: { ok, insurable, policy_id, quote { venue, jobChainId, escrow, jobRef, buyer, seller, jobToken, jobPrice, fundedAt, jobDeadline, pool, coverCap, premium, sellerExposureCap, validUntil, quoteId }, signatures, price { ratio, why }, job { venue, chain_id, job_id, client, provider, price, deadline, events, refund_rule }, next, rule }. 409 { insurable:false, why[] } when the job cannot be covered now (not the client, already delivered or ended, outside the buy window, the seller’s record too thin, no pool with free capital). 404 no_cover_line.

tools.name: cover_buy
tools.summary: The exact unsigned transactions to buy a quoted cover from your own wallet: an approval of exactly the premium when the allowance is short, then buyCover. The layer never signs and never holds a key.
tools.returns: Send { network, quote, signatures, from } (as cover/quote returned them) → { ok, policy_id, txs[] { what, from, to, data, value "0x0", chainId }, have { balance, allowance }, after }. 409 refused (another buyer, expired quote, unsigned, balance short).

tools.name: cover_policy__id
tools.summary: One cover policy read from the chain: its status, claim window, the ending the attestors signed once the job ended, and the transaction that settles it (anyone may send it) or expires it.
tools.returns: ?network= → { ok, status active|settled|expired, says, policy { buyer, seller, pool, jobKey, coverCap, premium, jobDeadline, boughtAt, splitBps }, claim_window { from, until, now }, ledger[] (chain:tx:logIndex rows), attestor (the signed ending or why it is pending), claim { ending, pays, loss, can_settle_now, txs[] } }.

tools.name: cover_policies
tools.summary: Every cover policy a buyer bought on a line, with its status now.
tools.returns: { ok, buyer, policies[] { id (chain:tx:logIndex), policyId, jobKey, seller, pool, coverCap, premium, jobDeadline, status, says, link } }.

tools.name: agents_contracts
tools.summary: The contracts this layer reads jobs from.
tools.returns: Each contract, its role, and its address — so anyone can read the same logs.

tools.name: registry_agents
tools.summary: Browse hireable agents by field, best-trust-first.
tools.returns: Filter with ?chain= (+ optional ?kind=a2a|mcp|x402) or ?skill=, and ?limit=. Each agent: chain, id, owner, endpoint, kind, skills, trust, corroboration, TEE-served, status. Spam/Sybil/scam agents are already excluded.

tools.name: registry_agents__chain__id
tools.summary: One agent’s full registry record.
tools.returns: Identity, endpoint, skills, the rails it was seen on, its trust breakdown, filter verdict, and the as-of dates behind them.

tools.name: registry_search
tools.summary: One search over on-chain agents AND n8n capabilities, source-tagged.
tools.returns: Filter with ?q= and/or ?skills=comma,separated, ?source=onchain|n8n, ?hireable=true, ?limit=. Each hit carries a `source` badge (onchain | n8n-node | n8n-template); on-chain hits are spam-filtered and trust-ranked (contractable), n8n hits are capabilities (hireable:false).

tools.name: registry_agents__chain__id_assurance
tools.summary: The assurance interval for an agent, with its evidence.
tools.returns: The Wilson interval over its cheat rate, widened for stale/thin/uncorroborated evidence and gated to UNKNOWN when there is no settled record — always shipped with the inputs (settled/cheated, reachability, TEE, staleness, as-of) so the number is auditable.

tools.name: registry_owners__addr
tools.summary: Every hireable agent an owner controls (the Sybil view).
tools.returns: The owner’s agents and a sybil_signal flag when the cluster is large — the same signal the registry prices against.

tools.name: registry_lookup
tools.summary: Registered agents by owner or by endpoint URL, hireable or not (_REGISTRY_LOOKUP_v1_).
tools.returns: Send exactly one of ?owner=0x…, ?url=https://… or ?host=name. agents[] { chain_id, agent_id, owner, name, endpoint, endpoint_kind, card_host, agent_uri, skills, wire { status, cause, probed_at, url }, match owner | wallet | endpoint | card-service | agent-uri | host, matched }, best match first (≤ 50; total counts all). A URL no agent publishes falls back to the agents on its host (match host). Read from the harvester export, the rows the registry is built from; registry/owners and registry/search list hireable agents only. 503 when the export is unreadable.

tools.name: registry_stats
tools.summary: Registry totals and the provable set root.
tools.returns: Total records, hireable count per chain, and the MMR set-root committing the Live agent set.

tools.name: judge_ref
tools.summary: Ask TypeSafe/Jev one question about an item with your own TypeSafe key — or, without a key, get Taifoon’s grade of it.
tools.returns: Send { state | jobId, chainId?, question?, options?, key? }. With `key`: the calibrated answer to your question — value, the full probabilities distribution, confidence — its lifecycle ending and the recorded decision. Without `key`: Taifoon’s grade (RUBRIC_v1: facts proved in code, a composed verdict, a receipt and an anchored decision), exactly as /v1/judge/compose returns it, with product:"grade"; a custom question is not asked. quota { who, grades { free, used, left } }.

auth.rule: With body.key (your own TypeSafe key, forwarded, never stored) Jev answers your question. Without one you get Taifoon's grade of the item (the /v1/judge/compose pipeline), counted as one of your three free grades.

tools.name: hire_assemble
tools.summary: Have the judge assemble the whole path to hiring an agent for a task — a shareable record.
tools.returns: Send { task, required_skills: [..], budget_usdc?, key? }. Signed in, this ranks the vetted shortlist (/v1/match), fixes the verdict tier per listing (DET if the capability declares an output schema, else REF — Rule 1), asks Jev ONE calibrated question over the shortlist on your own TypeSafe key (`key`, forwarded, never stored; without one: 403 byo_key), and records the assembled path — shortlist, tier, judge pins, the guidance verdict with its full distribution, the Rule-6 digest, and the next unsigned steps (handshake → quote → calls). Returns { id, share_url, path }.

auth.rule: Or your own TypeSafe key in body.key; the path is owned by whichever identity assembled it.

tools.name: hire_suggest
tools.summary: Auto-suggest the inputs of a hire from live data — skills, budget, terms — with an optional calibrated Jev pass.
tools.returns: Send { task, seller?, chainId?, jev? }. Skills are matched from the harvester’s live skills vocabulary, budget from the observed market (/v1/agents/market), terms from the seller’s record; every suggestion carries data_as_of (harvest generatedAt, ageSeconds, stale). With jev:true and your own TypeSafe key as `key`, ONE calibrated question ranks the matched skills.

auth.rule: A read. jev:true adds a calibrated ranking that runs on your own TypeSafe key (body.key); without one it is skipped.

tools.name: hire_lifecycle__jobId
tools.summary: The whole lifecycle of a job, traced and verifiable — every phase from listing to settlement, against the chain.
tools.returns: GET ?chain=8453|5042&prove=1&tenant=moonbeam. Reads the hook that HOLDS the job: the layer’s first, then each tenant’s hook on that chain (or only the named tenant’s) — `tenant`, `hook` and `source_of_state` say which; events and verify links come from that hook. Folds the assurance hook’s state (read from chain), the layer’s records (handshake, sealed completion, judge verdict, the assembled hire path) and the observatory’s decode into the whitepaper’s state table: state, who can exit, timeout, default on timeout, terminal, and what the ending does to the record. Every transaction carries a verify link (/v1/proof/tx/{chain}/{tx}); with prove=1 each is proven live under the superroot (V5) and its finality reported.

tools.name: hire_path__id_attach
tools.summary: Attach the on-chain job to an assembled hire path, so the lifecycle trace carries the judge’s guidance.
tools.returns: Send { jobId, chain }. Only the account that assembled the path may attach. Returns the path with job_id/chain set and its lifecycle URL.

auth.rule: Only the principal that assembled the path (its key or account) may attach.

tools.name: onboarding_journey
tools.summary: Where you are on the one onboarding flow (account → need → match → run → watch → cockpit): your tenant, your demands with every step the loop wrote, and the one next step.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.onboarding.journey.v1: tenant { id, tag, kind, via, created_at, keys[] { prefix, env, revoked } }, step, next_step { step, title, why, action { label, href?, http?, mcp? } }, steps[] { id, title, state done | current | todo }, first_demand, latest_demand, demands[] (newest 5: id, state, class, need, seller, job_id, ending, events, read), counted { calls, demands, settles, credits, window 90d }, cockpit_url, tenant_url, flow. 401 carries the first step (register or sign in).

auth.rule: The key names the tenant. On www.taifoon.io the console reads the same answer with the signed-in session.

tools.name: onboarding_journey
tools.summary: The flow’s need → match → run for your tenant: a dry run answers the class, the sellers the loop ranks for it and the terms from POST /v1/pools/quote; without dry_run the demand is kept on the devnet 36927, opened by the key you sent (or your sandbox key).
tools.returns: Send { need } or { catalog_id } or { class, input }, dry_run?, price_units?. Dry run: class, input, resolved?, catalog?, sellers { rule SELLER_CHOICE_v3, rows[] { seller, rank, chosen, score, hires, answered, latency_ms } }, cover_preview (as POST /v1/demands dry_run, with record { n, incorrect, wilson [lo, hi], calibrated, insurable } as the quote stated it), terms (the same fields, read, never recomputed), next_step. Kept: 201 { demand, read, next_step }. 4xx answers carry next_step.

auth.rule: The key names the tenant (a person on www.taifoon.io uses the session). The tenant keeps the POST /v1/demands budgets: 3 kept demands a minute and 20 a day, 30 dry runs a minute.

tools.name: onboarding_funnel
tools.summary: How far outside tenants got on the onboarding flow: registered → first call → first demand → settled → paid, stuck per stage, Taifoon’s own tenants apart. Counts only.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.onboarding.funnel.v1, stages[], outside { reached { stage: n } (cumulative), furthest { stage: n }, stuck { stage: n } (same stage 1 h to 24 h), tenants, newest_at, new_24h }, ours { reached, tenants }, rule, tenants_walked, as_of, took_ms. No tenant id, key, wallet or email. 30 s memo.

tools.name: onboarding_flows
tools.summary: Ready-to-run hire flows resurfaced from the harvest — the onboarding surface.
tools.returns: GET ?skill=&source=hireable-agent|settled-job|registered-n8n&limit=&id=. Each flow: a task in words, required skills from the card, a budget with its basis (the settled job’s own price, else the observed market), the candidate, the prefilled next calls (suggest → match → assemble → handshake → calls → trace) and a console_url that opens ASSEMBLE prefilled. Built deterministically by the delivery loop; TTL 7 days; every row carries data_as_of.

tools.name: onboarding_batch
tools.summary: The first onboarding batch: the agents that answered on the wire, in their own protocol.
tools.returns: GET ?limit=. The latest probe: how many candidates were spoken to (MCP initialize/tools/list, A2A message/send, legacy tasks/send), how many answered, by protocol, how many charge per call (x402), and each ready agent with its card, tools or reply, latency and price. Trust ranks card presence; this ranks who answers.

tools.name: onboarding_refresh
tools.summary: Rebuild the onboarding flows from the live harvest, jobs feed and registry (what the delivery loop calls).
tools.returns: Idempotent (stable ids); one real rebuild per 10 minutes, callers in between get the last report with memo:true. Returns built/created/refreshed/live counts, by_source, data_as_of.

auth.rule: Open (a 10-minute memo bounds rebuilds); ?force=1 bypasses the memo and needs the operator token.

tools.name: onboard_worklist
tools.summary: The agents that are almost hireable, for anyone to help over the line: the first check of the one hireable definition each fails, or hireable but not listed, or listed with no first offer.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.onboard.worklist.v1. ?stage=fix (publishes an endpoint, fails a check: card | owner | skills | no-answer | wrong-dialect | needs-key | rate-limited | stale | hire-path; the rows the almost-hireable file carries, at most 3 per endpoint host, host_n says how many agents that host carries) | list (hireable, its owner has no card in GET /v1/agents/registered) | first-job (hireable, listed, no handshake names it); list and first-job carry every row (the first 3 of each host first, then the rest). &check= &chain= &q= &limit 1..200 (default 25; above 200 reads 200, never an empty page) &offset; &agent=<chain>:<id> for one agent. Paging (_WORKLIST_PAGING_v1_): one total order per stage (the rank, ending on the key), so pages read with limit + offset neither overlap nor skip; limit, offset and next_offset (null on the last page) in the answer; matched is the rows after the filters. rows[] { key, chain_id, agent_id, name, owner, wallet, card_url, endpoint, host, host_n, kind, skills, check, cause, reason, probed_at, value_usdc, stage, action probe | message | list | job }, counts per stage (unchanged by paging), by_check, by_chain, checks { words, fix, who }, class (the class a fixed agent enters and its price band), read_at, age_s. Rewritten every 30 min.

tools.name: onboard_spec_check
tools.summary: Check an agent against the one agent spec (_AGENT_SPEC_v1_, coord lang/cue/agent-spec.cue): every reference point OK, FIX or MISSING with the fix words and who fixes it, the totals per gate (H1–H4 and the almost-hireable checks) and whether it is ready to be listed. Read-only: nothing is registered, minted or probed.
tools.returns: Send an AgentSpec (schema taifoon.agent.spec.v1), or { card_url } (the card is read into a spec: identity, doors from services[] and kind, skills, classes[], price_usdc per class, payTo from the card's address or agentWallet; an x402 door named by the card is asked once, unpaid, for its 402 accepts), or { agent: "<chain>:<id>" } (the layer's readiness of that agent, with its probe, record and quote as the observed points, and its card when it has one). 200 schema taifoon.agent.spec.check.v1 { ok, ready, input card | spec | agent, spec (the normalised AgentSpec), points[] { id, section, need, gate, covers, status OK | FIX | MISSING, words?, fix?, who?, detail? }, open[] { id, why } (optional points not declared), not_read[] { id, why } (observed points the layer has not read for this input), gates { <gate>: { ok, fix, missing } }, totals { ok, fix, missing }, blocking[] (the required ids not OK), fields { <ref>: { status, fix, who, gate, open?, unread?, detail? } } (every point by id and each section as spec.<section>; a tour reads fields.{ref}.status), reads { card?, x402?, readiness? }, rule, read_at }. 400 bad_request { field } for a body that is none of the three; a card that cannot be read answers 200 with spec.identity.card_url MISSING and the reason.

auth.rule: Public by design, read-only: a visitor is held to the POST /v1/onboard/help budget (10 a minute, 100 a day); a key spends its own.

tools.name: onboard_graph
tools.summary: The onboarding graph (_ONBOARD_GRAPH_v1_, coord lang/cue/onboard-graph.cue): every reference point an agent is checked on, the gate it answers to, the check that proves the gate, the fix and who clears it, the op that proves it, the tour step that walks it, the classes, the onboard flow and the hops of a sale, derived from the language. Read-only.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.onboard.graph.v1 { rule, ops, sources[] { id, expr, file, contributes, docs, skill }, goals { vaultable | hireable | covered | metered: { gates, hop, words } }, goal_order, edge_kinds, counts { nodes, edges, by_node_kind, by_edge_kind }, unresolved_ops[], nodes[] { id, kind ref_point | gate | check | fix | class | op | tour_step | lineage_hop | doc | skill, label, source, text?, words?, fix?, who?, … }, edges[] { from, kind requires | proves | fixes | next | anchors | explains | belongs_to, to, source } }. ?node=<id>&depth=1..4 (default 1): the slice around one node (both directions), with center; ?q=<words> (&limit 1..50, default 8): hits[] { id, score } best first, and the nodes and edges of the hits with their neighbours (the slice the Studio agent is grounded on); ?kind=<node kind>: nodes of that kind only. 404 unknown_node for a node the graph does not have.

tools.name: scout
tools.summary: The scout (_SCOUT_v1_, coord lang/scout + lang/cue/scout.cue): the search and the search for clients, one pipeline both ways over the indexes the layer keeps (the market book, the regular buyers, the venue buyer pools, the live match twigs). Words name a need by the catalogue's vocabulary (class, model, chain, budget; no model guesses); every row is fitted 1 to 10 with its reasons, what counts against it and what is not read yet; a class's ICP counts paid demand only (bids apart). Read-only: a swarm task is a plan and nothing is sent.
tools.returns: no query: { ok, schema taifoon.scout.v1, counts { classes, paid_usd_7d, notional_usd_7d, venues, index }, digest, classes[] { class, usd_7d, notional_usd_7d, buyers, venues, expected_usd_7d, top }, calls }. ?q=: { ok, schema taifoon.scout.find.v1, live?, need { text, side buy | sell, class, class_from, category, model, chain, venue, budget { usd, per } | null }, filters { side, class, model, chain, venue, max_usd_per_call, v1 }, rows[] { id, side offer | demand | pool, venue, who, class, model, usd_per_call, usd_7d, calls_7d, route, proof { index, twig, head, claim } | null, fit { score 1..10, factors, reasons[], against[], gaps[] } } }. ?class=: { ok, icp (schema taifoon.scout.icp.v1: class, model, seller_usd_per_call, our_usd_per_call, paid { usd_7d, notional_usd_7d, calls_7d, buyers, venues }, price_band, cadence_median_s, bound_share, expected_usd_7d, segments[], venues[] { venue, name, segment, usd_7d, notional_usd_7d, calls_7d, buyers, price_band, our_price_fits, bound, sellers, expected_usd_7d, route, channel }, prospects[], next[], digest), swarm { width, send: owner, root, tasks[] { n, venue, segment, reads[], walk, move, draft | null, expected_usd_7d, digest } }, context (at most 2,400 characters, what the genie reads) }. 400 bad_param for a side, limit, price or width out of range.

tools.name: onboard_diagnose
tools.summary: Diagnose an agent on the onboarding graph: runs the spec check (POST /v1/onboard/spec/check) on a card, a registered agent or an AgentSpec, paints every reference point's status onto the graph, and answers per goal (vaultable H2, hireable H1 + hire path, covered H3, metered H4) the state and the shortest list of fixes, each with its words, who, the op that proves it and the tour step that walks it. Read-only: nothing is registered, minted, probed or paid.
tools.returns: Send what POST /v1/onboard/spec/check reads: { card_url }, { agent: "<chain>:<id>" } or an AgentSpec. 200 schema taifoon.onboard.diagnosis.v1 { ok, input card | agent | spec, ready, gates { H1 | H2 | H3 | H4 | <almost check>: { state OK | FIX | MISSING | UNREAD, points[] { id, status } } }, goals { vaultable | hireable | covered | metered: { state OK | FIX | MISSING | UNREAD, gates, hop, words, fixes[] (node ids) } }, fixes[] (ordered, deduped across goals) { id (fix:<ref>), ref, status, need, gates, goals, words, fix, who, proved_by (op id), walked_by (tour step id) | null, ops (the ops the fix words name) }, not_read[], check { totals, blocking, reads } (the spec check's own answer, trimmed), graph { schema, nodes, edges }, rule, read_at }. 400 bad_request { field } as the spec check.

auth.rule: Public by design, read-only: a visitor is held to the POST /v1/onboard/help budget (10 a minute, 100 a day); a key spends its own.

tools.name: onboard_help
tools.summary: One helper action on one agent, credited to the helper: probe it now, count a copied message to its operator, confirm a listing, confirm a first offer.
tools.returns: Send { action: probe | message | list | job, chainId, agentId, wallet? (a label: nothing is signed) [, address (list: what POST /v1/agents/register answered)] [, handshake_id (job: what POST /v1/handshake answered)] }. probe: elapsed_ms, probe { status, protocol, url, cause, latency_ms }, why { words, fix, who }, answered, hireable, verdict. Every action: helper, caused[] and created[] of checked | fixed | listed | first_job | hireable (each held once per agent, by the first helper whose action caused it). Nothing is ever sent to an operator.

auth.rule: Public by design: a probe is held to the POST /v1/agents/probe visitor budget (4 a minute, 40 a day); the other actions to 10 a minute and 100 a day per visitor. A key spends its own budget.

tools.name: onboard_help
tools.summary: The caller’s credit as a helper, every attributed transition, or the helper transitions counted per day.
tools.returns: credit { acted_on, helped, became_hireable, settled } for the caller (?wallet= for a connected wallet), agents[] it acted on with their transitions, events { transition, at, tx, ref } and graduation progress { settled, buyers } (an agent graduates at 10 settled jobs with unrelated buyers), grid (GRID earned from helping, read from the GRID API once it answers for helpers; null until then). ?view=attributions&helper=&since=: every attributed transition, Attribution v1 { v, helper, chain_id, agent_id, transition, at, day, tx, ref }, the first helper who caused it (the GRID earning rules read this). ?view=metrics&days=14: totals per transition, helpers, by_day[] { day, transition, chain_id, n }, by_helper[] { day, transition, helper, n }, actions[] { day, action, n }.

tools.name: hire_path__id
tools.summary: Read an assembled hire path (the shareable record).
tools.returns: The stored path: task, shortlist, tier, judge pins, verdict + distribution, digest, next steps, who assembled it (account id, never an email), when, and its expiry.

tools.name: hire_pad
tools.summary: The Jev pad: every field of a phase as a typed multiple-choice question over live data, answered by ONE calibrated call.
tools.returns: Send { phase: quote|calls|batch|assemble, chainId?, seller?, task?, skills?, price?, bar? (0.7|0.8|0.9, default 0.8), dry? (choices only, no call), key? }. Each field carries its choices with their basis (pools record, observed market, the seller’s record), Jev’s pick, the full distribution, confidence and whether it clears your bar. batch also returns ready_jobs: settled and rejected jobs whose seller’s record is calibrated (Wilson interval over the seller’s fail rate, n ≥ 5, width ≤ 0.35) — the ones worth a calibrated grade. Jev’s picks run on your own TypeSafe key (`key`, never stored). Jev fills in the numbers; you sign them.

auth.rule: dry:true (the choices) is open; Jev's picks need your own TypeSafe key in body.key (forwarded, never stored).

tools.name: judge_ready
tools.summary: Jobs resurfaced for a calibrated grade — sellers with a well-calibrated record first.
tools.returns: GET ?chain=. Every settled/rejected job in the observatory with its seller’s record folded in (n, fail rate, Wilson interval, pool record when one exists) and calibrated:true|false with the reason. Grading is enabled where the interval is narrow enough to mean something; the rest is listed, not hidden.

tools.name: grid_review
tools.summary: Paid deliveries worth reviewing — the work behind the reviewers’ 20%.
tools.returns: Paid, non-self-dealing ERC-8183 jobs (the Virtuals ACP contract on Base, paid in USDC) with createdAt (where to start your own chain read), the feed’s event names, the contract and the GRID a review earns; plus the oracle’s review rule.

tools.name: grid_review
tools.summary: Report a review: the delivery you re-derived from chain through your own RPC.
tools.returns: POST { owner, chainId, jobId, verdict, evidence: [{ event, tx, log_index, block, block_hash }] }. Credited when the owner runs a Grid resource, the job is paid and not self-dealing, and the evidence matches the gateway’s own reading exactly; the oracle bounds it (≤3 reviewers a job, each once). GRID points on the ledger; settlement not deployed.

auth.rule: Points go to the wallet bound to the key: bind once with owner + owner_signature (the owner signs gridReviewerMessage(owner, key_prefix)); a body owner that differs from the binding is refused.

tools.name: judge_study
tools.summary: DET against Jev on settled jobs: the ending the chain settled versus the calibrated grade from the pre-verdict trail.
tools.returns: The latest recorded study: agreement rate, the confusion by DET ending, calls spent, the model, every row (job, chain, events, DET with its basis, Jev with its full distribution, agree, proof blob) and the caveat (no deliverable content is on chain; the judge saw only the trail).

tools.name: settle
tools.summary: The unsigned settlement of one paid call — a judge call, a call to another agent, or a grid resource call — on the coordination layer.

auth.rule: A relayer key (X-API-Key, free from POST /v1/register) on every chain but the Taifoon devnet 36927, which stays keyless for the studio and the quickstart (test tokens); a key that is sent must be valid on any chain. The plan is unsigned either way. _GATE2_v1_: a sent `economy` is re-quoted by POST /v1/pools/quote (jev-wilson quoteEconomy) and refused when it differs (409 economy_requoted { quoted, yours }) or the line has none (409 economy_not_on_line); `allow_custom_economy: true` keeps the sent legs on the devnet 36927 only; a sent `deposit` under 2 × price is held to the quoted floor (400 deposit_below_floor { floor }); `decision_digest` needs its `decision_id` (400 decision_unbound).

tools.name: fees_scheme
tools.summary: The published fee rate (_FEE_SCHEME_SERVED_v1_): the ONE payment scheme every sale of the layer is priced by, price_to_buyer = seller_price + our_fee + venue_fee(in) + venue_fee(out); the layer's price is the one price rule (_UNDERCUT_v3_: 20 % under the cheapest matching seller, never under cost × 1.2, rounded up), the layer's fee the spread, each venue's own fee with the contract read it rests on. Served from the scheme module itself (payment-scheme schemeBlock); also GET /v1/fees?view=scheme.
tools.returns: { ok, schema: taifoon.fee.scheme.v1, id and scheme_id taifoon.payment.scheme.v1, rule_id ONE_PAYMENT_SCHEME_v1, what, formula, terms, legs[], ending_legs[], our_fee { over_seller_pct (20), bps (2000), rule wall, rounding ceil, min_units, own_floor_units, words, rules[] (wall · job_quote · metered, each with its door and base), note }, venue_fee { rule, taken, by_venue { <venue>: { status, total_bps, parts[] { part, bps, to, when }, base, rounding, taken, on_refund, evidence { contract_ref, chain, block, reads[], how } } }, table[] { venue, status, platform_bps, evaluator_bps, total_bps, taken, rounding, on_refund, contract_ref, chain, block, net_of_10000, gross_for_10000 } }, gross_up { rule, steps[] }, refund, invariant, modes, code, tests, quote }. A venue's contract is named by its address-registry reference (contract_ref).

auth.rule: Open: no key needed; a key sent is passed on, never required.

tools.name: fees_quote
tools.summary: The layer’s fee on one job settled through it, priced from live gas (_JOB_FEE_v1_): the larger of the routing bps and the layer’s own gas on the job at the quoted gas price plus a volatility buffer, plus a margin; refused below the smallest price where that fits under the hook’s 10 % cap, so a settled job never costs the layer more than it pays.
tools.returns: GET ?chain=8453 (default) | 36927 &price=<USDC> or &price_units=<smallest units> &profile=stand-in (default: our stand-in seller accepts, submits and forwards the price to the doer) | direct (the doer is the seller of record: only our verdict) | relayed (we also open the job). 200 schema taifoon.fee-quote.v1 { served, fee (null when refused), why, by_bps, floor, cap, min_price, floored, gas { legs[] {leg, who, gas, bytes, l1_fee_wei}, units, base_fee_wei, tip_wei, buffer_bps, buffer_basis, quoted_gas_price_wei, l2_wei, l1_wei, total_wei, eth_usd, eth_move_bps, usdc, block }, margin, bps, valid_until, ttl_s, rule, sources { rpc (razor, else the warmbed rotation), feed, gas_oracle, window_blocks, via (razor | direct feeHistory and why), rise_basis }, line { live, why } }; amounts in the token’s smallest units. 36927 answers the devnet’s fixed rule (its gas is free). 503 stale_price (ETH/USD older than the limit) or rpc_unavailable.

tools.name: fees
tools.summary: What settling through the layer has earned: the fee on each job that named the Taifoon JudgeAdapter as its evaluator, read from the chain.

tools.name: settle
tools.summary: Settlements recorded on the coordination layer, newest first — from every write path (runner, relayer, evaluator leg, site).
tools.returns: GET ?source=runner|relayer|evaluator-leg|keeper|site&chain=<id>. settlements[]: id, source, kind, chainId, jobId, buyer, seller, price, token, tenant, verdict (complete | reject | expire | cheat), decision_id, jev_decision_id (the Jev decision; decision_id is the same id), operator_decision_id (the operator’s own decision on a held needs_review job, recorded through POST /v1/settle/evaluate; null when none), decided_by (who decided the ending: jev | loop-agent | operator; null when nobody decided it — a keeper expire (which may still name, in jev_decision_id, the Jev decision that held the job, proven through POST /v1/settle/decided), a row with no ending yet, or a buyer’s completion observed by a lifecycle read, which does not know the decision; the label as the row was written, never rewritten), decided_by_now { recorded, now, corrected } and corrections[] (the append-only corrections of its operator record, each with its anchor link and GET /v1/settle/operator/:id, overlaid on read), transition (the coordination machine’s transition id when a writer proved it from the ending transaction: auto_complete_v4 | finalize_reject_v4 | stale_dispute_v4 through POST /v1/settle/ended; else null), at, txs[] { role, hash (full), link (basescan · Arc explorer · /scan/36927/tx on the devnet) }; the old runner’s own fields under `runner`. Present only on the rows whose writer knew them (lib/settle-records SettlementRecord): handshake_id (hs_…), fee_usdc, fee_rule, seller_whose ours | outside, paid_on (CAIP-2), funded_from; from a V4 job read on its chain: doer, test_doer, doer_paid, premium, fee, deposit, to_seller, to_buyer, to_pool, to_evaluator (the token’s smallest units), fee_to; from the chain watcher: pool, opened_at and ended_at (unix seconds, block times), class_id, demand_id. Plus count, total, filter { source, chain }, by_source, by_chain. A row is written only on a confirmed on-chain outcome: a mined relayer transaction, or a lifecycle read that observed the terminal state on the hook (BACKLOG 42).

tools.name: settle_evaluate
tools.summary: The evaluator leg: the job’s evaluator ends a job on chain from the recorded decision — the verdict a grade decided (complete | reject), or, on a job held on needs_review, the operator’s own recorded decision — one unsigned JudgeAdapter.postVerdict, never a second judge call. Jev’s answer is never replaced.
tools.returns: Send { jobId?, chainId: 36927, tenant?: "moonbeam", decision_id, verdict: complete | reject, reason, receipt? }. tenant moonbeam ends a job on Moonbeam’s devnet hook through its own adapter; a decision made about the hook job itself (subject = the job id) names the job. Answers the unsigned call postVerdict(jobId, 1 Conformant | 2 NonConformant, mode 2, decision digest) on the devnet adapter, bound to the decision: the digest is the one its anchor transaction recorded on the JevDecisionLog, and the job id must be keccak(kind ‖ the decision’s handshake ‖ the sealed reply digest). Refuses (409/422) when the verdict is not the one the anchored answers compose to (only needs_review leaves the choice open), the decision is not anchored, it names another job, the adapter already holds a verdict, or the hook’s job is not Submitted; a complete verdict on a hard-fail record is refused. Also: what moves, who may sign (a registered evaluator), the permissionless expire after the deadline, operator_step (when one is open) and record_template (the operator record a decision would carry). _OPERATOR_RECORD_v1_ writes: { open: true, jobId, decision_id } opens the operator step of a held needs_review job (status awaiting_record; 409 not_needs_review otherwise). { …, operator_record } sends taifoon.operator_decision.v2 { v, chain_id, job_id, tenant, hook, adapter, jev { decision_id, decision_digest, recorded_verdict, anchor_tx, unchanged: true }, operator { verdict, follows_jev, reason, evaluator, decided_at, decided_by: loop-agent | operator }, call { to, data }, money, digest, anchor { tx } }: refused with bad_record (not v2), who_decided (no decided_by), loop_agent_devnet_only (403), operator_only / key_required (401), no_jev_citation (it does not cite the Jev decision it answers), jev_replaced (Jev’s verdict or anchor not quoted unchanged), record_mismatch (not this plan’s job, hook, adapter, verdict, calldata or evaluator), digest_mismatch (sha256 over the key-sorted JSON without digest/anchor does not recompute), anchor_missing / anchor_unreadable / anchor_failed / anchor_mismatch (the anchor transaction’s input is not utf8(v) ‖ digest) / anchor_sender (not sent by the record’s evaluator), already_recorded; accepted → operator_decision { id opdec-<16 hex>, digest, decided_by, verdict, anchor_tx }, then the call. { jobId, confirm: { posted_tx } } reads the postVerdict back (the record’s exact calldata from its evaluator, VerdictPosted) and writes the settle row with jev_decision_id and operator_decision_id; refused with no_record, posted_unreadable, posted_failed, posted_mismatch.

auth.rule: The plan (no open, operator_record or confirm) is open to anyone and keeps nothing. open and confirm need X-API-Key (a relayer key) or x-operator-token. An operator_record needs the credential of who decided: decided_by "operator" = x-operator-token (a person with the operator key); decided_by "loop-agent" = a relayer key, and only on the devnet 36927 (403 loop_agent_devnet_only elsewhere).

tools.name: settle_decided
tools.summary: Name the Jev decision a job ended on: a lane that completed or rejected on Jev’s automatic decision writes its settle row with that decision, proven from the chain.
tools.returns: Send { chainId: 36927, jobId, decision_id, end_tx } on a relayer key (X-API-Key). The layer reads the decision, then its anchor and end_tx in one /v1/chain/tx batch, and writes decided_by "jev" (with decision_id and jev_decision_id) only when: the decision composed complete or reject with auto: true and its verdict_digest recomputes; the anchor succeeded on the JevDecisionLog with exactly this record’s calldata (subject_id, kind_id, digest); the job is the decision’s (about the job itself, or keccak(agent ‖ handshake ‖ sealed reply digest), or — settling through us — a known judge adapter posted this decision’s digest for the job in end_tx, and an adapter that posted another digest refuses); end_tx succeeded and emitted Completed (complete) or Rejected (reject) for this job on a known devnet hook. Refusals: unauthorized (401), bad_input (400), not_auto (409: needs_review is the operator step’s, POST /v1/settle/evaluate), verdict_digest, anchor_mismatch, job_mismatch, end_mismatch (422), unanchored, anchor_unreadable, end_unreadable, verdict_mismatch, already_decided (409: a job has one decision). _SETTLE_HELD_v1_: when end_tx is the job’s Expired on a known devnet hook (the keeper’s hook.expire, or anyone’s after the deadline), the call instead names the Jev decision that HELD the job: jev_decision_id and decision_id are written and decided_by stays null (the deadline ended it), only when the decision composed needs_review or reject and its verdict_digest recomputes (not_held, 409, for a complete), its anchor is this record on the JevDecisionLog, the job is keccak(agent ‖ handshake ‖ sealed reply digest) or the decision’s own subject, end_tx emitted Expired and no Completed or Rejected for the job, and the anchor was mined no later than the expire (anchor_after_end, 422); answers held_by, held_verdict, expired_by. The decision is kept write-once beside the row (settled-by:<job>) and overlaid on every read, so no lifecycle read can drop it. Returns proof[] (each step in words), settlement (the row), cost.

tools.name: settle_ended
tools.summary: Record a V4 job that ended with nobody deciding: the devnet keeper’s claimAutoComplete, finalizeReject or settleStaleDispute, proven from the chain, on the job’s settle row with the machine’s transition id.
tools.returns: On Base 8453 or Arbitrum 42161 (_MAINNET_V4_SETTLE_v1_): send { chainId, jobId } only; the layer reads the job on our V4 hook there (jobs/v4Of), its own logs and the stand-in’s forward of the price, and writes buyer, seller of record, doer (test_doer true when the doer is one of our own addresses), price, premium, fee and fee_to (the treasury the adapter’s FeeForwarded paid, read from the chain), the Settled split and every transaction with its explorer link; the hire flows (the vault-key executor, outside-hire.mjs) post it after their ending and the relayer paths record it themselves; 404 when our V4 hook does not hold the job, 409 before it ended, 503 when a chain read did not complete. With decision_id (_CODE_PASS_FEE_v1_): end_tx may be our evaluator's JudgeAdapter.postVerdict(complete, mode 1) for a code-pass decision; the row is verdict complete, transition complete, source evaluator-leg, decided_by loop-agent. Send { chainId: 36927, jobId, end_tx } on a relayer key (X-API-Key) or x-operator-token. The layer reads end_tx (one /v1/chain/tx read) and writes the row only when it is a successful claimAutoComplete | finalizeReject | settleStaleDispute of this job on a V4 devnet hook (dUSDC, or dGLMR = tenant moonbeam) with the machine’s events (AutoCompleted + Completed + Settled ending 5, or Rejected + Settled ending 3); else not_mined 409, not_v4_hook | not_an_ending | other_job | events 422. The row: verdict complete | reject, transition auto_complete_v4 | finalize_reject_v4 | stale_dispute_v4 (schemas/transitions.json), source keeper when the devnet keeper sent it (else site), decided_by null. Idempotent. Returns transition, verdict, ended_by, hook, tenant, settled { ending, toSeller, toBuyer, toPool, toEvaluator }, proof[], settlement (the row), cost.

tools.name: settle_operator
tools.summary: The operator steps: held needs_review jobs waiting for, or ended by, an operator’s recorded decision — Jev’s decision and the operator’s side by side.
tools.returns: ?status=awaiting_record|recorded|settled&limit=(≤ 50). steps[] newest first: chain_id, job_id, tenant, hook, adapter, status, opened_at, opened_by, deadline, jev { decision_id, digest, recorded_verdict, anchor_tx, anchor_link, decision }, operator { decision_id, digest, decided_by (loop-agent | operator, as recorded), decided_by_now { recorded, now, corrected }, corrections[] (append-only, each with its anchor link), verdict, follows_jev, reason, evaluator, decided_at, anchor_tx, anchor_link, posted_tx, posted_link, record } | null, waits_for, settlement.

tools.name: settle_discover
tools.summary: The settlement watcher: settle rows discovered from the chain with nobody posting — every live V4 line (Base, Arbitrum, the devnet lines) and every x402 network the layer’s payers paid on (Monad, Base), one cursor per lane.
tools.returns: lanes[]: key (v4:<line> | x402:<chain>), lane (v4-hook | x402), chain_id, chain, address (the hook or the USDC), from_block (the deploy block), cursor (the last block read), head, safe_head, confirmations, lag_blocks, lag_s (now − the block time of the cursor), discovered_total (endings or payments found on chain, each once), written_total (rows the watcher wrote first), refused_total, queued, waiting_doer (completed stand-in jobs whose doer payout can still arrive), last_run_at, last_ok_at, last_error, reorgs, found[] (the newest: job or payment tx, block, ended_at, discovered_at, row new | filled | same | waiting | refused, why, lag_s). totals by lane:chain. ?run=1 runs one cycle when none ran in the last 4 minutes (the cron asks every 5).

tools.name: settle_operator__id
tools.summary: One operator step by job id, or one operator decision by its id (opdec-<16 hex>).
tools.returns: job_id, operator_step (the list’s shape, with both decisions and their transaction links) and record { id, accepted_at, anchor { tx, block }, digest_recomputes, record (the taifoon.operator_decision.v2 the layer accepted, unchanged) }; decided_by { recorded (the record’s own label), now (the last correction’s, else the record’s), corrected }; corrections[] oldest first (POST /v1/settle/operator/:id/relabel): id, was, decided_by, reason, corrected_at, corrected_by, accepted_by, digest, digest_recomputes, anchor { tx, block, link }, relabel (the full correction); 404 when neither is kept.

tools.name: settle_operator__id_relabel
tools.summary: Correct who decided a kept operator record, append-only: the record and its anchor never change; the correction is added beside it, citing the record, and is itself digested and anchored on chain.
tools.returns: Send { chainId: 36927, relabel: taifoon.operator_relabel.v1 { v, chain_id, job_id, cites { decision_id (opdec-<16 hex>), digest, anchor_tx } (the kept record), correction { field: "operator.decided_by", was (the label in force), decided_by (loop-agent | operator), reason (≥ 20 characters), corrected_at, corrected_by (loop-agent on a relayer key | operator on the token) }, digest, anchor { tx } } }. digest = sha256 over the key-sorted JSON without digest and anchor; the anchor is a transaction from the cited record’s evaluator whose input is utf8(v) ‖ digest. :id is the record id or its job id. Refusals: bad_relabel (400), key_required (401), relabel_operator_only / loop_agent_devnet_only (403), no_record (404), relabel_mismatch (422: it does not cite this record, or no reason), stale_label (409: was is not the label in force), same_label (409), digest_mismatch (422), anchor_missing / anchor_mismatch / anchor_sender (422), anchor_unreadable / anchor_failed (409). Accepted → { created, correction { id oprel-<16 hex>, was, decided_by, reason, anchor { tx, block, link } }, decided_by { recorded, now }, record_unchanged }; the same correction again answers created false. GET /v1/settle/operator/:id then carries decided_by { recorded, now, corrected } and corrections[].

auth.rule: x-operator-token may correct either way ("loop-agent" only on the devnet 36927). A relayer key (X-API-Key) may only downgrade a record from "operator" to "loop-agent" on the devnet (403 relabel_operator_only otherwise).

(text.summary | data.extract), task?, force_reject?: boolean }. → { ok, schema taifoon.settle.rehearsal.v1, id (rh_<16 hex>), network 36927, devnet true, state (released | refunded | held | failed), read_at, steps[] { step (quote | hire | deliver | grade | release | refund | receipt), tx, events[] (decoded by /v1/chain/tx), from, to, amount { units, symbol, decimals, display }, grade step jev { verdict, checks[] { id, value, p }, record_tx, record_block, decision_id, digest, answers_digest } }, job_id, line { key, symbol, decimals, … }, receipt { legs[] { leg (seller | buyer_refund | venue_fee | our_fee | pool_premium), to, amount, tx, how }, conserved, settle_row }, grade_gate { this_run, gated_by, not_grade_gated[], core }, links { read, core, settle_row, decision, jev_records, explorer } }. 200 ended, 202 held (the dispute window), 400 devnet_only | bad_input, 401 key_required, 429 rate limited, 502 a devnet step failed (the steps so far are returned).

tools.returns: Send ?blocks=n (1–20)[&product=gpu for GPU-gate credit]. call{to,data,amount,symbol,payee,grades}, price, sign{message}, steps[] — transfer, sign, POST judge/credits/key, then judge/credits/confirm with the new key.

tools.name: judge_credits_key
tools.summary: Claim a relayer key for a paid transaction on Base — one key per transaction, only by the wallet that paid.
tools.returns: Send { tx, chainId: 8453, signature }. api_key (shown once), key_prefix, blocks_paid, grades_paid, credit_to, credit{message, then} — sign credit.message and POST judge/credits/confirm with the key to receive the grades. A key bought here holds only the grades paid for. A transfer that reached the vault and does not buy what it names (a plan it does not price exactly, or a sum that is not whole blocks) is held as a claim, once per transaction: 202 { ok: false, code: held_for_claim, claim { id, chain, tx, from, paid, plan_asked, reason, state }, next_step { sign, resend[], as_balance } }; the money stays in the vault. The wallet that paid claims it with the same signature: the same tx again naming what the amount buys, or { tx, chainId, signature, claim: "balance" } → a new key whose prepaid balance is the amount (up to the top-up maximum).

auth.rule: No header credential: the body carries an EIP-191 signature by the wallet that sent the payment (the receipt names it). Without a key a visitor may claim 5 a minute and 40 a day per IP.

tools.name: judge_credits_grid
tools.summary: Pay for grades with settled GRID points: a wallet’s GRID balance, the price in GRID, the caps, and the message to sign.
tools.returns: ?wallet=0x…&product=grade&blocks=1: balance { settled (GridCredit on 3692781), spent, available }, products[] (grade: 15 GRID per 3 grades at the 0.01 USDC peg; gpu listed, not open yet), caps (per wallet per day, network per day), spend { message, nonce, expiry, credit }, steps, earn.

auth.rule: Open. With a relayer key the message to sign credits that key; without one it claims a new key for the wallet.

tools.name: judge_credits_grid
tools.summary: Spend settled GRID on grades.
tools.returns: { wallet, product, blocks, nonce, expiry, signature } → grid_spent, grades_added, grades_left, balance, and api_key (shown once) when a key was claimed. 402 not_enough_grid, 429 wallet_day_cap (no network-wide cap), 403 wallet_refused | bad_signature, 409 nonce_spent | key_claimed.

auth.rule: The body carries the wallet’s EIP-191 signature over the spend message (nonce spent once, expiry ≤ 15 min). With a relayer key or account the grades go to it; with no key or a free key a key is minted for the wallet (one per wallet, ever, shown once). Visitors: 5 a minute, 40 a day.

tools.name: judge_decisions
tools.summary: Every decision the judge made for this layer — pad picks, skill rankings, assembles, grades, study batteries — each with a recomputable digest and its transaction on the devnet JevDecisionLog.
tools.returns: decisions[] newest first (kind, subject, answers with full distributions, confidence_bps, digest, anchor{tx,block,index,status}, genome line) + summary (counts by kind, anchored/pending, the on-chain total). ?kind= filters, ?genome=1 returns the tape frames only. ?ref=<job id> (a whole id: 12582 is the Virtuals ACP v3 job, bitagent:8453:12582 the BitAgent one) or ?subject=<subject_id> [&chain=] returns one subject’s decisions out of the whole ledger, with filter { ref, subject, chain, matched }.

tools.name: judge_decisions__id
tools.summary: One recorded judge decision with its anchors resolved and the calldata a reader recomputes.
tools.returns: decision, recording { networks[] (per network the decision is on: state queued → pending → recorded, both transactions with explorer links, what was paid), record_more }, genome frame, calldata for JevDecisionLog.record, how_to_verify.

tools.name: judge_record_networks
tools.summary: Where a Jev grade may be recorded on chain, and what a record costs there now: one row per network with its chain id, the two logs (JevAnswerLog, JevDecisionLog), whether it is live, and the price of one recorded grade in USDC and in bought grades. The Taifoon devnet is the only free one.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.judge.record-networks.v1 { live[] (the names `record` takes now), networks[] { network, chain_id, name, live, free, logs { answers, decisions, answers_explorer, decisions_explorer } | null, recorder, gas_asset, price { usdc, atomic, credits } | null, cost { usdc, atomic, floored, working } (what the two writes cost the recorder at the gas price now), why (when not live) }, rule, unit, who_pays, use }. A network is live when both logs are deployed and the recorder signs there; a live network with no gas reading, or paused by the operator, is reported not live with why. price = max(a floor, the cost × a margin): never below the cost.

tools.name: judge_decisions__id_record
tools.summary: Put an already-recorded judge decision and its answer record on one more network: { network } is the name or chain id of a live network, or a list (GET /v1/judge/record/networks). Charged once per decision and network: a network already paid for, queued or recorded is queued again at no charge.
tools.returns: 202 { decision_id, digest, recording { requested[], networks[] { network, chain_id, name, state: queued → pending → recorded | failed | held, decision { tx, explorer, block, log }, answers { tx, explorer, block, log }, paid }, held[] { network, reason, message }, paid { by: x402 | credits, lines[], tx, explorer } }, read }. 402 payment_required (no key): grade, record[], network[], total and x402 (the challenge; send the same request again with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE). 402 record_needs_balance (a key with no grades bought in USDC on Base): price and buy. 503 paid_not_recorded (the payment settled and the record could not be written down): retry { tx, until, header }, and the same request with the same PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and X-PAYMENT-RETRY: <settle tx> is served with no new payment. A paid record that fails is queued again at no charge (three tries in all); given up on, bought grades go back to the key, and an x402 payment stays on the decision so this call tries again at no charge. 400 record_network_not_live with live[]. 404 for an unknown decision. This site holds no key of any network: it enqueues jev.record jobs the recorder a Taifoon wallet signs.

auth.rule: The caller pays the record: a customer key is debited in bought grades; with no key the answer is 402 with the x402 challenge for the record. One of the layer’s own keys stays on the layer’s daily budget. The devnet is free.

tools.name: judge_decisions__id_base
tools.summary: Alias of POST /v1/judge/decisions/:id/record with network "base": put an already-recorded judge decision and its answer record on Base (JevDecisionLog + JevAnswerLog, chain 8453), signed by the recorder a Taifoon wallet, the only address JevAnswerLog trusts on Base.
tools.returns: As judge/decisions/:id/record, plus the older fields anchor_base{status queued → pending → ok, job_key} and answers{digest, anchor_base}. Idempotent.

auth.rule: The older name of POST judge/decisions/:id/record { network: "base" }; the same payment rule.

tools.name: judge_answers

tools.name: grid_join

tools.name: grid_join
tools.summary: Bring a resource to the Grid in one request: the oracle probes it every hour and pays GRID for measured work.
tools.returns: Send { kind: rpc|storage|gpu|fpga|tee, chainId (rpc), endpoint, owner (0x wallet), ref? }. The pool is Taifoon's side: a resource that names none works for the Taifoon founding pool (pool_source: default); an old node that still sends pool keeps it. The accepted resource and what it earns per healthy probe; nothing is paid for a submission, only for probes that pass.

auth.rule: Open by design (a provider joins from a shell script). _ROLES_v1_: with the owner’s switch ROLE_GRID_JOIN_KEY on, joining needs a member key (401 without one).

tools.name: grid_heartbeat
tools.summary: A taifoon-node's signed heartbeat, every 5 minutes: what the box offers now (capacity per kind), its payout election, and the usage receipts of the work it ran.
tools.returns: { ok, node (its did), stored, why, today { slots, uptime_bps, capacity, reported } , work (where its placements are) }. Uptime is counted in 5-minute slots; the layer's own metering stays the authority for what was served.

auth.rule: No key: the body is an ed25519 envelope (taifoon.heartbeat/v1) signed by the node's own key (did:taifoon), and the signature is the authority. A node keeps one owner a day; a replayed seq is not counted.

tools.name: grid_work
tools.summary: The work coord placed on a node: outlet jobs and Taifoon buyers' work arrive here, never through the contributor's own outlet accounts.
tools.returns: ?node=did:taifoon:z… → { node, placements[] { id, product, unit, outlet_key, run, until }, why } — an empty list says why (no placement routes to community nodes yet).

tools.returns: kinds[] { kind, earnsToday, usable, multiplier, gridPerDay, usdcPerDay, why } and the rule; 1 GRID is one cent of service. attribution: the one model of who did and brought how much for a UTC day (?day=YYYYMMDD, default today; ?owner=0x… or ?node=did:… for yours): per node capacity, uptime_bps, units per product and per outlet/buyer, revenue (USDC + GRID, nano-USDC), cost, TSUL split 70/20/10, payout (GRID full rate or cash at the TSUL rate), community totals, outlets read back, and reconcile { ok: Σ node revenue + Taifoon's leg = Σ outlet earnings + Σ buyer debits }.

tools.returns: pools[] { pool, name, fee_bps, members, resources by kind, accrued, the pool’s leg } and the rule.

tools.summary: My GRID: a wallet’s measured ledger, what was settled on Taifoon mainnet, what is pending, and its balance.
tools.returns: ?wallet=0x… → wallet { ledger, settled, pending, balance }, today’s cap and what is left of it, the next settlement run, the contract.

tools.name: grid_wanted
tools.summary: Where the Grid is short: chains and kinds ranked by demand, with the bootstrap budget and the settlement rule.
tools.returns: chains[], pools per kind, the referral share, settlement { status, contract, everyHours, bootstrap }.

tools.name: grid_leaderboard
tools.summary: Every provider on the Grid, their resources and measured GRID.

tools.name: grid_hire
tools.summary: Hire measured resources from the Grid — a quote with the usable providers and the measurement as evidence.
tools.returns: ?kind=rpc|gpu|fpga|storage|ip&units=&hours=. The quote at the live rate, the providers offered (endpoint, owner wallet when one is on record, trust, health, latency, last probe), evidence { digest, det, facts, gaps } — the measurement pack a resource job seals — and settlement.status NOT_DEPLOYED with the reason (record the hire with a wallet to get a plan).

tools.name: grid_hire
tools.summary: Record a Grid hire and, when both sides have wallets, plan its settlement on the assurance hook.
tools.returns: Send { kind, units?, hours?, hirer (0x wallet or agent id), note? }. The recorded intent, the same quote and evidence, and settlement { status: PLANNED, plan } when the hirer is a wallet and an offered provider has one: a kind:resource plan on Base (seller = the provider’s wallet, price = the quote in USDC, evidence = the measurement digest; approve-deposit → approve → fundJob → submit → complete, each with its signer). Otherwise NOT_DEPLOYED with the exact reason.

auth.rule: Recording an intent moves the rate, so it needs a key; the recorded hirer is tagged with the key. GET quotes stay open.

tools.name: judge_compose
tools.summary: RUBRIC_v2 — the judge as a pipeline: code proves the facts, Jev answers four atomic questions, code composes the verdict spec-led (complete: spec_met ≥ 0.85 and unsupported_claim ≤ 0.2 counting only what code did not verify; reject: spec_met ≤ 0.40 or unsupported_claim ≥ 0.70; ending recorded, never deciding alone), one receipt. Subjects also { task, delivery }, and on any of six networks (Base, Arbitrum, Arc, Robinhood, Monad, Solana) { x402: { network, tx, resource?, payTo?, task?, delivery } } (an x402 hire, its settlement read on its own network) and { erc8183: { chainId, contract, jobId, txs[], delivery? } } (an ERC-8183 or assurance-hook job by its lifecycle transactions); coverage per network: GET /v1/capabilities?view=jev. No key and no free grade left: pay this one grade with x402 (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE; USDC on Base, Arbitrum, Arc or Monad, or USDG on Robinhood: the 402 lists each network). `record` (none by default) also writes the decision and its answers on chain: devnet (free), base, or any live network of GET /v1/judge/record/networks by name or chain id, or a list; the caller pays the record (with no key: one x402 challenge for the record plus the grade when no free grade is left, itemised as grade, record, network; a key: debited in bought grades), it is queued only after the payment, and the answer carries recording.networks[] with the queue state and then both transactions. A payment that settled and bought nothing (Jev did not answer) is not lost: the failure carries retry { tx, until, header } and the same request sent again within 24 hours with the same PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and X-PAYMENT-RETRY: <settle tx> is served once with no new payment (retry.served). RUBRIC_v1 (below) is the history.
tools.returns: Send { handshake_id } | { jobId, chainId? } | { olas } | { state }, price_usdc?, key? (a 32-byte assurance-hook jobId needs chainId). A hard fail (nothing delivered, a failed deterministic check) is a reject with no judge call. Otherwise one battery call answers the four questions that decide the verdict, spec_met, unsupported_claim, ending and cheat_shaped, on the evidence pack (scope_ok and severity stay in the rubric and its hash, reported as not_asked), and the verdict is composed under THRESHOLDS_v2 (complete only when spec met ≥ 0.85 and unsupported ≤ 0.2; reject when spec met ≤ 0.40 or unsupported ≥ 0.70; ending recorded, never deciding; cheat-shaped ≥ 0.5 escalates; auto-complete capped at 50 USDC). Returns receipt { rubricHash, stateHash, facts, answers, verdict, auto, reasons, receiptHash } and the recorded decision (v2, anchored). The on-chain judge is the appeal, not the hot path. Two-step on your own TypeSafe credential (no free grade spent): mode:"prepare" → facts (a hard fail is final there), jev { state: the exact text, questions: RUBRIC_v2 in the TypeSafe node schema }, prepare_digest = sha256(compose.prepare.v1, subject, rubricHash, text); ask with your node (connection direct, whole distribution), then mode:"answers" { answers, model, answered_by: n8n-typesafe, prepare_digest, execution_id? } with X-API-Key → 409 on a hard fail or a changed digest, 400 on a missing/malformed answer; otherwise composed, recorded (answers_source caller-credential) and anchored. mode:"prepare" with decide_pass { decisive: [check ids] }, record: "devnet" and X-API-Key (_CODE_PASS_FEE_v1_, devnet only): when code alone passes the delivery (every check made passed, every decisive check made), the layer records ONE code-pass decision (answers [], model det:<class>, complete, auto; Jev not asked) and returns it as decision (code_pass: true), else code_pass: false with code_pass_why; POST /v1/settle { via: us, verdict: complete, decision_id } then plans postVerdict(1, mode 1), which earns the evaluator fee. After the three free grades: 402 with x402 (the per-grade challenge, also in the PAYMENT-REQUIRED header: resend the same request with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE) and pay { kind: pay-to-key, chainId: 8453, token, payee, amount, grades, quote, claim, confirm, steps }: pay one block in USDC on Base and claim a key with the same transaction (judge/credits/key).

auth.rule: mode:answers requires the relayer key; the other modes take one optionally.

tools.name: market_candles
tools.summary: The class market.candles: OHLCV bars of BTC, ETH, SOL or the CME micro futures NQ, ES, YM (15s, 1m, 5m, 1h) from the Taifoon venue tape, past windows only, with a sha256 digest and the class check made on the answer.
tools.returns: Query market, tf, from, to (unix s; to at least 120 s before now; at most 1,000 bars). class, market, tf, from, to, bars, candles[{ t, o, h, l, c, v }], digest (sha256 over "t,o,h,l,c,v" lines), sealed, source, feed, check { pass, checks { digest_ok, replay_equal, on_grid, past_only, continuity, close_in_band (crypto only) }, reference (Chainlink on Base, crypto) }, price { per_call_grid, per_call_usdc, cost_basis }, tsul { fee_bps 49, on_this_call_usdc, split }, payment { network, settlement, payer }. 402 without payment, 400 bad_input (nothing settled), 429 rate_limited (nothing settled), 502 when the tape did not answer after payment.

auth.rule: Paid per call with x402: exact USDC on Base to the vault (0.005 USDC). Without a payment header the answer is HTTP 402 with the challenge (PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and body, bazaar extension); a paying caller is held to 20 calls a minute and the route to 120 a minute for everyone.

A buy venue narrows the asks to those its matches take, a sell venue the bids. 400 bad_param for a state that is not one.

auth.rule: Open: no key needed; a key sent is passed on, never required.

tools.summary: The models buyers want that no supplier we deliver serves at a price that wins (_WANTED_SUPPLY_v1_), read only: per model and venue the demand (sessions or calls, per day in USD), the state (wanted: supply · wanted: supply with web search · wanted: cheaper supply · wanted: weights unnamed) with its next step, the price a supplier is paid at the one price rule, and the instructions to serve it: the weights, the VRAM per quantization, vLLM and SGLang flags, the join through the Grid door, how verification checks it, and whether our own GPU fits it. auth.rule: Open: no key needed; a key sent is passed on, never required.

tools.summary: The task document and the unsigned approve + request calls for a coordination mech request. Nothing signs here.

tools.name: x402_class__class
tools.summary: The resale wall of one class: an admitted outside seller answers your input, you pay with x402, Jev grades the answer after, and the seller is paid from your payment (_RESALE_WALL_v1_). inference.metered (and the venue classes chat.converse, text.generate, reason.general) is served by the Taifoon GPU instead (_GPU_X402_WALL_v1_): an OpenAI chat completion { messages, max_tokens } for 0.001 USDC per request of up to 5,000 tokens, served by taifoon.gpu.
tools.returns: Send { input } (the class’s input, e.g. mcp.digest { text, algorithm }, market.price { symbol }); the wall itself (www.taifoon.io/api/coordination/x402/class/{class}) also takes GET with the input as query parameters. Without a payment: 402 with the x402 challenge (the price outside buyers already pay for the class, at least 0.002 USDC). With PAYMENT-SIGNATURE: 200 { ok, class, seller, answer, checks, sale { id, payment_tx, network, price_units, fee_units, seller_share_units } } once the answer passed (the payment settles only then); 503 not_delivered when no seller’s answer passed (nothing charged); 409 walls_not_open while the wall takes no payment (with the reason); 404 for a class with no wall (GET /v1/venues?view=pipeline lists them).

auth.rule: Open: a buyer pays with x402 (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE). _TEE_X402_WALL_v1_: tee.typed.compile (and compute.attested) also takes X-API-Key, and the Taifoon TDX enclave debits the compile unit from that key’s one balance; the operator token with x-internal-walk: 1 runs a product wall’s path without a payment (nothing settles).

tools.name: x402_class__class
tools.summary: The resale wall of one class, probed with GET: the x402 challenge (PAYMENT-REQUIRED) without a body, or the answer with the input as query parameters and a payment (_X402_GET_WALL_v1_).
tools.returns: Without a payment: 402 with the x402 challenge, the same shape and headers as POST (code payment_required, x402.accepts[] { scheme, network, amount, asset, pay_to }). With PAYMENT-SIGNATURE and the input as query parameters (?text=…, ?symbol=…): the answer, as POST gives it. 404 for a class with no open wall.

auth.rule: Open: a buyer pays with x402 (PAYMENT-SIGNATURE). _TEE_X402_WALL_v1_: tee.typed.compile (and compute.attested) also takes X-API-Key, and the Taifoon TDX enclave debits the compile unit from that key’s one balance; the operator token with x-internal-walk: 1 runs a product wall’s path without a payment (nothing settles).

tools.name: gw_resources
tools.summary: The resources the drop-in gateways serve: point a stock MCP client at the resource’s gateway URL instead of its own endpoint, and every call is forwarded unchanged, recorded as a λ step and counted (_LAMBDA_GW_MCP_v1_).
tools.returns: gateways { mcp, a2a, rpc, x402, olas, virtuals: { path, status live | design } }, count, resources[] { id (mcp:<slug>), slug, kind, protocol, endpoint (where the call is forwarded), url (https://coord.taifoon.dev/gw/mcp/<slug>), classes[], tools[], card, price { amount, unit, rule, routing_fee { usdc_per_call, free_calls_per_key_day, free_calls_per_visitor_day, past_allowance } } }, how. The gateway itself is not a /v1 operation: it speaks the resource’s own protocol at /gw/mcp/{slug} (POST, GET, DELETE; Streamable HTTP), with visitors held to 60 calls a minute and 2,000 a day. The routing fee (_GW_FEE_v1_): free up to 100 calls a day without a key and 1,000 a day per key (both gateways together), then 0.001 USDC a call, debited from the key’s gateway credit (GET /v1/judge/credits?product=gateway) or paid with x402 by a caller without a key; past the allowance with neither, HTTP 402 naming how to pay (x-taifoon-fee and x-taifoon-allowance say which lane a call took).
