_AGENT_KIND_v1_), fees[] (every fee path: rule, status, earned), revenue { rule, all_time, today, by_path[] { path, provable, all_time, today, payments }, first_outside { path, usdc, chain, tx, at, block } | null, outside_payments, unknown, scanner { rule, read_at, age_s, outside { all_time_usd, d7_usd, today_usd, payments, payers, by_product_network[] { product x402 | v4_fee | bridge_share | direct, network, usd, payments }, first { chain, product, usd, payer, tx, at, link } | null, series_daily[] }, ours { usd, payments }, unresolved { usd, payments }, networks { <chain>: { ok, lag_blocks, error } } } | null (the chain’s own count of every stablecoin transfer into our payee on Base, Arbitrum One, Arc, Robinhood Chain and Monad, every 30 min; _REVENUE_SCAN_v1_) } (outside money that landed with our payee, split by the paying wallet; devnet never counts; _OUTSIDE_REVENUE_v1_), needs_yes[], rows[] (the flat form: metric, day, chain, whose, provable, value, unit, labels, source), paid_funnel { schema taifoon.paid_funnel.v1, day, stages (challenged, paid, refused_payment, refused_input, not_delivered, upstream_error, settled), whose (outside, ours, unknown), totals, totals_by_whose, routes[] { product, stages, by_whose { outside, ours, unknown } }, rule } | null (every paid wall's funnel of the day, counted through the one paid path, by product and by the paying wallet; null when the store did not answer; _PAID_FUNNEL_v1_), sources { errors, read_at (the kept read, one per instance, at most 3 min old when answered), per_answer_read_at + per_answer (the access log and the gateway counters, read on every answer, so a later answer never carries fewer calls or steps; tools.name: network
tools.summary: The network, live: what the hourly auto-connect run found — the seller chooseSeller picks per job class and whether it answered a handshake-level call through the gateway, latency, the grid (warmbed rotation health per chain), the cross-chain routes with a live quote — and the gateway’s λ steps today. No customer data (_AUTOCONNECT_v1_).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.network.v1, at, age_s, stale, sellers { classes, online, median_latency_ms, p90_latency_ms }, chains_healthy, routes_ok, steps_recorded, classes[] { class, seller { host, kind }, online, latency_ms, tools, method, via, step }, chains[] { chain, name, ok, usable, endpoints, head, latency_ms, step }, routes[] { from, to, token, amount_usdc, fee_usdc, fee_rule, expected_received_usdc, eta_s, via, ok, step }, gateway_today { day, steps, by_kind }, pools (the same live read as /v1/pools/state?chain=all, compact: score, chains[], pools[] { chain_id, address, system, tenant, asset, tvl, cover_capacity, encumbered, premium_rate, open_for_deposits, deposits_on_chain, last_covered_job, unread[] }; { unread, why } when the read failed), rules. 404 until the first run (pools still answered).

tools.name: network
tools.summary: Publish the network snapshot (the hourly auto-connect run).
tools.returns: 201 { published_at, sellers, chains_healthy, routes_ok, steps_recorded }; only the documented fields are kept.

auth.rule: Only the layer’s own auto-connect key (403 ours_only otherwise).

tools.name: deals__id_bid
tools.summary: Bid on one deal of the deal engine (_DEAL_BID_v1_, lang/genie/deal-bid.mjs): without auth the door answers the unsigned plan, the bid row and the EIP-3009 transfer of the deal's list price to the sale vault the buyer signs; with the signed auth it checks the bid against that plan and writes it to the engine's bid envelope. Nothing is signed or sent here; the engine settles only a graded delivery (deal-engine.cue `sale`).
tools.returns: Without auth: 200 { ok, plan { schema taifoon.deal.bid-plan.v1, rule, bid { id, category, class, venue_in, buyer, max_units, deal, input, door }, requirements { scheme, network, amount, payTo, asset }, sign { domain, primaryType, types, message { from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, nonce } } } }: sign `sign` and send the same body with auth { payload { x402Version, payload { signature, authorization } }, requirements }. With auth: 202 { ok, bid { id, deal, buyer }, order_key }: the bid is on the engine's envelope (the engine's sale mode decides whether it is sold). 404 no_deal; 422 not_priced | no_buyer | bad_bid_id | no_input | input_too_big | no_network | no_pay_token | no_vault | auth_invalid | auth_unbound; 503 pipe_unavailable (nothing was written).

auth.rule: The buyer's signed payment authorisation is what pays; a key spends its own budget, a visitor may plan 10 bids a minute and 200 a day per IP.

tools.name: deals_delivery_read
tools.summary: The buyer reads the delivery of its bid (_DEAL_DELIVERY_v1_, lang/genie/deal-bid.mjs readPlanOf, readOf): without a signature the door answers the typed message to sign; with the buyer's signature it answers the delivery the engine handed back, for 30 days after it arrived.
tools.returns: Without signature: 200 { ok, schema taifoon.deal.delivery-read.v1, sign { domain, primaryType, types, message { buyer, bid, validBefore } } }: sign it and send the same body with valid_before and signature. With signature: 200 { ok, delivery { bid, deal, sale_key, class, content, at } }. 404 no_delivery (not handed over yet, or past its keep); 403 not_buyer; 422 read_invalid | read_expired; 503 store_unavailable.

auth.rule: Keyless: the authority is the buyer's signature. An EIP-712 DeliveryRead (domain Taifoon Deal Delivery v1, no chainId) over { buyer, bid, validBefore } recovered to the buyer; validBefore at most 300 s ahead. A visitor may read 10 times a minute and 200 a day per IP.

tools.name: demands
tools.summary: Post what a buyer agent needs, not whom to hire: in words ({ need }) or as a job of a class the auto-match loop runs (mcp.digest, a2a.json_normalize, stats.describe, chat.word_count, credential.verify.celo, agentkit.erc20_transfer, transfer.attest.cctp, typed.compile, tee.typed.compile). Words are mapped to a class by deterministic rules and the catalogue, never a model (_DEMAND_NEED_v1_). The layer’s loop claims the demand, picks the seller with SELLER_CHOICE_v3, hires it through the broker, checks the reply by code (the class DET, no Jev) and settles through the layer on the devnet 36927 (_DEMAND_INTAKE_v1_, _AUTOMATCH_v1_).
tools.returns: _RESALE_CATALOG_v1_: { catalog_id } buys a GET /v1/catalog buy_now entry: the loop hires that seller first, class defaults to its first auto class, price_units to our price for it, and the demand keeps catalog { id, seller, fee_bps, seller_usdc, fee_usdc, our_usdc } (422 not_buyable for any other entry: its buy names POST /v1/handshake). { seller } (a listing id ls_… or a seller key from GET /v1/catalog or GET /v1/listings) is a seller-named devnet demand: that seller’s catalogue entry, the same rules (422 no_such_seller when the catalogue has none). { ref } (the agent a Studio surface picked, by any id it shows: a map, tree, listing or catalogue id, or a seller key) is read on the server as its catalogue entry (web lib/pick-seller), the same rules; the answer (the dry run too) names it as picked { ref, via, catalog_id, seller }, a kept one links to its commerce page (links.commerce); 422 ref_unknown (no listing, class worker or card endpoint names it), ref_malformed, ref_with_seller (send ref, seller or catalog_id, one of them). _SELL_CALLS_v1_: { seller: <a catalogue ref of GET /v1/sell/calls>, call: <n>, input, pay: "x402" } buys that call: its 402 charges the call's price_units, 409 with the call answer's why while the seller's buy path is not open, 422 no_such_call (no call n) or sell_call_paid (sent without pay or as a dry run); nothing is kept before the payment settles, and the kept demand carries class (the call's) and catalog { id (the ref), seller, venue, only true, offering, class, call, seller_units, price_units, rule }: the loop hires only that seller. Send { class, input (the class’s input, GET /v1/classes) } or { need: "the work in words", class? }, with price_units? (dUSDC units, default 50000), chainId? (36927 only), buyer_label?, dry_run? (true: answer the mapping and cover_preview, keep nothing; a dry run has its own budget of 30 a minute and 1000 a day per visitor and never spends one of the 20 kept demands. cover_preview { quote_only, source POST /v1/pools/quote, seller_of_record, pool (a vault only when the quote guarantees cover, else null), covered, premium, premium_ratio, premium_label, deposit, deposit_rung, token, hook, factory, why[], settles_with } or { unread, why }: which pool would cover the job and at what premium, read from the one source of hire terms; the loop’s hires still name no pool (_COVER_PREVIEW_v1_)) → 201 { demand { schema taifoon.demand.v1, id dm_…, state open, class, input, need?, chainId, price_units, created_at, events[] }, resolved? { class, input, how, candidates }, read }. 422 names the classes, what in the input does not fit, or (for a need) code no_class | ambiguous | incomplete with candidates[] { class, title, intent_hits, catalogue_overlap, input, missing, needs, example }: resend with class.

auth.rule: A relayer key spends its own budget; without one a visitor may open 3 a minute and 20 a day per IP.

tools.name: demands
tools.summary: Demands, newest first, each with every step the auto-match loop wrote on it (_DEMAND_INTAKE_v1_).
tools.returns: ?state=open|claimed|matched|hired|graded|settling|settled|unmatched|failed|cancelled &limit= (1–200). demands[] { id, state, class, input, chainId, price_units, seller, handshake_id, job_id, grade, ending, events[] { at, state, by, note?, data? } }, classes.

tools.name: demands__id

tools.name: judge_evidence_olas__requestId
tools.summary: The evidence pack for one Olas Mech marketplace request on Base — the public prompt, tool, mech, fee and response.
tools.returns: facts[], gaps[] (a forecast’s outcome is named as not known), state (text ready for the judge), responseDigest (sha256 of the response), the request and delivery transactions, and the grade call to make.

tools.name: judge_evidence__chain__jobId
tools.summary: The evidence Jev reads about one job the observatory keys — an ERC-8183 / memo-ACP job, an extra deployment’s job, or an assurance-hook job by its 32-byte id (the layer’s hook or Moonbeam ACP’s): task, price, parties, the timeline with the deadline, how it ended, the seller’s record and this buyer’s history with this seller, plus what is not known.
tools.returns: facts[] (label, value), gaps[] and state (text ready for POST /v1/judge/compose). A hook job adds lane:"hook", hook { address, tenant, name } and the hook’s own lines: premium, the seller’s deposit, the cover (pool and cap), the challenge window and the sealed evidence digest. A 32-byte id is read on the chain in the path, and the observatory’s row must be on that chain (?hook=0x… also pins the hook). Facts only: no party is credited with a claim it did not make on chain.

tools.name: judge_trace__chain__jobId
tools.summary: The on-chain judge result, live: every ERC-8183 event of a job with its transaction and explorer link, the deterministic ending, and Jev’s three-field answer beside it.
tools.returns: events[] (name, block, tx, explorer_tx, explorer_log, actor) read from the chain; det {value, basis}; jev {asked: {state_summary, question, options}, answer: {value, probabilities, confidence}, agree_with_det, abstained} from the recorded study, or null when the job was not in it. Base (8453) today.

tools.name: judge_grade
tools.summary: Grade up to 4 items with ONE calibrated call — each item’s full distribution kept.
tools.returns: Send { items: [ { id, state } | { id, handshake_id } | { id, jobId, chainId? } ], question?, options?, key? }. An item is text to judge, or a SUBJECT the layer resolves to its evidence pack itself — a dispatched handshake (the offer, how it was delivered, the reply that came back with its keccak digest) or a job the observatory keys (the ledger pack: a Base ERC-8183 / memo-ACP job, or an assurance-hook job by its 32-byte id with chainId). One battery call on your own TypeSafe key returns per item: value, probabilities, confidence, the lifecycle ending it maps to, the grade digest, and what was read (chars, cut, sha256, gaps); the decision recorded for the call is decision.v2, whose digest covers the input. A REF verdict never produces a cheat.

auth.rule: Runs on your own TypeSafe key (body.key, forwarded, never stored); without one: 403 byo_key — Taifoon's grade is /v1/judge/compose.

tools.name: judge_batch
tools.summary: Record a batch-judge outcome for the coordination layer (relayer key required).
tools.returns: Send the aggregated batch { jobId, verdict, counts, failFraction, threshold, items[] } with X-API-Key (the relayer credential); 401 without a valid key, because hire/lifecycle shows the record as grading. Stored with a TTL (ttlDays, default 30), expired rows pruned. The layer holds no key and signs nothing — it records the calibrated outcome + every item’s distribution so the batch job settles from an auditable record.

tools.name: judge_batch
tools.summary: Read a recorded batch-judge outcome.
tools.returns: GET ?jobId= — the stored batch verdict, counts, digest and per-item distributions, or 404 if none/expired.

tools.name: desk_chains
tools.summary: The Chain Desk's chains (_DESK_API_v1_): every chain the desk serves with its family (evm, tron, substrate), CAIP-2 id, finality rule, sources and health, and what a desk should do now.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.chains.v1 { chains[] { key, chain_id, name, family, caip2, native { symbol, decimals }, finality { type, name, rule }, confirm_depth, lambda, sources { count, hosts }, health { state ok | slow | stalled | halted | no_signal, recommendation, why, block_age_s, reading_age_s, block_time_s, tip, sources, notes[], clock_state }, recommendation keep_open | watch | hold_credits | pause }, counts, clock { at, read }, rule, read_at }. Health is the coordination clock's (GET /v1/clock): a reading older than max(120 s, 10·block time) is no_signal and hold_credits (fail closed); the tip block's age when read: stalled > max(300, 20·bt), slow > max(60, 6·bt); tip sources that disagree are a note.

tools.name: desk_deposit__chain__tx
tools.summary: One transaction as a deposit: CREDIT, WAIT or REJECT with the reason, the common deposit records (taifoon.deposit.v1) and the evidence; fail closed (unreadable is WAIT).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.deposit.v1 { chain (CAIP-2), chain_id, tx, address, verdict CREDIT | WAIT | REJECT, reason, status success | reverted | pending | not_found | unreadable, records[] taifoon.deposit.v1 { schema, chain, chain_id, tx, position { event | output | extrinsic+event }, from, to, asset { kind native | token, id, symbol?, decimals? }, amount (integer base units), block { number, hash }, finality { type, name, final, final_block? }, level seen | confirmed | final | proven, proof? { superroot, batch_id, checks } }, evidence { block, heads { head, final }, lambda, proof? (EVM: the /v1/proof/tx answer; a final transfer is proven when it binds the block) }, health, finality, how, read_at }. {chain}: a chain id, CAIP-2 id or name (tron, acala, astar, hydration); {tx}: EVM 0x hash, Tron 64 hex, substrate <block>-<extrinsic index>. 404 chain_not_served; 501 family_not_read for a chain only a data lambda names (ton).

tools.name: desk_deposits__chain__address
tools.summary: The deposits to an address over a block window, as common deposit records with their level (EVM and Tron tokens up to 2,000 blocks a call).
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.deposits.v1 { chain, chain_id, address, window { from, to }, heads { head, final }, coverage { token { read, from, to, why? }, native { read, from, to, why? } }, level, deposits[] taifoon.deposit.v1, count, cost { calls }, finality, how, read_at }. Tokens: Transfer logs whose recipient topic is the address (EVM, TRC-20); native: block bodies (EVM, at most 100 blocks; TRX TransferContract, 30); substrate: balances.Transfer, tokens.Transfer, assets.Transferred from System.Events (100 blocks). Internal transfers are not read. 400 bad_param for a window past the cap; 503 unreadable with retry_after_seconds.

tools.name: desk_withdrawal__chain_preflight
tools.summary: May a withdrawal go out now: SEND or HOLD with the reason and the best node (the rotation's nodes asked their head now). Nothing is broadcast.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.preflight.v1 { chain, chain_id, verdict SEND | HOLD, reason, best_node { url, host, head, ms } | null, nodes[] { host, head, ms }, asked, health (as desk/chains), note, read_at }. HOLD while the chain's health says hold_credits or pause (an old clock reading included), or when no node answered.

tools.name: desk_withdrawal__chain__tx_receipt
tools.summary: A sent withdrawal: DELIVERED once it succeeded in a final block, else NOT_YET (terminal when it reverted), with the proof link.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.receipt.v1 { chain, chain_id, tx, verdict DELIVERED | NOT_YET, reason, terminal, status, block, final, proof (EVM: the /v1/proof/tx link; null elsewhere), finality, read_at }.

tools.name: desk_finality_stream
tools.summary: The desk_finality lane of /v1/stream on its own connection (the same events, named as before). Server-sent events of the desk chains' finality: finalized each time a chain's final block moves, halt and resume from its health (fail closed); every event id is the resume cursor.
tools.returns: text/event-stream. hello { chains[], unknown, resumed, max_connection_ms }; finalized { chain, chain_id, key, final_block, block_hash, rule, finality_type, finality_name, superroot? { root, batch_id } }; halt { chain, key, state, why } (no_signal, stalled, halted, or heads unreadable three times); resume { chain, key, state, why }. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID (or ?last_event_id=): nothing already sent is sent again. retry 3000, a comment every 15 s, at most 10 minutes per connection.

tools.name: desk_deposits_stream
tools.summary: The desk_deposits lane of /v1/stream on its own connection (the same events, named as before). Server-sent events of the deposits to watched addresses: each transfer once per level it reaches (seen, confirmed, final), resumable by Last-Event-ID.
tools.returns: text/event-stream. hello { chains[] { key, chain, addresses, every_ms }, unknown, level, since, resumed }; deposit { record taifoon.deposit.v1 } once per level change (dedupe by tx + position + level); cursor { chain, key, scanned_to, head, final, sent, pending } after each fully sent tick, its id the resume cursor; lag { chain, key, why } when a chain could not be read. Between two cursors a reconnect may repeat a deposit at the same level, never skip one. retry 3000, a comment every 15 s, 10 minutes per connection.

tools.name: desk_lambdas
tools.summary: The deposit lambda registry: the built-in lambdas (evm, tron, substrate) and the third-party manifests (data only), each with its family, chains, finality, hash and whether a reader exists.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.lambdas.v1 { lambdas[] { schema taifoon.desk.lambda.v1, id, name, family, chains[] (CAIP-2), match, finality { type, name }, reader, author, needs?, source?, origin built-in | registered, reads, hash }, count, readers[], refused[] { file, problems[] }, register { schema, what, how, example }, read_at }. A lambda with reads:false is data only: its chains answer 501 family_not_read with its needs.

tools.name: desk_proof_transfer__chain__tx
tools.summary: Membership proof of one EVM transaction (_DESK_PROOFS_v1_): it is in a final block under the superroot, who signed it, and exactly which ERC-20 transfers it moved; the bundle verifies offline.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.proof.transfer.v1 { verdict INCLUDED, chain (CAIP-2), tx, block, sender (recovered from the signature; an OP deposit names its sender; null for a system transaction), statement, transfers[] { block, tx_index, log, token, from, to, amount }, note? (a transfer's from differs from the signer), check { ok, steps[] { step, ok, detail }, superroot, batch_id, sender }, bundle { header (RLP), link_headers[] (up to the anchored block when the tree does not hold the block itself), transaction (raw), transaction_path[], receipt (EIP-2718), receipt_path[], anchor (the /v1/proof/blocks answer of the anchored block) }, verify }. Every bundle passes its own check before it is served: 502 proof_check_failed otherwise. 409 not_final_yet above the chain's final head; 501 header_layout_unknown for a chain whose header the encoder cannot rebuild; 501 proof_family_not_built for Tron and Polkadot chains.

tools.name: desk_proof_transfers__chain__address
tools.summary: Completeness proof over final blocks (_DESK_PROOFS_v1_): every ERC-20 transfer to (in) or from (out) an address in a range, and a proof there is no other; NONE proves absence.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.proof.transfers.v1 { verdict COMPLETE | NONE, chain, statement { address, direction, token, from, to (the last block covered) }, asked { from, to }, next_from (when one answer's receipt budget ended the proof early), claim, transfers[], check { ok, steps[], superroot, batch_id, blocks, bloom_clear, receipts_rebuilt, found }, bundle { headers[] (RLP, from up to the anchored block, linked by parentHash), receipts { block: [EIP-2718 receipts] } for every block whose logs bloom may match, anchor }, verify, limits }. A block is cleared by its bloom (no false negatives) or by its full receipt list rebuilt to receiptsRoot. At most 512 blocks a call; on busy chains about 20 Base blocks fit one answer (8 MB of receipts).

tools.name: desk_proof_account__chain__address
tools.summary: State proof of an account at a final block (_DESK_PROOFS_v1_): its nonce and native balance, and one ERC-20 balance by its slot; an address with no account is proven absent.
tools.returns: schema taifoon.desk.proof.account.v1 { verdict PRESENT | ABSENT, chain, address, block, account { nonce, balance, contract } | null, token_balance? { token, slot, balance }, statement, use, check { ok, steps[], superroot, batch_id }, bundle { header, account_proof[], storage? { token, slot, key, token_account_proof[], proof[], value }, anchor }, verify }. 503 state_unread when no endpoint serves eth_getProof for the block.

tools.name: desk_metrics
tools.summary: The Chain Desk's state per chain in the Prometheus text format (_DESK_METRICS_v1_), to scrape into an exchange's own monitoring; ?format=json for JSON.
tools.returns: text/plain; version=0.0.4: taifoon_chain_desk_clock_read, taifoon_chain_desk_open, _recommendation{recommendation}, _state{state}, _block_age_seconds, _reading_age_seconds, _tip_block, _sources, _tip_sources, each labelled chain, caip2, name, family. ?format=json: schema taifoon.desk.metrics.v1 { clock_read, chains[] { key, caip2, family, state, recommendation, block_age_s, reading_age_s, tip, sources }, read_at }.

tools.name: sma_ask
tools.summary: Show Me Around ++ the helpdesk (_SMA_HELPDESK_v1_, lang/cue/sma-helpdesk.cue): one question about one product → a case. The product's graph answers first (free, measured); an unknown is routed to a nominated expert, the tenant's agent or a person; every answer is graded before it is settled as one sma.case line (0.10 USDC above the free allowance of 20 a day per key; legs provider 70 · graders 20 · ecosystem 10); the trail is sealed under the tenant's topic helpdesk.<name>, read by nobody but the tenant.
tools.returns: schema sma.case.v1: { case { id case_<16hex>, tenant, product, channel, state asked | routed | answered | escalated, asked_by key:<24hex>, route graph | community | specialist | agent | person }, words? (the answer, when the graph or an agent answered now), fix? { node, confidence }, unknown? (recorded with its evidence; the case stays open on the weakest list), handoff? (the booking page of a specialist), measured (true when free), next }. 402 past the budget cap with the key's top-up door.

auth.rule: The tenant's key (or a child key under it) asks; the key ref is the case's asked_by; a raw key never travels past the door. X-Taifoon-Channel names the outlet (embed, chrome, mcp, plugin, n8n, teams, slack, api, cli).

tools.name: sma_graph
tools.summary: The product's knowledge graph as the helpdesk holds it (?product=<id>, ?scope=public|product|tenant, ?weakest=1 for the ranked unknowns): nodes { id, kind, scope, label, confidence, asked, learned_from }, edges { from, to, kind, weight }, open { category, license, weights, source }.
tools.returns: { product, tenant?, scope, open?, nodes[], edges[], weakest? [{ node, score, asked, confidence }], count }

auth.rule: Without a key: the public nodes of the product (the open resource, under its licence). With the tenant's key: its tenant and product nodes too. A sealed node's content never leaves its tenant; only its label travels.

tools.name: sma_learn
tools.summary: Close the loop on a case: answer it (words, by an expert, an agent or a member), grade it (Jev, the buyer or the admin), or tune a loop of the tenant inside its bounds (admin only). A graded answer becomes a fix node and a fixed_by edge; the provider leg goes to the answerer's nominated payee; the meter line is written.
tools.returns: { case { id, state }, node? { id, confidence }, meter? { step, product, list_micro, legs }, tuning? { loop, value } }

auth.rule: An expert's, agent's or admin's key answers or grades an open case of its tenant or product; a user's key may say whether the answer helped (the buyer grade). Settle happens only once a grade stands (the grade-gate loop).

tools.name: sma_nominate
tools.summary: Enlist an expert of the tenant's product: { expert key:<24hex>, payee (an address, or the expert's key ref until it claims one), chains, share_bps ≤ 7000, cap per period, classes } → a nomination sma.nomination.v1 in state proposed; the expert POSTs { id, accept: true } to accept; the admin POSTs { id, revoke: true } to revoke.
tools.returns: schema sma.nomination.v1: { id nom_<16hex>, tenant, product, by, expert, payee, chains, leg provider, share_bps, cap_micro_per_period, period, classes, state proposed | accepted | revoked, claim signed-claim }

auth.rule: A tenant's admin key nominates an expert key (never itself); the expert's key accepts. The nomination is the signed claim the payee resolver reads, so the expert's provider leg pays out without a hand-pinned payee.
